He says the scan had returned 13 findings.

"So instead, I just asked Codex, can you fix it? And so it opened up my Cloudflare control panel, and it just used computer use, it clicked around, it set a bunch of headers, changed a bunch of settings."

"I used to have it so that I had Cloudflare in front, and then AWS on the back end, and I was going over insecure HTTP here. Codex had figured that out. I actually am not even sure how it saw that, because I thought everything was hidden behind Cloudflare."

"I had an old jQuery version that was insecure. It just got rid of jQuery entirely. And it was like 15 minutes to find all these findings. It was another hour to fix all of them."

"And for me, I just was the manager. I just gave it the intent."

Additionally, from the information available, NVDA, liquidity, App Fees, and ecosystem expansion are all essentially built around $AI.

AI is the core asset → NVDA is the value anchor → LONG is the infrastructure/ecosystem → Fees continuously flow back into the AI/NVDA market → Liquidity increases → AI’s asset attributes become stronger.

There are several key changes right now:

The AI/NVDA market already has $3.5M of NVDA
A large portion of App Fees will be reinvested into NVDA
LONG emphasizes that AI is one of the most liquid assets in the ecosystem
Capital has started actively bidding AI
AI has a clear exchange relationship with NVDA: 1 AI ≈ 0.001048 NVDA
The ecosystem is expected to expand further in the next stage

So the key question is whether AI can gradually evolve from an “AI Meme” into a core asset on Robinhood Chain with real liquidity, real asset backing, and real trading demand.

If this direction works, then LONG’s ecosystem expansion will actually continue adding liquidity and use cases to AI as the core asset.

author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
受到好兄弟 @GuHype 启发，在 $HYPE 找找新玩意

原来稳定币不止可以存着赚利息， 还有另一种玩法：

Hyperliquid HLP。
什么是 HLP ？
通俗的讲法，它有点像属于Hyperliquid 自己的Wintermute。
你出钱，它帮你当庄。

用户把 USDC 存进去，HLP 会拿这些钱去做市，在平台上挂买单和卖单赚取买卖价差。
如果有用户爆仓，HLP 也会接管和处理他们的仓位，如果后续还有利润，就会分回给存款的用户。

如果相比自己组 LP，HLP 不需要持有两种不同的资产，也不会传统 LP 那种无常损失。

但是，HLP 绝对不是保本理财。
如果做市策略亏钱或爆仓仓位继续亏损，本金一样会缩水。

所以如果你是想稳稳收利息，每天加鸡腿， HLP 可能不适合你。
这种玩法更适合手上有闲置 USDC，想提高资金效率，又不想自己做市或盯盘，同时可以接受收益波动和短期亏损的人。

研究完后我想放个几万进去，
体验一把当庄的快乐。
平时都是别人接我盘，这次该轮到我了

text:
🚨 On September 4, 2026, the well-known decentralized lending protocol @NotionalFinance was attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $1.73 million. The SlowMist Security Team has fully analyzed the incident.

🧩 Attack flow:

1️⃣ In a preceding transaction, the attacker deployed auxiliary contracts and called setApprovalForAll on ERC1155Trade to authorize them, after querying two CashMarket maturities and the required AssetIds.
2️⃣ First safeTransferFrom: minted an fCash pair with amount 1 (maturity Sep 4, 2026). The position was too small and rounded to 0 in ETH terms, so the free-collateral check passed.
3️⃣ Second safeTransferFrom: minted an fCash pair with amount uint128.max at a different maturity (Dec 3, 2026), so the two liabilities would not be added in the same bucket and revert under SafeMath.
4️⃣ mintfCashPair then checked free collateral. The two liabilities summed to -2^128, overflowed to 0 when converted to ETH, and the protocol treated the account as healthy.
5️⃣ Receiving contract 2 split the large claim to two auxiliary contracts. The payer was now contract 2, which already held a positive claim, so the check passed and the two contracts received receiver fCash.
6️⃣ In a second transaction, the attacker settled those two positions, increasing the cash balances in Escrow, then called withdraw to realize the profit.

⚙️ Root Cause: ExchangeRate._convertToETH does uint128(balance.abs()) on Solidity 0.6.x with no range check. When the liability is -2^128, 2^128 truncates to 0, so mintfCashPair only sees free collateral ≥ 0 and allows an unbacked position.

🔒 SlowMist Insight: A successful cast is not a successful valuation. Reject any abs() result above type(uint128).max, use SafeCast, and test extremes such as uint128.max and -2^128. Collateral ≥ 0 is not the same as collateral that is real.

Full analysis👇

David Sacks: Trump’s Instincts on AI and Data Centers Are Right

@Jason:

“Trump is going to turn out to be right about this data center issue.”

@DavidSacks:

“I have told you guys before that Trump is ultimately the best friend of innovators in Washington.

If anybody could make the decision about technology in DC, I'd want it to be President Trump. Not cabinet secretaries, not the White House staff, not members of Congress, not senators, not think tanks, I would really want every decision, if he had the time, to be made by President Trump because his instincts on this are really good.

He wants America to win. He does not believe in unnecessary regulation. He doesn't have all these doomer anxieties. He listens to a broad cross-section of people. I mean, he talks to all the CEOs. He is very up to speed on all these issues.

And I spoke to this at the G20 this past week. There are great deals for local communities to be had. This is the point that I think needs to be made, the reason why local communities should embrace this is not because of some abstract concern about innovation.

They should do it when the deal is good for them, and there are good deals to be had.

We've seen that in Loudoun County, Virginia, property taxes went down by $6,000 because they're getting all this data center revenue. In Louisiana, there's a county that was able to give teachers their first bonus in years because of data center revenue.

So we're starting to see all these examples where if you make the right deal, it will lower your electricity costs because they will stand up net new power generation, they will pay for grid upgrades. It does not use an excessive amount of water, that's total fake news. We know the systems recirculate. And these data centers can be put in places where they're not bothering people.

So there is a good deal to be made there and ultimately, just one last point on this, President Trump supports local choice on this. I'm seeing all this fake news, you know, Democrats saying that the administration's trying to shove these data centers down the throats of local communities.

Not true. In the policy document that I worked on, we expressly said that data centers remain a state and local decision. author: Rafi_0x
quoted_text:
Today, @vladtenev tweeted about bringing access to tokenised stocks to a global scale, which clearly shows that Robinhood is making them a major focus and narrative for the rest of the cycle.

If that’s the case, the infrastructure powering this ecosystem deserves some serious attention and @PareStocks is looking like one of them.

$PARE is the Pendle of Robinhood.

Pendle proved that you can build an entire market around tokenised yield.

$PARE is running the same playbook on tokenised stocks, except this time, the market is basically wide open. Very interesting setup 👀

So what exactly is $PARE?

$PARE is an RWA protocol on Robinhood Chain that takes tokenised stocks like AAPL and separates the underlying stock exposure from the future dividend stream, with a merge function to recombine at par.

So let's say you have 1 AAPL token on Robinhood Chain.

That token represents exposure to AAPL, and when Apple pays a dividend, Robinhood automatically reinvests it. So now your 1 token represents slightly more stock exposure.

$PARE takes that idea and says “Let's take that stock position and split the stock itself from the future dividends it generates."

So: 1 AAPL = PT-AAPL + YT-AAPL

• PT (Principal Token) = the stock without its future dividends
• YT (Yield Token) = the future dividends generated by that stock until maturity

The concept might sound complicated at first, but it’s actually pretty simple.

Imagine you own a $100K rental property generating $5K in rent over the next year.

You could split that position into:

• PT: “I own the property, but I don't receive the rent.”
• YT: “I don't own the property, but I receive all the rent for the next year.”

That’s essentially what $PARE is doing with tokenised stocks.

The PT captures the underlying asset exposure, while the YT captures the income stream. This opens up an entirely new market around tokenized equities.

What makes the setup even more interesting is that the team has been consistently shipping and improving the protocol, while protocol revenue is used to deepen PT/YT liquidity and support $PARE buybacks and burns.

So with $PARE you have a protocol with actual PMF, a rapidly growing RWA narrative, a team that keeps shipping, and a token with value accrual.

That combination is pretty rare nowadays.

If you’re bullish on tokenised stocks becoming a major part of crypto, $PARE is one of the infrastructure plays I’d be paying attention to. The timing is one of the most interesting parts.

We’re still extremely early in the tokenised stock market, and even earlier in the life of $PARE.

The market hasn't even caught on to what's being built here.

And remember... Pendle once grew to over $13B in TVL. Dream big.

text:
Steve Kerr says Roger Federer taught his Warriors team the secret to sustained success wasn’t outworking everyone, it was building a life around your craft you never want to escape from

“I’ll tell you a great story about Roger Federer. We were playing in China with the Warriors in 2017. Roger was in Shanghai for the Masters tournament, so we invited him to come speak to the team.”

“Draymond Green asked him, ‘How do you sustain success? How have you managed to win majors 20 years after you first won one?’ Everyone was expecting him to say, ‘I work harder than everybody,’ the will, all the clichés.”

“Roger Federer says, ‘I get up every morning and I make breakfast for my kids. Then I take them to school and drop them off. Then I go practice tennis for about two hours, and I’ve figured out a really good routine where I don’t destroy my body, but I can get all the work in I need.”

“‘Then I go have lunch with my wife. In the evening, we cook dinner together. The kids are all home from school. We ask them about school. There’s so much joy in the house. We put them to bed, and then I put my head on the pillow and go, “Man, that was just a great day.” And I’ve been doing that for 20 years.’”

“And it was like, yes. That’s it. That’s the formula. That’s what leads to sustained success. He loves tennis. He loves his family. He loves life. It’s not outworking everybody and banging your head against the wall, ‘I’m going to be better than everybody.’ It’s allowing your natural talent to shine through with a work ethic, with a great family life, with perspective, with peace, with mindfulness.”

“It’s perspective. It’s joy. It’s passion. It’s mindfulness. It’s an awareness that we are truly lucky. To get the most out of ourselves, it’s our daily rituals and experiences and love and joy.”

text:
TL;DR: Solana's endgame isn't just higher TPS. It's open financial infrastructure that keeps adapting to physics.

In a new interview, founder @toly and team member @b_migliaccio unpack why: Solana should never be "frozen." Like Linux, it should evolve as hardware, networking, and market structure evolve.

Key takeaways from the conversation:

▪️ A trader in Singapore sees market-moving information. Why should the trade need to travel to New York before it can affect the market?

▪️Concurrent proposers aim to make price discovery less dependent on one geographic center and one temporary block leader.

▪️ With Firedancer and Alpenglow targeting major performance gains, including ~150ms finality cited in the interview, the goal is not a faster chain for its own sake.

▪️ It is globally distributed market infrastructure: open source, 24/7, auditable, and built for competition at the limits of latency.

Toly's view on MEV is equally pragmatic: it is not inherently good or bad. The real test is whether apps and users have transparency, optionality, and a way to avoid consistently bad execution.

@solana reportedly processed $1.1T in volume last quarter, according to the interview, but the harder milestone is behavioral: when "DeFi" stops being a separate category and simply becomes finance.

The job isn't finished. That's the point.

author: justinsuntron
quoted_text:
WIN三个月涨幅超100%，再叠加100%收入回购

以涨服人，过去一个月WIN涨了20.5%，三个月涨幅已经到108.1%，翻倍。

还有单日交易额相比一个月前增加了85.6%，盘面上的交易也明显比之前活跃。

再看WINkLink本身，今年其实也有一些变化。

WINkLink本质上就是TRON上的预言机，给链上的DeFi、金融类应用提供价格等链下数据。上半年它一直在扩充价格数据覆盖，也做了价格服务页面的升级。

从Q3开始，WINkLink预言机业务产生的收入，100%拿出来回购WIN，之后按照计划进行销毁，而且相关数据会在链上披露。

业务有收入 → 回购WIN → 销毁供应。

所以现在再看WIN，除了价格本身，我觉得还可以观察它的预言机业务到底能产生多少收入，以及后面的回购和销毁规模。

text:
I realise talking about specific fork upgrades, EIP numbers and technical arguments doesn't always help get the message across to people that are not spending their life in the weeds of all this, so here is one attempt:

Today, physical cash lets you pay someone without telling the world or trusting a middleman. This level of privacy and freedom should be the baseline. We shouldn't settle for less.

So the first, and maybe most important, goal is to bring this level of freedom to the digital world, so we don't need to meet in person and hand over pieces of paper to benefit from these privacy guarantees.

Beyond that, what Ethereum can uniquely enable is private DeFi beyond transfers and payments. I honestly don't think this exists in the world just yet, and the idea of letting anyone lend, borrow, vote and trade without publicly linking those actions to them, without asking permission, and without relying on a trusted middleman is very powerful.

This is one of the reasons I'm so passionate about working for Ethereum. There are challenges, but digital independence is a future worth building towards.

quoted_text:
In the upcoming weeks, we'll have to decide what to ship next year in the Hegota hardfork.

A few themes appear to get most of the focus:

-> native privacy: that's the bundle of EIP-8141 (Frame Transactions) + EIP-8250 (Keyed Nonces) + EIP-8272 (Recent Root Refs). This moves Ethereum closer to native + scalable onchain privacy.
-> repricing/security: with increasing block sizes and more blobs, networking throughput goes up. To counter that, EIP-8131 and EIP-8279 meter and reprice data, ensuring blocks propagate safely. The same applies to state growth: EIP-8368 (recalibrating state growth costs) deals with increased state growth at higher gas limits. Those changes can translate into further gas limit increases.
-> clean-ups: there's EIP-3289 (removing refunds), EIP-8015 (removing the eth1data field), EIP-8253 (bumping the nonce of a few ancient accounts), EIP-7668 (removing bloom filters), or EIP-8146 separating the BAL from the payload, which also has security benefits from smaller networking objects.
PQ prep: EIP-8365 retiring BLS withdrawal credentials, EIP-8298 introducing SETCODEFROM for easier wallet migration, or EIP-8151 restricting ecRecover.

Besides the already mentioned EIPs, there are a bunch more, but core-dev resources are scarce and Ethereum's 100% uptime is the #1 priority. This means that while many ideas make sense, they'll have to be deprioritized for the sake of shipping fast and securely.

In the upcoming weeks, ACD will make decisions about which EIPs to drop (DFI - "declined for inclusion") and which to move into the next round (CFI - "considered for inclusion"). This usually begins with easy/clear DFI decisions, and the further we get, the clearer the shape of Hegota becomes.

Imo, we should focus on privacy and security. This means shipping a cleanly scoped fork in a timely manner, keeping interacting changes to a minimum, and fighting scope creep at every stage of the process. Shipping secure, contained forks doesn't mean we'd stop being ambitious wrt increasing gas limits or blob counts, though.

There is still much to do, e.g, prepare Ethereum for PQ, enshrine strong privacy, scale, reduce tx inclusion times, confirmation times, and time to finality, and, in general, harden the chain on every front: sync, RPCs, indexers, wallets, etc. There's still much to do, but Hegota can be a big step forward.

The process is fully open and transparent btw. Everyone can rank the proposed EIPs, put them into a tier list, and post it on the Hegota EthMagicians thread.

We did so as the Architecture team at EF here:
https://t.co/f3SWNLnUYu

text:
Solana, BNB Chain And Arbitrum Clash Over Robinhood Chain Fee Model

Robinhood (@RobinhoodCrypto) Chain’s revenue model has sparked a wider debate about blockchain economics.

Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko previously criticized Robinhood’s revenue arrangement with Arbitrum.

The network lets Robinhood retain most gas revenue while sharing 10% of its protocol net revenue under its Arbitrum agreement. Its applications generated $2.66 million in revenue over 24 hours on August 31.

Offchain Labs CEO Steven Goldfeder defended the arrangement, saying Robinhood keeps most gas revenue.

Nina Rong, Executive Director of Growth at BNB Chain said lower gas fees are no longer the industry’s top priority. She argued that blockchains need sustainable revenue models to keep funding technology and development.

  - 明确属于自建或定制：210 个。
  - 其余待归类：262 个，包括第三方安装、历史迁入和未标注作者的自建技能。

首先 skills 绝大部分是业务相关的。这个业务相关的 skills 举个例子，比如说当我发了一个会议纪要给他，我希望他做什么事情。

这种类型的 skills 是模型永远不可能内置的，因为它不知道我要怎么处理我的会议纪要，所以我就必须要一步一步讲解它。有的人可能用 Notion，有的人可能是发邮件，有的人可能是转化成一条一条的 todo，每个人不一样，所以说每个人的对于处理会议纪要的 skills 是不一样的。

所以 skills 其实非常有必要，但是这一类的 skills 并不是可以随意公开到外面的，或者说非常通用的。而是属于个人的业务逻辑，或者是 taste。

换个邪修的用法，在 AI 时代，如果想看一看这个人真正的水平。有一个最快的方式，就是让他把某一种问题的相关 skills 拉出来，这样可以直接看到他是怎么跟 AI 交互的，他的思路是怎么样的，他的步骤是怎么样的。

text:
A few weeks ago, it felt like everyone on the timeline thought crypto was dead.

So I wanted to see how much money VCs were actually putting into crypto this year compared to previous cycles. It’s an interesting leading indicator.

Well, crypto investment hit $13.3B in the first half of 2026, including acquisitions. 

2024 took 12 months to hit roughly that number…2026 did it in six.

That matters because investors aren't putting up that kind of money unless they expect a decent ROI. They can be wrong, but billions still being deployed is a useful counterpoint to the idea that crypto is dead.

There's something different happening compared to past cycles:

• Deals per month are down 56% from 2022
• Seed rounds per month are down roughly 77%

But the reported average deal size went from $11.7M in 2024 to $47.4M in H1 2026.

Basically, no more spraying and praying. They're writing huge checks to a handful of proven companies (Kalshi, Polymarket, stablecoin rails) and being much more selective about everything else.

The upside to this is we're seeing a new generation of dApps with no VC money behind them.

That means no VC allocations waiting to unlock, or VC funds waiting to dump on you at TGE. 

This is much healthier compared to what we had in the past.

author: lex_node
quoted_text:
I want to close my chapter, for now, on the EIP-8363 analysis. After having a few more calls with people who are for- and against- issuance reduction (stakers, founders, DeFi people, and regular Ethereum holders) - here is a subjective view on the matter. I think it has some new aspects I didn't see much of before (💡)

- TLDR 1: I don't think this should go through right now. The proposal is raw and the arguments are still weak. It's weird to say this because it has been in the works for five years on and off, but it still doesn't make sense. I respect the authors who put time and effort into this, but after looking into it and having so many conversations across the space - it doesn't check out.
- TLDR 2: Neither side should be talking about anyone being "captured." You cannot say that core devs living and breathing the network are captured. No, they care about it and are involved. That is good! Similarly, you cannot say DeFi founders or the staking companies are captured. These people own the asset and are economically interested in having it grow. We have to put those arguments aside - it is just cheap talk.
- TLDR 3: Regarding the process: whether now or later, issuance policy shouldn't just go through a normal network upgrade process. It's not just about repricing or a minor technical tweak; this is way too big to be considered in that fashion. Maybe it could work within the existing process, but only if the opinions of founders and other stakeholders were respected a bit more, rather than just discarding them all as being captured.

Now to the arguments 🦞

I haven't really strayed from what I wrote a few weeks ago (tweet below). As a shorter summary, the argument for reduction falls through three main holes.

1. First, there is this allegiance to a "no inflation" economy perception: the idea that inflation is inherently bad, that (over)paying for something is bad, and that there is just too much of something. That mindset is not correct. In the modern economic world, since we stopped making money only from growing potatoes, it doesn't make sense. The belief that this will somehow make the Ethereum price moon, or that there is too much ETH being dumped on the market, is nonsense. It's one of the least inflating assets.

💡 You have to consider your broader goals. Your issuance strategy should reflect your general adoption strategy. If you think ETH is just an asset, money, a unit of account, or whatever narrative you want to come up with - like the "pet rock" meme Bitcoin style - fine. It's not bad, and it's okay to say that. But then the general adoption strategy should reflect it. It should just be marketing a hard asset, not worry about devs, open-source or anything creative. It's just digital gold, go to hard money conferences and enjoy.

However, if you see Ethereum as a World Computer, as a way to build different use cases, as an "infinite garden" for lack of a better phrase, as a platform - then there is no point in cutting the issuance. Currently, issuance creates different opportunities and products on this platform. EVEN IF you think it's a subsidy, then what? Platforms have subsidies. Why tamper with it if you have no definite alternative. These subsidies worked, they continue working and getting attention, and the platform is winning as a result of that (adoption, liquidity, trust, security, etc.)

If you offboard one big user segment from your marketplace, what's your alternative? Because you are then killing some of the plants in your garden that you've previously incentivized. It's not a weed, and presenting it as a weed is incorrect because nothing shows that's the case.

2. Second, the argument falls through on all the talk about the staking ratio, staking centralization, supply capture, solo stakers, inability to pass slashing, and so on. These are generally good discussions to have, but the suggested proposal does not fix those 🚫

💡 Take the part about slashing and forks, for example. All of these fancy ideas of how staker behavior is going to play out aren't really realistic. Nobody writes about which network - in terms of a slashing event or a fork - USDC, USDT, and centralized issuers would actually consider and back. 

Important factors affecting network resilience should be solved, but this proposal does not solve them. It does not improve conditions for solo stakers. The argument that the staking distribution will get worse if we continue - is also unproven. There is no proper distinction made between "good" LSTs and "bad" LSTs (if you want to think this way). If you believe that Binance and Coinbase staking shouldn't be increasing as much, that's a different discussion. A blanket cut wouldn't kill them as much as it would kill some LSTs that are actually favorable to the development of the core network. I'm not against an issuance reduction as a move potentially; I'm against how it is being argued, and that it's being argued in a weak way .

3. Third, the mechanics of yield are now being accepted as an asset in DeFi protocols (stETH over raw ETH, for example). These are interesting opportunities to consider, but thinking you can mess with this in isolation while killing what exists now isn't cool. Having Ethereum's economic policy be more set in stone is far more important to current participants than just trying out stuff by breaking an ecosystem that exists today.

💡 If institutions and such players appreciate ETH as an asset and engage with real use cases, do not stop them by trying to hypothetically make other use cases possible. They appreciate the current staking rate and have built strategies around it. 

If the proposal would solve security or network resilience while causing some pain in the short term, that would be acceptable. But as I've established, the arguments presented are weak and in many cases incorrect, so it doesn't even solve the purpose.

-----

You have to decide what you actually want to happen:

- Do you want to play trader and mess around with the ETH price by thinking less inflation is better
- Or do you want to solve network resilience and make it uncapturable?

You have to answer one of these questions. Right now, they are all packaged together. As a result, it's a mess, because it's not solving a problem that is explained - or it's solving a problem that is not proven to exist. 

Sorry 8363, but hope no.

text:
BAYC is in the crossroads between the new yield-generating NFTs and the old NFTs who pivoted to brand building

On one hand you have innovations that comes with generating yields tied to NFTs

On the other hand you have OG brands pivoting their building towards mainstream

One’s overly web3, the other’s leaning to web2. And where is BAYC? In the middle

Compared to OG NFT brands who have expressed desires in growing in web2, BAYC has remained largely web3. Most of their drops are token-gated. Most of their meet-ups are token gated. ApeFest is token-gated. Clubhouse will likely have some token-gated features too.

On top of these, BAYC has been trying to put the value back into buying NFTs with initiatives pushing collectors to collect the NFTs they want ie Grails OTC, NFT swaps

Compared to the other OG NFT collections back in 2021-22, they are trying to do more on web3 rails

But in the advent of Robinhood and ERC-6551, this may not be enough to some NFT buyers. Thus, they’re asking BAYC now to innovate again and play around these new rails for its holders

But the bigger issue may not be being in the middle of these 2 contrasting NFT paths. The issue might be the questions asking “what’s the next big thing for BAYC?”

While Figge and team has been laying out the ground work and building the unique holder count to ensure that BAYC grows sustainably, holders are still looking past that and asking what would make the price go up for BAYC?

ApeFest is right around the corner. This will be Figge’s first ApeFest as Yuga CEO. I expect to hear more from Yuga then about the future of the club

text:
Since the beginning of summer, we've all noticed how liquidity on Polymarket gradually started to decline, and at this point, the drop has reached significant proportions.

While previously you could boost liquidity through sponsored rewards, now, even after deploying a significant amount of capital and landing in the top 5 markets by yield, nobody is in any rush to farm rewards. Bots and airdrop farmers went offline back in the summer, and the massive influx of new markets is essentially useless without the necessary liquidity.

Now, to get your orders filled, you sometimes have to wait for weeks, and even then, in most cases you never get the share volume you need.

It's all snowballing: CLOB issues, lack of liquidity, the exodus of bots and farmers - it's very bad, and the team's lack of sound communication and a clear roadmap only exacerbates the situation.

In all my time trading on Polymarket, I've never complained and always tried to maintain an optimistic attitude, but now, after so long, my outlook on the situation is beginning to turn pessimistic.

text:
Moss @MossAI_Official  项目简析：从 AI 交易工具到链上 Agent 资本市场

Moss 的定位“AI Agent 的链上资本市场”

项目试图解决三个问题：

- 其一，交易信息高度碎片化，用户难以从 X、新闻和链上数据中筛选有效信号；

- 其二，量化策略与 AI Agent 往往缺乏可验证的实盘记录，回测结果和收益截图容易被包装；

其三，用户即使认可某个策略，也缺少低门槛、非托管的参与方式

为此，Moss 将信息发现、策略生成、交易执行与 Agent 评估串联起来,让能够持续执行、产生决策的 AI Agent 成为可验证、可持有和可交易的链上资产

Diamonds 激励：持续为Moss注入新鲜血液

Moss Diamonds 本质上是生态参与激励，其早期主要通过 Predict、Agent Arena 和社区任务发放

从公开记录看，Diamonds 至少在 2026 年 4 月前后已被用于 Agent Arena 第三季奖励；截至 2026 年 9 月，激励已持续约四个月以上。

当前阶段的核心变化不是停止发钻，而是从旧插件体系迁移至新的 Moss Agent Marketplace。

与此同时，新的活动开始将 Diamonds 与 Agent 份额铸造、治理参与及合作项目权益结合：例如部分治理或消费型 Agent 的 Mint 活动会额外给予 500 Diamonds。

核心机制玩法：

- 创建策略
- Mint Agent

当前主要涵盖三类 Agent：

- 第一类是 Hyperliquid 永续合约交易 Agent，Agent 在 Hyperliquid 执行策略，份额持有人按持有比例分享 Agent 收益

- 第二类是治理 Agent，面向项目方或 DAO，持有人可获得固定 APY、项目额外奖励，并参与社区提案投票

- 第三类是消费 Agent，面向第三方权益发行方，用户累积足够份额后可以解锁专属兑换或消费权益。

无论哪一种Agent，Moss都把用户信任和AI Agent建立起长期连接，同时也让脑子里的一个交易想法轻松变成一个可以自动运行的Agent

text:
My notifications and group chats won’t stop buzzing about @shroom_network built by @0xcarnation.

So I take a look, and I’ll own it:

It’s a legitimately compelling idea for addressing the growing pains hanging over tokenized stocks as they expand day after day on @RobinhoodCrypto chain.

Robinhood chain already lists 190+ stock tokens. That’s not just “more stocks,” it’s an explosion of possible trading pairs.

If every stock needed its own direct liquidity pool against every other stock, 190 assets can theoretically spawn 17,955 pairs.

- NVDA/AAPL.
- NVDA/TSLA.
- AAPL/MSFT.
- MSFT/SPY.

Push that to 1,000 assets and you’re staring at nearly 500,000 pairs, with liquidity splintered everywhere and markets getting less efficient by the minute.

You see where this goes. Liquidity gets fragmented everywhere.

And $SHROOM might be one solution.

Instead of building every possible pair, SHROOM wants to become the liquidity hub connecting them all.

Think:

- AAPL → SHROOM → NVDA
- MSFT → SHROOM → TSLA
- SPY → SHROOM → AMD

Now you only need roughly one SHROOM pool per asset, rather than liquidity across thousands of combinations.

Why does this matter?

Without a common liquidity hub, traders may have to route through several thin markets:

AAPL → USDG → ETH → NVDA

Every extra swap can mean another:

- LP fee
- Price impact
- Source of slippage

So a $100K trade can lose meaningful value before reaching the final asset.

SHROOM is trying to turn its liquidity hub into the path of least resistance, so deep that routers end up routing through it by default simply because it offers the cheapest execution.

But the real twist is how it’s built.

Most of these pools are protocol-owned liquidity (PoL). SHROOM’s treasury actually holds the LP positions across tokenized assets like NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, SPY, MU, and more.

As trades happen, fees accrue and those fees go right back into strengthening the pools:

Volume → Fees → Deeper Liquidity → Tighter Slippage → More Volume

Right now, SHROOM reports roughly 48 protocol-owned LP positions and about ~$624K in PoL.

Over time, once liquidity reaches “thick enough” territory, the plan is for surplus fees to fund SHROOM buybacks and burns. Robinhood Stock Tokens add a unique edge here: they trade onchain 24/7, even when the US equity market is closed.

So when NASDAQ shuts, RHC don’t. Tokenized NVDA, TSLA, and AAPL can still reprice, gaps open, and that’s where the machinery kicks in.

Arbs step in to harvest the discrepancy, SHROOM pools collect the fees, and prices get moved back toward fair value.

And if you zoom out, RHC isn’t even three months old. If Robinhood eventually pushes thousands of stocks, ETFs, and RWAs onchain, liquidity won’t just be “nice to have.” Fragmentation becomes a real infrastructure bottleneck.

That’s the opening SHROOM is aiming at: becoming the liquidity layer that keeps Robinhood’s onchain stock market from splintering.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
过去做一次深入的竞品调研，你往往需要买一堆每个月上百刀的订阅，然后在 Similarweb、Ahrefs、Reddit 和 X 之间来回切网页，最后填到表里的数据还经常对不上。

但现在，你不需要单独买任何一个月费订阅，也不用再搞一堆复杂的 API 密钥。

你只需要把产品网址丢给已经接好 AIsa 的 Claude Code 或 Codex，用一句最实在的业务目标，把它打发去干活。Agent 会自己去查产品事实、找竞品、比流量渠道、翻用户原话，最后交给你一份能直接拿去开会讨论的竞品报告。

我们可以直接看一个最典型的场景。这是我扔给 Agent 的原话：

“请分析这个产品 Youmind，识别 5 个主要竞品。比较它们的定位、核心功能、网站流量来源、用户评价和内容渠道，最后输出一份竞品分析报告，并给出 3 个值得切入的差异化方向。”

注意，我没有指定它该调哪个接口。规划任务、筛选数据源、交叉核对，全权交由 Agent 自己完成。

真正接通了外部商业数据的 Agent，在这个过程中会走出一条非常清晰的思考链： 先读官网，搞清楚这产品卖给谁、主打哪一句； 接着用 Tavily 或 Exa 把公开事实和候选竞品补全； 随后调用 Similarweb，把几家网站的访问规模、渠道结构和搜索表现直接拉到同一张桌子上；

同时，Reddit 和 X 负责另一半——去看看真实用户在夸什么、骂什么、在什么场景下反复提及； 最后收口，一份包含定位、功能、流量来源、评价、内容渠道的报告生成完毕，并顺手给你指出了 3 个还能挤进去的差异化方向。

这里面最核心的一层，必须单拎出来说一下，那就是底层的 Similarweb 数据。

AIsa 是目前极少数能把 Similarweb 官方 API V5 直接交给 Agent 调用的平台。走的是正规授权接口，和市面上那些爬虫、镜像站压根不是一路东西，而且那些镜像站最多只能让你在网页上查查数据，根本不提供API。 

你要知道，这种官方服务主要面向企业客户，个人开发者和小团队自己去谈，一年从 5 万美元起步很常见。哪怕是 Ahrefs、Semrush，各开一份进阶订阅，一个月也得大几百刀。

而 AIsa 的做法是：把这些顶级情报源全部打包到一个账户里，共享余额，按次扣费。这意味着，Agent 每次帮你做竞品调研，你不用再同时订阅多份服务。

一份真正敢拿来做商业决策的报告，必须留下证据。 在这份报告里，哪段数据来自 Similarweb，哪段是 Reddit 的用户原话，哪段来自搜索结果，全都能精准指回去。模型自己补的判断，和接口返回的硬数据，被分得清清楚楚。 以后你拿这份报告做决策，至少知道哪一行经得起推敲复查。

顺着这套打法，你能做的事还有很多：

产品 SEO 检测：丢一个网站 URL，它能出 SEO 诊断，告诉你关键词覆盖率、SERP 表现，以及最该先修哪几个页面。
GEO / AI 可见度检测：丢品牌名加几个竞品，它能直接告诉你，在 Perplexity 这类 AI 答案页里谁被提得多、引用从哪来、你的内容该往哪补。

So here's the workflow that I found working really well. 
For webs, it's really easy to make agents run and test. You can order Grok @bot to go through your websiste as a user and test.

For apps, it's really hard, and that's where I found @Replit and @AsideAI kick some ass. 

So I have Replit project open and Aside AI on the side panel, and I can make Aside AI literally act like a user and click through my app to find bugs on Replit's app preview.

Then, using Replit MCP, it can pass on the bug report, and the agent will fix it right away. When Agent is done, Aside can get back to work. In the video at about 20 sec, you can see Aside passing on the work to Replit Agent.

For other ADEs or Browsers, they have to look at the screen and click through, but Aside works differently. It works by embedding an AI agent directly into the core Chromium engine rather than running it as an external screen-scraping tool or a restricted browser extension. So, it's better and faster debugging.

@Replit's MCP update has allowed me to come up with this new workflow. This is just a short demo, more coming up soon.

text:
In the upcoming weeks, we'll have to decide what to ship next year in the Hegota hardfork.

A few themes appear to get most of the focus:

-> native privacy: that's the bundle of EIP-8141 (Frame Transactions) + EIP-8250 (Keyed Nonces) + EIP-8272 (Recent Root Refs). This moves Ethereum closer to native + scalable onchain privacy.
-> repricing/security: with increasing block sizes and more blobs, networking throughput goes up. To counter that, EIP-8131 and EIP-8279 meter and reprice data, ensuring blocks propagate safely. The same applies to state growth: EIP-8368 (recalibrating state growth costs) deals with increased state growth at higher gas limits. Those changes can translate into further gas limit increases.
-> clean-ups: there's EIP-3289 (removing refunds), EIP-8015 (removing the eth1data field), EIP-8253 (bumping the nonce of a few ancient accounts), EIP-7668 (removing bloom filters), or EIP-8146 separating the BAL from the payload, which also has security benefits from smaller networking objects.
PQ prep: EIP-8365 retiring BLS withdrawal credentials, EIP-8298 introducing SETCODEFROM for easier wallet migration, or EIP-8151 restricting ecRecover.

Besides the already mentioned EIPs, there are a bunch more, but core-dev resources are scarce and Ethereum's 100% uptime is the #1 priority. This means that while many ideas make sense, they'll have to be deprioritized for the sake of shipping fast and securely.

In the upcoming weeks, ACD will make decisions about which EIPs to drop (DFI - "declined for inclusion") and which to move into the next round (CFI - "considered for inclusion"). This usually begins with easy/clear DFI decisions, and the further we get, the clearer the shape of Hegota becomes.

Imo, we should focus on privacy and security. This means shipping a cleanly scoped fork in a timely manner, keeping interacting changes to a minimum, and fighting scope creep at every stage of the process. Shipping secure, contained forks doesn't mean we'd stop being ambitious wrt increasing gas limits or blob counts, though.

There is still much to do, e.g, prepare Ethereum for PQ, enshrine strong privacy, scale, reduce tx inclusion times, confirmation times, and time to finality, and, in general, harden the chain on every front: sync, RPCs, indexers, wallets, etc. There's still much to do, but Hegota can be a big step forward.

The process is fully open and transparent btw. Everyone can rank the proposed EIPs, put them into a tier list, and post it on the Hegota EthMagicians thread.

We did so as the Architecture team at EF here:
https://t.co/f3SWNLnUYu

Do as we did and participate:

text:
I've been looking into @zorpians and the way they're combining NFTs with tokenized stocks is pretty interesting.

Every one of the 4,000 hand-drawn Zorpians is assigned one of 12 real companies at mint, written on-chain.

But the part that caught my attention is how the stock is held.

Through ERC-6551, every Zorpian gets its own on-chain account. Once activated, the treasury buys stock daily and credits active Zorpians into the company assigned to them. So the NFT itself can hold its stock.

And if you decide to sell your Zorpian, whatever you leave inside that account goes with it.
You're potentially passing on a Grey with its own accumulated portfolio.

The collection also uses an inverted rarity table, where companies with lower supply have fewer Zorpians carrying them.

4,000 hand-drawn Greys.
12 companies.
Robinhood Chain.

Definitely an interesting direction for what an NFT can actually carry with it. https://t.co/PWWaLvLkLO

Total panic I’d lost a good chunk of Bitcoin this morning. 

Keystone wallet fucked, I don’t know how the battery has died already but it seems it has. Piece of shit, don’t buy, stick to Ledger/Trezor.

I didn’t know where I’d put the seed phrase. Yes fucking dumb, but I have so many seed phrases and this one was set up at a time where I’d had a newborn and was insanely sleep deprived.

Turns out I made a cryptic note on my phone telling me I put the seed phrase in a particular watch box, which I then couldn’t find, and eventually realised I must have put in my loft. 

If I hadn’t made that note then it was probably over. 

Wake up call for me to stop being totally lax that devices will work and everything will be fine. 

If you have been putting off sorting out a better set up for your self custody then this is your warning. 

I’ve been doing this for 10 years, and am still running paper seed and hardware set up, which was the gold standard back in the day, but it’s time to step up now. 

If any security experts want to tell me the best Bitcoin set up in 2026 I would be most appreciative!?

text:
🇺🇸🇨🇳 The next financial crisis may be a crisis of confidence in the system itself.

U.S. federal debt has climbed above $40 trillion, with enormous borrowing requirements and rising interest costs making the Treasury market increasingly important to global stability.

But America is not alone. Japan is carrying an enormous government debt load just as Japanese bond yields rise, while Europe and Britain face their own combinations of high debt, weak growth and increasingly expensive borrowing.

None of these problems individually guarantees a crisis.

The danger is what happens if investors begin questioning all of them at roughly the same time.

Previous crises occurred in a world where Western governments and central banks remained the unquestioned backstop. When private markets broke in 2008 or economies froze in 2020, governments could borrow enormous amounts and central banks could intervene because confidence in sovereign debt itself remained largely intact.

A crisis centered on sovereign debt would be different because the traditional backstop could itself become part of the problem.

And the world is considerably more multipolar today.

The dollar remains dominant, and there is still no genuine replacement for the enormous U.S. Treasury market. But China and other countries have expanded local-currency trade, alternative payment infrastructure and gold reserves. 

The dollar doesn’t need to be replaced for the system to become more fragile. Major foreign holders simply need viable alternatives, and therefore less reason to keep recycling their savings into U.S. debt.

If Treasury yields rise, Japanese capital moves home, Western governments need even more borrowing and major reserve holders diversify at the same time, separate financial pressures could rapidly become one global confidence crisis.

Then there is a new source of volatility: artificial intelligence.

The DeepSeek shock demonstrated how quickly a Chinese technological breakthrough could challenge assumptions about American AI dominance and sharply reprice U.S. technology stocks.

Another major Chinese breakthrough, particularly a frontier model at dramatically lower cost, could reinforce the perception that technological power is becoming multipolar too, potentially redirecting investment and weakening another pillar of American financial dominance.

AI could also make any crisis move faster. Automated markets, increasingly capable cyber tools and information moving globally within seconds mean confidence can disappear much faster than in previous eras.

The risk isn't simply American debt, Japanese debt, European fiscal pressure, de-dollarization or AI disruption.

The real danger begins when those pressures reinforce each other and investors stop asking what the system can withstand, and start asking how quickly they can get out.

text:
Understandable reaction, but the details point the other way. Per Liquid's own statement, no keys were compromised. The withdrawal exploited the peg-out authorization mechanism, a software-level flaw in how the federation approves withdrawals.

In other words: the failure was in pooled, intermediated custody, a federation wallet holding everyone's BTC. Exchanges are the same model at bigger scale.

Self-custody wasn't the attack surface here. With a hardware signer, your keys are generated and stored offline in a secure chip, and every transaction is verified on a screen you can trust before anything moves. Paired with a wallet built for clear signing, you know exactly what you're approving, every time.

Not your keys, not your bitcoin still holds. This is exactly why.

text:
Here’s my thesis on HYPE’s price over the next few months, keeping it as rational as possible.

How do we do that? By focusing on revenue.

We know more and more TradFi players are getting involved in $HYPE. These players value stocks using P/E ratios and I think that’s exactly how $HYPE is being valued. It isn’t trading like any other major or revenue-less altcoin like $ZEC etc. Otherwise, we’d already be at $300 given all the insane news we’ve had so far.

With that in mind, here’s my thesis:

I still believe there will be another airdrop. And I’ll keep believing that until the team changes the tokenomics, which explicitly state that the community will be rewarded again.

Based on that, I’m estimating the next airdrop at around 6–8% of the total supply, worth roughly $6–8B at $100. Of that $8B, I expect a decent chunk to be used as collateral to borrow USDC. Somewhere between $1B and $2B in borrowing doesn’t sound unreasonable to me.

That would mean at least $2B in USDC being minted on Hyperliquid, before even accounting for people who simply sell instead of borrowing. We could potentially reach $10B in USDC held on Hyperliquid pretty easily.

$10B in USDC would generate $314M in annual revenue (almost 50% more revenue on top of the roughly $700M annualized we’re doing right now).

Then there are the CEX integrations: Kraken, Coinbase, and probably others. Those integrations would bring more people trading on HL which also means more USDC held on HL.

That could easily take us to $15–20B, depending on the integrations and how much traction they get. That doesn’t seem far-fetched at all.

At $20B we’d be looking at $628M in additional annual revenue, almost doubling what we’re generating today.

While $HYPE has been pricing in some of this revenue growth over the past few weeks, imo it’s only pricing in the USDC already held on HL.

On top of that, we’d have trading fees from users accessing HL through CEXs. That could be huge too.

It’s hard to estimate, because we know CEXs heavily fake their reported volume, liquidation, and other stats. But Hyperliquid averaged $8B in daily trading volume over the year, including around $7.7B in perps and $320M in spot.

Doubling that really doesn’t seem like a stretch with Kraken and especially Coinbase. And that’s before any other major exchanges join the party.

If volume doubles, assuming the same effective fee rates, trading fee revenue would double too. That would put us at $1.3–1.4B in trading fee revenue + $1B from AQAv2, for a total of $2.3–2.4B in annual revenue (roughly 3x what we’re generating today).

We could also add HIP-4 revenue if it takes off and starts generating meaningful fees, along with priority fees, which could scale massively (particularly from arbitrage between HIP-3 star order books and the standard order books on HL.

But even without those last two factors, we’d already be looking at roughly 3x current revenue.

That’s why I think $HYPE could easily hit $200 over the next few months, driven by these integrations alone, without needing market euphoria or an absurdly inflated P/E ratio.

And I’m not even talking about long term price targets, with HSI very likely to keep accumulating supply, the Assistance Fund doing the same and so on.

You’re not bullish enough.

Hyperliquid.

Here's what's happening behind the scenes:

Japan spent ¥15.4 trillion supporting the yen in July and August.

Sell U.S. Treasuries → sell dollars → buy yen.

Investors who borrowed cheap yen to buy assets abroad face more expensive repayments as the yen strengthens.

Japan's currency rally could become a massive liquidity problem for the entire world economy.

text:
1/x @Liquid_BTC Liquid Network appears to have experienced a consensus divergence at block 4,050,336. Approximately 13 minutes later, a 3,996.01834922 L-BTC peg-out was recorded on the branch that continued beyond the divergent block.

Our preliminary analysis, informed by the findings shared by @stutxo, suggests that a potential issue in the rangeproof-verification cache mechanism in certain Elements Core builds may have contributed to the incident:
https://t.co/hGf1ZxSISy

Previously, the cache key for successful rangeproof verifications was derived only from the rangeproof and value commitment. It did not include the asset commitment or scriptPubKey, although both are inputs to full verification.

This could allow different verification contexts to map to the same cache entry. After a valid context populated the cache, a modified context might hit that entry and return true without undergoing full verification.

A recent patch adds the missing inputs to the cache key:
https://t.co/q63HEFBZwX
If reachable during consensus validation, this behavior could cause nodes with different cache states or implementations to reach different conclusions about the same transaction.

这个团队发的盘子非常的多，而且频率非常高

quoted_text:
Today, @vladtenev tweeted about bringing access to tokenised stocks to a global scale, which clearly shows that Robinhood is making them a major focus and narrative for the rest of the cycle.

If that’s the case, the infrastructure powering this ecosystem deserves some serious attention and @PareStocks is looking like one of them.

$PARE is the Pendle of Robinhood.

Pendle proved that you can build an entire market around tokenised yield.

$PARE is running the same playbook on tokenised stocks, except this time, the market is basically wide open. Very interesting setup 👀

So what exactly is $PARE?

$PARE is an RWA protocol on Robinhood Chain that takes tokenised stocks like AAPL and separates the underlying stock exposure from the future dividend stream, with a merge function to recombine at par.

So let's say you have 1 AAPL token on Robinhood Chain.

That token represents exposure to AAPL, and when Apple pays a dividend, Robinhood automatically reinvests it. So now your 1 token represents slightly more stock exposure.

$PARE takes that idea and says “Let's take that stock position and split the stock itself from the future dividends it generates."

So: 1 AAPL = PT-AAPL + YT-AAPL

• PT (Principal Token) = the stock without its future dividends
• YT (Yield Token) = the future dividends generated by that stock until maturity

The concept might sound complicated at first, but it’s actually pretty simple.

Imagine you own a $100K rental property generating $5K in rent over the next year.

You could split that position into:

• PT: “I own the property, but I don't receive the rent.”
• YT: “I don't own the property, but I receive all the rent for the next year.”

That’s essentially what $PARE is doing with tokenised stocks.

The PT captures the underlying asset exposure, while the YT captures the income stream. This opens up an entirely new market around tokenized equities.

What makes the setup even more interesting is that the team has been consistently shipping and improving the protocol, while protocol revenue is used to deepen PT/YT liquidity and support $PARE buybacks and burns.

So with $PARE you have a protocol with actual PMF, a rapidly growing RWA narrative, a team that keeps shipping, and a token with value accrual.

That combination is pretty rare nowadays.

If you’re bullish on tokenised stocks becoming a major part of crypto, $PARE is one of the infrastructure plays I’d be paying attention to. The timing is one of the most interesting parts.

We’re still extremely early in the tokenised stock market, and even earlier in the life of $PARE.

The market hasn't even caught on to what's being built here.

And remember... Pendle once grew to over $13B in TVL. Dream big.

text:
1/x @Liquid_BTC Liquid Network appears to have experienced a consensus divergence at block 4,050,336. Approximately 13 minutes later, a 3,996.01834922 L-BTC peg-out was recorded on the branch that continued beyond the divergent block.

Our preliminary analysis, informed by the findings shared by @stutxo, suggests that a potential issue in the rangeproof-verification cache mechanism in certain Elements Core builds may have contributed to the incident:
https://t.co/hGf1ZxSISy

Previously, the cache key for successful rangeproof verifications was derived only from the rangeproof and value commitment. It did not include the asset commitment or scriptPubKey, although both are inputs to full verification.

This could allow different verification contexts to map to the same cache entry. After a valid context populated the cache, a modified context might hit that entry and return true without undergoing full verification.

A recent patch adds the missing inputs to the cache key:
https://t.co/q63HEFBZwX
If reachable during consensus validation, this behavior could cause nodes with different cache states or implementations to reach different conclusions about the same transaction.

昨天还有个点没说到，为什么 @PareStocks 很重要。

因为robinhood当前的代币化股票分红是通过multiplier。

比如NVDA今天分红了，像币安的解决方案是把现金分红买入对应的股票然后发到用户手中，可能你原本有一股nvda，现在手上就有1.01了。

Robinhood采用了另一套方法，他不给用户任何东西，而是把脸上对应 1 token的NVDA代币化股票可赎回的真实股票数量multiplier调整到1.01 。这样做市商在赎回的时候就能赎回更多的NVDA正股。

Robinhood的这种方法并不好，因为并不是所有链上持有人都能理解这套逻辑。

长期这样积累下去，链上代币化股票的1 单位公允价格会略高于美股市场，因为multiplier在累计。要么有人会以为有套利空间，要么有人会在市场折价的时候低价卖出自己手上的代币化股票。

Pare认识到了这个问题，对代币化股票进行pt和yt的拆分，这样长期最后pt的价格其实就会和美股市场的价格一样，避免了用户误解和教育成本。multiplier中大于1的部分则被每期的yt吸收。

🇯🇵 THE JAPANESE YEN RALLY COULD TRIGGER A GLOBAL CRISIS

Here's what's happening behind the scenes:

Japan spent ¥15.4 trillion supporting the yen in July and August.

Sell U.S. Treasuries → sell dollars → buy yen.

Now, BOJ rate-hike expectations and Japanese investors bringing money home are adding pressure, pushing USD/JPY below 155.

And that creates a problem for the carry trade:

Investors who borrowed cheap yen to buy assets abroad face more expensive repayments as the yen strengthens.

If they unwind, they sell assets and buy back yen, potentially accelerating the rally.

Japan's currency rally could become a massive liquidity problem for the entire world economy.

text:
The most interesting number in BUTT is how much TAO has reached holders.

At 08:01 UTC on 7 September, StonkFun reported 1,361.76 TAO distributed across 119,327 payouts. The accompanying dashboard capture shortly afterward valued the distributed TAO at $359,820 using the then-current TAO price.

Here is the mechanism behind those numbers.

BUTT has a 3% transfer tax. Collected fees fund distributions in TAO on Solana, with a separate deduction for distribution costs and operations.

Funds accumulate until a distribution is economical. At that snapshot, eligible wallets must hold at least $20 worth of BUTT. Each receives a proportional share based on its eligible holdings.

The allocation is straightforward:

Net TAO available × your share of eligible BUTT holdings = your payout.

For example, a 100 TAO net distribution and a 0.1% eligible share would mean 0.1 TAO. That illustrates allocation, not an earning rate. The available funds, eligible balances and timing all vary.

Once received, the TAO is a separate asset you can retain or sell. Retained TAO gains dollar value if its price rises and loses dollar value if it falls. Your overall result also depends on BUTT's price and the costs you paid.

The broader opportunity is discovery. A meme can introduce someone to TAO; receiving it can give them a reason to learn what Bittensor and its subnets actually do. Turning attention into lasting interest is something the community can build toward.

The model's durability depends on continued activity funding distributions after costs. Past payouts establish a track record; they do not establish a fixed future return.

Cumulative payouts are not unique holders. Distributions are not the same as profit. The numbers are more useful when their meaning is clear.

Artificial unintelligence. Follow the TAO.

(‿|‿)

author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
Liquid hack explained.

Liquid has confidential transactions that hide the amounts for improved privacy. A bug in how these transactions are validated caused inflation of Liquid BTC (L-BTC) and allowed hackers to empty the entire side chain. 

Liquid nodes don't see the amounts of a confidential transaction, so to make sure that the transaction is still valid and doesn't cause inflation nodes check something called a balance proof and a range proof.

The balance proof establish that sum of the input amounts equal the output amounts, i.e., that "x L-BTC going in and x L-BTC going out". But there's a catch. Only relying on a balance proof isn't enough. You also need the range proof.

The range proof establishes that a hidden output amount falls within a positive range. That means a valid output must be at least 1 L-sat and at most 2^64 − 1 L-sats. Range proofs make sure that you can't mint "negative L-BTC".

Why is this even necessary? Remember, the amounts are hidden and a hidden negative amount would allow extra positive outputs to balance against it. Without a range proof, a transaction could say "I've put 1 L-BTC in, and I'm taking two outputs out: one with 4000 L-BTC and one with -3999 L-BTC)." 

This is going to cause a disaster in a little bit.

Once the balance proof, the range proof, and other validations pass, a transaction is regarded as valid and can pass consensus. However, because especially the range proof is computationally expensive, Liquid nodes cache the result of a successful range proof in memory. Essentially, the node remembers "I saw this range proof before and it was valid, all good!".

In order to recognize the same range proof later on, you need to assign a label to it. This is called a cache key. This cache key is the actual cause of the bug. 

The way this cache key was constructed allowed two different transactions to collide on their cache key. Essentially, one valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) had the same cache key as an invalid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out).

Here's the hack: the attackers submitted the valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) first. Liquid nodes verified this transaction successfully, created a cache key called REKT and stored it in their cache. Then the attackers carefully crafted a second invalid transaction with (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out) that created the same cache key REKT. 

Instead of validating the second transaction and realizing that it printed money out of thin air, Liquid nodes found it in their cache and said "hey I saw this transaction before, everything is fine" and that caused the inflation. 

The attackers then took their 4000 L-BTC and withdrew 4000 BTC onto the Bitcoin base chain.

Note: I might have gotten some details wrong, and I'm aware that I simplified quite a bit. I wrote this post to help people understand what happened. Please feel free to correct me in the comments or add more details below.

text:
Topic: Building a Strong and Coherent Worldview.
Quote 1: Every person has a worldview, but only philosophy makes it coherent and truly productive.
Author: Zafar Mirzo.
Every person has a worldview. Even if they never give it a name, everyone carries a set of ideas about how the world works, what matters most, and how one should live.
But most worldviews are messy, inconsistent, and built from whatever pieces life happened to throw at them. Philosophy is what turns that patchwork into something coherent and actually useful. It examines assumptions, tests beliefs for contradictions, and tries to build a picture of reality that holds together under pressure.
A philosophical worldview is not just smarter. It is more productive. It helps a person make better decisions, hold firmer values, and face life with clearer eyes. Without it, even intelligent people can live with deep contradictions and never notice. With it, life gains direction and strength.
Philosophy doesn’t claim to have all the answers. It simply gives us the best tools we have to build a worldview worth trusting.
Quote 2: The core of a worldview is the unity of rational knowledge and creative feelings.
Author: Zafar Mirzo.
The core of a worldview is the unity of rational knowledge and creative feelings.
Rational knowledge gives structure, clarity, and honesty. It helps us understand how the world actually works. Creative feelings bring warmth, meaning, and direction. They turn cold facts into something we care about and want to act upon.
When these two work together, a worldview becomes alive and powerful. Without rational knowledge, feelings become blind and easily misled. Without creative feelings, knowledge stays dry and disconnected from real life.
The strongest worldviews are not purely logical nor purely emotional. They are both. They allow a person to see clearly and care deeply at the same time. This balance is what turns beliefs into a reliable guide for living, making decisions, and building a life that feels both true and worthwhile.

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
We should bring back mining — but not in the way you think: 

The industry today is overwhelmed with tokens. Tens of thousands are launched daily. Alongside this, we’ve seen a shift in how tokens are distributed. Private markets dominate, memecoins flood public discourse, and many community members who aren’t insiders or pro snipers glued to dexscreener often feel left out of the value equation.

It wasn’t always this way. Bitcoin and Ethereum didn’t just launch tokens; they created ecosystems. Their distribution models weren’t built on insider allocations or bot sniped ‘fair launches’, they were built on work.

Somewhere along the way, we lost this.

First of all, this isn’t a criticism of funding or investment, crypto ecosystems need capital to grow and can’t always rely on wealthy founders. 

But it is a criticism of how the overemphasis on financial contributions has created a bigger problem: the rise of lazy capital. 

Lazy capital is money that shows up, invests, and waits for returns without engaging with or adding real value to the ecosystem. 

Lazy capital may fund projects, but it doesn’t build communities.

So, what if we could reimagine mining as a way to activate capital, not just monetary, but latent capital hidden in the ecosystem?

One potential way to do this is if every token launch had a mining mechanism; a way for everyone, from VCs to community members, to earn tokens through real contributions?

Here’s how it could work:

1. Segment Mining by Stakeholder Groups

-> Investors: Allocate a fixed percentage of tokens for investors but make the rest only available through mining. If investors want a bigger stake, they need to earn it by contributing in some way shape or form; eg if they make an intro that was successful, that should be attested onchain and then awarded in allocation. 

-> Builders: Reward those who contribute technical expertise, build apps, or provide infrastructure.

-> Community Members: Create pathways for evangelists, artists, and content creators to mine tokens by spreading awareness and driving engagement.

It needs to be designed for meritocracy 

-> Bitcoin and Ethereum succeeded because they rewarded effort. Mining today can reward effort in new forms like building products, hosting events, or growing online communities. Onchain attestations will need to be used to back these up — a job for @eas_eth ? 

An example of how allocations could look:

Team: 10% (to incentivize early contributors).

Investors: 10% (with a cap and opportunities to mine more).

Community Mining: 70% (to unlock latent capital and drive participation from all stakeholders + investors).

Treasury: 10% (for long-term sustainability).

3. Enable Organic Price Discovery

@cobie has pointed out how artificial valuations plague token launches today. Mining solves this. It allows for tokens to be earned, used, and valued in the open market, reflecting real demand which fosters healthier market dynamics.

Crypto’s future depends on its ability to tap into the energy, creativity, and passion of its communities. Lazy capital doesn’t scale ecosystems—latent capital does. 

The ecosystems that design mechanisms to unlock and reward this latent capital will be the ones that endure.

By bringing back mining, not as a technical process but as a community-driven framework, we can restore balance to token launches. 

Everyone from VCs, degens, artists, builders, evangelists should have the opportunity to contribute and earn in a fair, meritocratic system.

Curious what you think!

OpenAI Puts $1 Billion Toward AI Cybersecurity, Starting With U.S. Water and Power

⭐️News: OpenAI said it will spend $1 billion to subsidize AI cybersecurity tools, training, and technical support. First partners include U.S. water utilities, grid operators, state and local governments, community banks, and nonprofits. The move follows an open letter from more than 100 companies warning that AI-driven cyberattacks will become widespread within months.  

🪼DA'Take: $1 billion is not going to the open-source community. It is going to power grids and water plants. OpenAI’s logic is blunt. If AI attacks spread, the first to break will not be tech firms. It will be critical infrastructure still running on old systems. This looks less like charity and more like prepaid defense. Better to help them raise the wall now than wait to be blamed after a breach. Market forces will not upgrade life-and-death systems on their own. That takes a shove from someone big enough.  

👀What do you think: An AI company helping critical infrastructure defend itself. The right thing to do, or an early purchase of liability insurance?

EU DSA Labels ChatGPT a Very Large Search Engine

⭐️News: The European Commission designated ChatGPT a “very large online search engine,” pulling a native AI service into the DSA’s toughest duties on transparency, risk assessment, and independent audits. ChatGPT will now face both the AI Act and the DSA at once.  

🪼DA'Take: OpenAI never set out to be a search engine. The EU says if it behaves like one, it gets regulated like one. Once that logic sticks, any AI product that retrieves information can get dropped into the same bucket. Dual regulation is not new. What is new is an old legal frame being stretched over a new species. AI companies now have to solve more than technical problems. They also have to answer a legal one: what exactly are you?  

👀What do you think: When regulators use old definitions to box in new technology, are they drawing boundaries for the industry, or buying time for themselves?

text:
French bitcoin treasury firm Capital B said Monday it bought 376 BTC for €25.3 million ($29.4 million), its largest bitcoin purchase in a year. The acquisition brings its total holdings to 3,521 BTC, bought for €309.4 million ($359.3 million) overall, implying an average purchase price of €87,878 ($102,058) per bitcoin.

The purchase was funded by proceeds from recently completed capital raises, including a €28.7 million ($33.3 million) private placement. That placement included an additional €7.6 million ($8.8 million) investment from Adam Back, lifting his stake to 17.64% on an ordinary basis.

Monday's buy is Capital B's largest since September 2025, when it acquired 551 BTC; the firm bought just 6 BTC last month. Originally known as The Blockchain Group, Capital B rebranded in July 2025 to focus on its bitcoin treasury strategy. In June, it said it was exploring a bitcoin-backed credit product for the European market modeled after Strategy's STRC and Strive's SATA.

Bitcoin traded around $79,500 on Monday, little changed over the past 24 hours, after reaching a local high of about $81,700 last Thursday.

Dear @jaredkushner 

I’m actually on your side. Many doubt your intent, but I know what it is you’re trying to do and achieve and I’ve had several briefings from Jerusalem on various meetings and proposals and discussions you’ve had with them. So I get it. 

But this new-found realization that Gaza is more weaponized and heavily armed than you believed isn’t something new for me or Israel. We’ve been trying to tell you, the administration, the previous administration, and 3 previous administrations before that, and the world that very fact. 

It isn’t easy. Nobody thought it would be. And we’ve sacrificed hundreds of our soldiers, our children, to try to clear it and disarm it, all while receiving nothing but hate and condemnation from the media and much of the world. The various terrorist factions not only in Gaza but in Samaria and Judea, including Fatah and the PA and groups outside of our borders repeatedly pushed the lies and used their own civilians as human shields which is what led to much of the casualties. 

There is simply no easy way to do this. And pressuring us to open it up and somehow just hand over the place while Hamas and others are still fully armed and walking around fully armed and killing their own people while allowing the world to blame us for it will only make it harder. We’re tired of playing the role of the villains when you know full well who the real villains are. And nobody has the right to question how we do things after October 7 and every day of hate towards us since. Nobody. Not even you. 

We’re not your enemy. And many are tired of the politics of labeling us the bad guys to appease the actual terrorists and all their supporters in the Arab world. It’s high time you call out Qatar and Turkey and Saudi Arabia and Egypt and others for their complicity and responsibility in all of this. Repeatedly attacking us may be your method of negotiation with jihadists. But it’s alienating the people and army who are here wanting to support you. The pressure and rhetoric never seems to be aimed at where it should be. And that is also down to a complete lack of understanding and knowledge of the full history that got us to where we are. It does matter. And that mirror needs to be pointed at the faces of those who are responsible for it. Not at us. You will never get peace so long as you keep telling those butchers that they’re not wrong. 

And yes, I do know enough about what’s said behind closed doors. 
I’m happy to have a proper conversation about this if you wish. Peace is the objective. Appeasing those responsible for war isn’t going to achieve it.

text:
there is a certain skill or mindstate that some portion of the people in ai are in, but many people are not. 

that skill is just taking the default reality seriously.

this is a skill because the next 10 years of our lives will be defined by the weird feeling of trying to explain in a calm manner that the science fiction technology you are describing is not only real, but months old at this point

i think many folks see the big labs say basically "the technology we have created is a big deal, it must be taken seriously, and it has problems we are trying to avoid but we want you to be aware of" as a marketing ploy. i believe this represents incompetence in the skill of taking things seriously. if you think this, i think you are  either mostly misinformed, acting childish, or just kind of dumb. 

one version of this is the journalist type, who seems to have a default belief that scientists and technologists are somehow tricksters here to deceive the public. some of this i think comes from journalists reporting on stem leaders as though they were politicians, and so expect them to act as a politician does. 

notably journalists often misunderstand scale or units. someone spending $1m feels like the same level of seriousness as someone spending $1b. so when stargate was announced and it was a $500b budget, that should have been the cue that now is the time to start to take things seriously. instead it was reported on like any other minor news day. 

another version of this is the silicon valley vc type or investor, who, as a whole, seemed to both be completely blindsided by ai, and continue to be blindsided by ai. investors are quite good at retrospectively claiming they saw the thing coming, but their investments & relative allocations say otherwise. 

venture, at it's best, is not good at predicting the future. it's good at predicting people. some people have this little sign above their heads that says "this person is a money machine" is often very good at seeing it and putting money into it. venture is (sometimes) good at promoting things it has already invested in, and i believe this sometimes encourages them to not take things seriously (likely to their own financial ruin).

text:
🚨 On September 4, 2026, the well-known decentralized lending protocol @NotionalFinance was attacked, resulting in a loss of approximately $1.73 million. The SlowMist Security Team has fully analyzed the incident.

🧩 Attack flow:

1️⃣ In a preceding transaction, the attacker deployed auxiliary contracts and called setApprovalForAll on ERC1155Trade to authorize them, after querying two CashMarket maturities and the required AssetIds.
2️⃣ First safeTransferFrom: minted an fCash pair with amount 1 (maturity Sep 4, 2026). The position was too small and rounded to 0 in ETH terms, so the free-collateral check passed.
3️⃣ Second safeTransferFrom: minted an fCash pair with amount uint128.max at a different maturity (Dec 3, 2026), so the two liabilities would not be added in the same bucket and revert under SafeMath.
4️⃣ mintfCashPair then checked free collateral. The two liabilities summed to -2^128, overflowed to 0 when converted to ETH, and the protocol treated the account as healthy.
5️⃣ Receiving contract 2 split the large claim to two auxiliary contracts. The payer was now contract 2, which already held a positive claim, so the check passed and the two contracts received receiver fCash.
6️⃣ In a second transaction, the attacker settled those two positions, increasing the cash balances in Escrow, then called withdraw to realize the profit.

⚙️ Root Cause: ExchangeRate._convertToETH does uint128(balance.abs()) on Solidity 0.6.x with no range check. When the liability is -2^128, 2^128 truncates to 0, so mintfCashPair only sees free collateral ≥ 0 and allows an unbacked position.

🔒 SlowMist Insight: A successful cast is not a successful valuation. Reject any abs() result above type(uint128).max, use SafeCast, and test extremes such as uint128.max and -2^128. Collateral ≥ 0 is not the same as collateral that is real.

Full analysis👇

text:
Liquid hack explained.

Liquid has confidential transactions that hide the amounts for improved privacy. A bug in how these transactions are validated caused inflation of Liquid BTC (L-BTC) and allowed hackers to empty the entire side chain. 

Liquid nodes don't see the amounts of a confidential transaction, so to make sure that the transaction is still valid and doesn't cause inflation nodes check something called a balance proof and a range proof.

The balance proof establish that sum of the input amounts equal the output amounts, i.e., that "x L-BTC going in and x L-BTC going out". But there's a catch. Only relying on a balance proof isn't enough. You also need the range proof.

The range proof establishes that a hidden output amount falls within a positive range. That means a valid output must be at least 1 L-sat and at most 2^64 − 1 L-sats. Range proofs make sure that you can't mint "negative L-BTC".

Why is this even necessary? Remember, the amounts are hidden and a hidden negative amount would allow extra positive outputs to balance against it. Without a range proof, a transaction could say "I've put 1 L-BTC in, and I'm taking two outputs out: one with 4000 L-BTC and one with -3999 L-BTC)." 

This is going to cause a disaster in a little bit.

Once the balance proof, the range proof, and other validations pass, a transaction is regarded as valid and can pass consensus. However, because especially the range proof is computationally expensive, Liquid nodes cache the result of a successful range proof in memory. Essentially, the node remembers "I saw this range proof before and it was valid, all good!".

In order to recognize the same range proof later on, you need to assign a label to it. This is called a cache key. This cache key is the actual cause of the bug. 

The way this cache key was constructed allowed two different transactions to collide on their cache key. Essentially, one valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) had the same cache key as an invalid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out).

Here's the hack: the attackers submitted the valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) first. Liquid nodes verified this transaction successfully, created a cache key called REKT and stored it in their cache. Then the attackers carefully crafted a second invalid transaction with (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out) that created the same cache key REKT. 

Instead of validating the second transaction and realizing that it printed money out of thin air, Liquid nodes found it in their cache and said "hey I saw this transaction before, everything is fine" and that caused the inflation. 

The attackers then took their 4000 L-BTC and withdrew 4000 BTC onto the Bitcoin base chain.

Note: I might have gotten some details wrong, and I'm aware that I simplified quite a bit. I wrote this post to help people understand what happened. Please feel free to correct me in the comments or add more details below.

text:
New post on Eth Research!

Order-dependence as the classifying dimension for frame-transaction mempool admission

By:
- AnkushinDaniil

🔗 https://t.co/oHKXufj8Qe

Highlights:
- The unifying classifier behind multiple proposed mempool/admission mechanisms is whether validation reads order-dependent (contended) state, not how much state it reads.
- The paper groups state reads into three contention classes: Class 0 (single-writer, e.g., sender nonce/balance debit), Class 1 (recent-root-bound where staleness is acceptable, enabled by recent roots), and Class 2 (live-contended shared state requiring the latest value, e.g., AMM price or first-come slots).
- Order-independence within a block aligns with commutativity; via the CALM theorem, the “coordination-free” (order-free) validity fragment corresponds to monotone/commutative checks.
- Existing proposals—MAX_VERIFY_GAS, VOPS profiles, recent roots, 2D gas, and validity proofs—are best understood as different thresholds/ways of handling these contention classes rather than unrelated rules.
- There is an irreducible floor: exactly-once assertions like “this nullifier is unspent” or “this slot is free” are anti-monotone and inherently require coordination/ordering (supported by CALM and the Herlihy consensus hierarchy), so no proof-carrying admission scheme can eliminate sequencing for that core.

ELI5:
When a blockchain node decides whether to accept a transaction into its waiting room (the mempool), it often has to run the transaction’s “validity check.” With account abstraction, that validity check can be any code, so attackers could make nodes do lots of unpaid work. This article says the key question isn’t “how much state does the check read?” but “does the check’s answer depend on the order of transactions in the block?” If the answer does NOT depend on order (like checking only your own nonce), it can often be checked cheaply or even proven ahead of time. If it DOES depend on order (like checking a shared slot is still free), then someone must coordinate and decide an order—there’s no way around it.

text:
💻 I ran an experiment at our weekly all-hands last week: zero laptops.
We always open with a round-robin of updates. I looked up mid-round: half the room heads-down, typing. Eyes glued to screens. No reactions. No eye contact.
In the room, but not IN the room.
So we tried something: one meeting, everyone fully present. No screens. Just listening and talking.
The first five minutes felt strange. Then something shifted — with nothing to hide behind, people started reacting. Interrupting. Building on half-formed ideas out loud. The quietest people had the best ideas.
Here's the thing nobody tells you: note-taking isn't documentation. It's a tax on attention. The person typing isn't fully in the meeting — they're acting as a slow, expensive microphone.
"But we'll forget everything!" — that's the easy part. One small device from @ComuAI_ on the table turns the whole conversation into a recap, decisions, and action items before we're back at our desks. 📝
Old way: half the room talks, half the room types.
New way: everyone thinks out loud. AI keeps the minutes.
Every meeting runs this way now.
My only regret: not trying it a year earlier. 🎙️

结合美国财政部近期的隐秘动作，这轮反弹的节奏可能比所有人预想的都要快。在他的最新复盘里，完整拆解了这波抄底的底层逻辑与操作纪律：

1/ 别被表象迷惑，“变相放水”才是本轮反弹的底座

表面上是 Trump 提了一嘴交易所引发的空头回补，但真正的燃料在宏观：美国财政部预计 9 月 9 日回购 120 亿美元长债、同时再发短债。这等同于缩短政府债务久期，直接向市场灌注流动性并压低美元。这是真金白银的利好。

2/ Uniswap 暴涨 30% 的硬逻辑：隐藏的回购买盘

除了 Uniswap 更改代币经济（让持币者分到协议收入）这层明牌，John 看到了一个隐藏买盘：Robinhood 链上的土狗和代币化股票交易量，正创纪录地流经 Uniswap V4。这直接为 UNI 构筑了最坚实的回购买压。

3/ 最具爆发力的新叙事：Robinhood 链的“资产武器化”

资金正在向新战场迁移。Robinhood 链把土狗和代币化股票绑在了一起，交易对从传统的 SOL、ETH 变成了英伟达、特斯拉。Vlad Tenev 成功把散户对土狗的热情“武器化”成了和华尔街资产对打的牌。这是当前资产代币化最鲜活的样本。

5/ 胜率最高的建仓纪律

不要被 FOMO 带着跑，对想买的资产挂追踪买单等回调；先建 5% 到 15% 的底仓压住手痒，再慢慢定投。“买在恐慌里，任何价格都是好买卖。”

终局思考： 无论叙事怎么变，最终的流动性都要结算回以太坊。
