FOMO 正在成为重要的加密交易入口，安全必须重视！（FOMO安全篇，必看）

首先，登录 FOMO 的 Apple 和 Google 账号，必须绑定自己长期使用的手机号，并开启双重认证。

Apple 账号检查受信任号码，Google 账号检查恢复手机号和两步验证，别把绑了手机等同于开了双重认证，也别把短信当成唯一安全线。

账号必须完全由自己掌控，别拿买来的、借来的账号登录资金账户，手机锁屏和生物识别保护也别关。

然后是下载，只从官网X账号  @fomo   进入，顺着官方链接下载。不要搜到一个同名 App 就装，更别接陌生人发来的安装包、所谓“内部版”“空投专用版”。头像、名字、页面都能仿，别只看 Logo，要核对入口。

下载后，在注册页面填写我的邀请码：oragnes，享受交易手续费优惠 10%，也就是手续费打九折，具体以 App 显示为准。

接下来，记住 FOMO 是非托管钱包，但“非托管”不等于整套系统不会出问题。

第一：钱包关联你注册时使用的 Apple 或 Google 账号，换手机前，先确认原账号能登录、恢复方式还能用。

第二：私钥需要备份就走官方流程、离线妥善保管，不要截图、发微信、存相册和云盘，更不要交给任何“客服”。

第三：FacdID一定要打开，充值、提现、打开应用等都够选上。

第四：大额进去之前，先用小钱走通充值→交易→提现，核对网络、地址、费用和实际到账，别只测试钱能不能充进去。

第五：交易钱包只留计划使用的仓位，长期资产单独保管，盈利定期转出。

第六：碰到验证钱包、修复提现、先转钱才能解冻，不要跟着私信操作，有问题从 App 内帮助入口处理。

平台安全也挡不住 Meme 归零和跟单亏损，排行榜再漂亮，都不能替你承担损失。FOMO 可以拿来找机会，别把全部身家拿来测试安全性。

Bold is the tree hiding the forest of friends who gave up on self-custody.

After a decade, we simply did a poor job of educating people on how to use the chains safely.

Stuck between being too dogmatic, pushing for purity of an overly complex system, and too reckless of yolo mode

Let me try again; don't just bookmark this do it. Give the link to this tweet to your AI and have it help you:

1) Use @ambire as your main wallet; it handles simulation, complex tx, and is designed to work well with @safe 
2) Deploy a Safe now. I don't care if it's a 1/1 linked to your hot wallet for now; it's fine. It's already better this way, and with Ambire, using it is seamless. 

YOU DO NOT HAVE TO USE THE SAFE UI; Ambire will do it all for you.

3a) Generate a real seed; use pen and paper. You'll get the fancy steel stuff later if you want. 

3b) Too lazy for the seed stuff? ok, use a "hotwallet" for your signer generated with a passkeys with an good password manager, you have a Mac? The Passwords app is fine; you're a Revolut client? NordPass is included; you ready to spend a bit? 1Password has a great API, and you'll love it once you're AI-pilled.

5) The signer wallet must hold no funds, doesn't hold gas, doesn't do any txs; it's the key to unlock the door of your safe; it signs, and that's it. You'll learn later that proposing (creating tx), signing, and executing tx are 3 different jobs that don't need to be done by the same wallets.

6a) Now create a second hot wallet, "executooor," and send some gas to it, a few bucks of ETH suffice. Use https://t.co/jnYpeoZ6nv to have some gas on every chain you use.

6b) Don't want to do that? No worries, use the "gas tank" feature on Ambire; it does the same job you can always improve later.

That's it for step one, and just that you're safer than Bold and 99% of guys out there.

Step 2 is buying a hardware wallet and rotating the safe signer with it for much safer holding

Once you're there, you can start considering a 1/2 with a second hw or with an old phone you have in your drawer that you've factory reset and will use only for that. You keep it out of easy reach; it's your insurance if something bad happens to your main signer.

Then maybe a 2/3 and the nerdy stuff; you can always do "better," but the foundation of all that is getting your first safe deployed and climbing from there.

Do it now; it's not hard, it's worth it.

text:
OpenAI 开始把 GPT-6 Astra 放进 KiCad 里做电路之后，我很好奇它画出来的东西，到底能不能真的工作？

EEBench 这篇文章就在认真回答这个问题。

他们没有只看电路图「像不像」，而是把设计放进验证流程里。Agent 负责改元件、连接和参数，后面再用 SPICE 仿真、真实器件参数、容差和 BOM 成本去检查。哪怕电路逻辑看起来没问题，只要真实条件下跑不通，照样算失败。

有意思的事情发生了，硬件 Agent 也开始出现类似 Coding Agent 的闭环了：设计、仿真、看失败、修改、再验证。

而这套 Verifier 以后甚至可以继续变成 RL 的 reward signal。

目前 EEBench V1 规模还很小，只有 13 个任务，也还没覆盖完整 PCB 布局、制造和实物 bring-up，所以离「AI 自己把板子做出来」还有距离。

但方向已经很清楚了。

接下来值得看的是我们能不能把「硬件到底做对没有」这件事，也变成一个可以自动验证的闭环。

text:
Arthur Hayes 的  solana:HwCG1Jr6RbAVsKX1qTaH6JtFYGeE6zaLd13W44YGpump 经济模型来了

FLOP 创世供应量约 24.83 亿枚，而且全部通过空投分配，不设 VC 预挖，也没有公开拍卖。

这个设计先把最容易被市场诟病的低流通、高 FDV、VC 解锁砸盘直接砍掉了，初始筹码主要分给矿工、验证者、Agent 和生态参与者。

真正决定长期供给的是区块释放。

FLOP 平均 1 秒一个区块，初始每个区块释放 96 枚，每 730 天减半一次：96 → 48 → 24 → 12 → 6 → 3，一共减半 5 次，之后永久维持每区块 3 枚。

也就是说 FLOP 不是比特币式的固定总量，而是前期高通胀启动网络，后期进入永久低通胀。

首期新增代币的分配也很明确：75% 给矿工、10% 给验证者、10% 给 Agent、5% 给普通质押者。

这个比例说明 FLOP 的经济模型明显偏向供给侧补贴：绝大部分新增代币都拿去奖励真正提供 AI 推理算力的人，Agent 和验证者拿较小部分，纯质押收益最低。

这套模型好不好，最后就看一个公式：FLOP 的真实推理需求，能不能跑赢新增代币释放。

如果大量 Agent 持续买推理，矿工拿到 FLOP 后有真实买方承接，通胀就是网络补贴.

如果 Agent 需求起不来，96 枚/秒的早期发行速度就会变成持续卖压。

所以 FLOP 的经济模型并不复杂：

前期用高通胀把算力、验证者和 Agent 全部拉进来，再靠每两年减半不断降低新增供给。

模型主要看未来 AI Agent 对推理算力的需求增长速度，能长期超过 FLOP 的发行速度。

text:
Our CEO, Dr. @bengoertzel, has responded to the @BernieSanders–Casar “Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act,” which would permanently prohibit the development and deployment of superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development pending federal review, and direct US foreign policy toward preventing superintelligence from being built anywhere in the world.

The legislation focuses on the concentration of frontier AI development among a small number of large corporations. Dr. Goertzel agrees that this concentration creates a problem and supports external audits, incident reporting, and independent technical oversight. He disagrees with prohibition as the response.

AGI development does not depend on a scarce physical resource that can be controlled through international agreements. The research consists of mathematics, software, published algorithms, and commodity hardware. A global ban would therefore require surveillance of general-purpose computing while leaving states, military programs, and other actors outside that system able to continue their work.

The effect on open development is a central concern. A ban carrying severe criminal penalties would be easier to enforce against researchers who publish their work, open-source their code, and collaborate across institutions than against programs operating in secret. “It selectively destroys the development that is visible, which is to say, the open, decentralized, academically published, internationally collaborative work, while leaving intact the development that is hidden.”

The proposed pause on advanced AI development raises another issue. Establishing a new federal agency and review process could favor companies with large compliance teams and existing relationships with regulators. The result could be greater advantage for the same incumbents the legislation seeks to constrain.

Dr. Goertzel proposes a different approach centered on public compute, open development, external oversight, cognitive-liberty protections, and mechanisms for distributing AI-generated economic gains. The question he puts forward is “under whose control, with what values, and toward whose benefit.”

author: Pluvio9yte
quoted_text:
过去做一次深入的竞品调研，你往往需要买一堆每个月上百刀的订阅，然后在 Similarweb、Ahrefs、Reddit 和 X 之间来回切网页，最后填到表里的数据还经常对不上。

但现在，你不需要单独买任何一个月费订阅，也不用再搞一堆复杂的 API 密钥。

你只需要把产品网址丢给已经接好 AIsa 的 Claude Code 或 Codex，用一句最实在的业务目标，把它打发去干活。Agent 会自己去查产品事实、找竞品、比流量渠道、翻用户原话，最后交给你一份能直接拿去开会讨论的竞品报告。

我们可以直接看一个最典型的场景。这是我扔给 Agent 的原话：

“请分析这个产品 Youmind，识别 5 个主要竞品。比较它们的定位、核心功能、网站流量来源、用户评价和内容渠道，最后输出一份竞品分析报告，并给出 3 个值得切入的差异化方向。”

注意，我没有指定它该调哪个接口。规划任务、筛选数据源、交叉核对，全权交由 Agent 自己完成。

真正接通了外部商业数据的 Agent，在这个过程中会走出一条非常清晰的思考链： 先读官网，搞清楚这产品卖给谁、主打哪一句； 接着用 Tavily 或 Exa 把公开事实和候选竞品补全； 随后调用 Similarweb，把几家网站的访问规模、渠道结构和搜索表现直接拉到同一张桌子上；

同时，Reddit 和 X 负责另一半——去看看真实用户在夸什么、骂什么、在什么场景下反复提及； 最后收口，一份包含定位、功能、流量来源、评价、内容渠道的报告生成完毕，并顺手给你指出了 3 个还能挤进去的差异化方向。

这里面最核心的一层，必须单拎出来说一下，那就是底层的 Similarweb 数据。

AIsa 是目前极少数能把 Similarweb 官方 API V5 直接交给 Agent 调用的平台。走的是正规授权接口，和市面上那些爬虫、镜像站压根不是一路东西，而且那些镜像站最多只能让你在网页上查查数据，根本不提供API。 

你要知道，这种官方服务主要面向企业客户，个人开发者和小团队自己去谈，一年从 5 万美元起步很常见。哪怕是 Ahrefs、Semrush，各开一份进阶订阅，一个月也得大几百刀。

而 AIsa 的做法是：把这些顶级情报源全部打包到一个账户里，共享余额，按次扣费。这意味着，Agent 每次帮你做竞品调研，你不用再同时订阅多份服务。

一份真正敢拿来做商业决策的报告，必须留下证据。 在这份报告里，哪段数据来自 Similarweb，哪段是 Reddit 的用户原话，哪段来自搜索结果，全都能精准指回去。模型自己补的判断，和接口返回的硬数据，被分得清清楚楚。 以后你拿这份报告做决策，至少知道哪一行经得起推敲复查。

顺着这套打法，你能做的事还有很多：

产品 SEO 检测：丢一个网站 URL，它能出 SEO 诊断，告诉你关键词覆盖率、SERP 表现，以及最该先修哪几个页面。
GEO / AI 可见度检测：丢品牌名加几个竞品，它能直接告诉你，在 Perplexity 这类 AI 答案页里谁被提得多、引用从哪来、你的内容该往哪补。

产品地址：
https://t.co/RITVjGXzim
查看 AIsa 支持的完整 Premium API 目录：https://t.co/MaYUK024g6
探索完整的 Go-to-Market 解决方案：https://t.co/VpFCTuSNUw

Darkbloom: Day 15

We have been locked in for last one week; It has been very exciting and we shipped a lot of improvements to the system.

Metrics:

- 16.3B tokens served: New ATH & 60% higher than last day.
- $420K Network ARR (4x in 2 weeks); 
- 99.96% uptime (very happy considering we're a  distributed network).
- ~15-17% utilization at peak; median: 13% utilization. 

Product:
- One big win: we take up 30% of traffic for Gemma 4 26B
- We cut latency by ~1.5 second. We plan to ship few more features that would reduce latency by 30-90%. This will include cache-aware routing.

- We shipped new routing and system optimizations which were key reason for us to cut down 429s. More such to come.

- We will be adding 3-4 more models in the coming week. Excited for @Spangler3000 to be helping us with this! 

- We conducted MLX(.)Fast which has improved Gemma 4's performance by 2.5x -- the improvements are in process of being imported by @TheDavidTai.

- We are exploring payouts solutions such as Stripe Global Payouts to add 67 more countries. 

- Astra has redesigned our Console UI (this is AGI, ngl). We will also be starting up our efforts for the MacOS app for better user experience. 

- We have also been looking more deep into Autopilot where we load up models according to the traffic and other factors to maximise the provider earnings.

- Our new landing page is almost ready and coming up with one suprise ;) -- huge kudus to @0xkydo and Estella. 

- Also huge thanks to @iLLRiPHiTTeR for helping us while onboarding new models on OpenRouter. We were able to find out minor issues in our inference engine.

- We are also working through engineering practices and cleaning up code.

Thank you everyone for being part of this journey and reading along this update. 

We build these systems to bring people together to contribute to this AI economy.

As always, it has been rewarding to keep doing what we do.

Until next time.

text:
In the last month, there were two attacks on scammers involving balconies. There have been several more without. These probably won’t stop. 

The world is a scary place. I wrote the post below for the same reason writers have told stories for millennia: to warn others of animals in the tall grass. 

In crypto, there are scams in every post. You cannot meaningfully engage without the potential to lose all your money on baited hooks. Some of the biggest accounts are the worst offenders. It’s nearly impossible to find opportunity, and harder to keep it. 

But the world is scarier if you're a bad actor. There are people who will wrong you, take your money, then spend it on penthouses and rental cars and Brazilian women, all without wondering what happens next. If you think working for retirement is bad, imagine looking over your shoulder for the rest of your life because of a scam you platformed when you were in your 20's. I’ve watched big, tough narcissists resort to blubbering about their mothers when confronted with evidence of their self-betrayals.

I grew up gambling, so it's funny when I see people who have no idea what they're doing. Scammers, widely known by thousands online, pocketing hard-earned money and hoping they didn't wrong someone bigger and meaner than them. Hoping their victim isn't the crying cousin of a cartel boss or a single father with nothing else to lose.

That's why it's easier to not do it. Never drop a contract address and not deliver. Never lie about charity then spend the money on yourself. People have long memories. They will remember every time you defrauded them, even if you act like it never happened.

After ten years in crypto, I still impress my wife with how fast I fall asleep as soon as my head hits the pillow. Some things money can’t buy.
author: notsofast
quoted_text:
crypto recently inspired me to write a short story this morning

“Rugged’

Bros out, phones out, as you leave Marquee. Someone said Ansem was coming but that was hours ago.
No one looks up even while they say good-bye.

Things are good in a bull market.
Well, they’re good for you.
It’s been like this for weeks but it feels like longer.
You’ve been putting in work. You’re not really good at anything, and you can’t code, but you can show up every day and that’s more than most.

That’s why you’re popular. Almost exclusively within a tiny internet niche populated by anonymous millionaires but that’s where you spend all your time so maybe that means something. How you style your hair, what your sunglasses reflect in your selfies, it’s all curated to return the highest EV from your followers.

You raised funding for a project. Kind of.
You’re waiting for it to finish. The designers are doing last touches. But you got the money. And when you launch, it’ll be something. Definitely not a rug, like people are saying. It’ll happen, but on a long time frame, kind of like how you’re bulking up or how you’re going to start a family.
You get called a scammer in the comments but you just block them and move on.
Life is too short.

The club had been too crowded. Not with hot girls but random guys just hanging around, way too close. Constantly bumping into you, it was annoying.

Your phone is about to die but you request an Uber before it does. You find the guy in a black SUV— parked across the street, which is annoying— then you’re on your way to where you’re staying in the city.

You ask the driver to turn up the music, then to slow down because he’s going way too fast.
Maybe that’s why he doesn’t tell you about the alert on his phone. A warning that there might be an AirTag near you and to check your belongings.
He dismisses it and keeps driving.

You get to your building, hop out, and slam the car door a little too hard.

The doorman is staring at his iPad, as usual, and the elevator is sitting open.
You go to your apartment, one of the top floors but not quite a penthouse.
Toss your keys on the counter in the dark.

They’re waiting for you.
The first one shows up behind you, after you shut the door.
Dressed in all black, not too much bigger than you but the way he appears out of the silence, mixed with the icy cold throughout your body, makes him feel as impossible as a brick wall.

When he throws you to the ground, it feels like you have to let yourself curl up, willingness to defer to fear.  Convince yourself it’s the right thing to do.

They put you in a chair in your “dining room.” All you think about is how you’ve never really sat in it before. This isn’t how things are done. This isn’t your apartment anymore.

You watch the two of them.
There’s almost an understanding. Flipping all the furniture, ripping into expensive cushions and breaking artisan wood, this must be some sort of retribution for something. You pray some neighbor hears and differentiates between the ransacking and your usual stomping around to Spotify. Pray, somehow, someone calls the cops.

They gather your wallets, phones, laptops. Any random USB sitting on a desk is collected.

Your adrenaline makes their accents thick, vague, an obstacle in their threats. Germans, Euros, maybe Koreans? Their masks and gloves cover every part of their skin and that scares you.

They tell you what they’re going to do. It doesn’t feel real. You might think explaining threats is ineffective but when you’re tied to the chair, hands behind your back— when they say they’re going to cut off your fingers one-by-one and hand them to you to keep count— you tend to believe them.

They show you pictures of your nieces. They might be pulled from Facebook but the fact that they have them is terrifying enough. The thought creeps in your mind that if you had kids, it would be them.

What are you supposed to say?

That you spent the money on a private box to watch your favorite team? That you paid too much for a brand-new car from a slick-haired Armenian? Would they be willing to take a five-figure deposit from an all-inclusive Bahamas resort?

You stare blankly at them, maybe having missed one of their demands, and the bigger one grabs you by the shoulders and drags you out to your balcony. He’s yelling, wanting something you can’t give him.

He holds you, tightly, over the railing, above twenty-three stories by the collar of your new Versace shirt.

Then, the one inside, now typing into one of your laptops, barks something out in a foreign language. You can hear the concern in his voice. Does he see your balance? Did he check the chain?

The man holding your collar looks at you with new eyes, seeing the fraud.

What happens next isn’t surprising.
Maybe it’s an accident, maybe the quality of the fabric from Canal St. isn’t what it used to be. It doesn’t really matter. You feel the air rush past you and the heart-racing pull of gravity makes your body buzz.

The apartment is staged so that the coroner rules no foul play.
The reply guys call it karma, in a way they’re right.

text:
4,000 XRP wallets were drained in 3 hours on Sept 3rd.

The culprit?
XRPH's mobile app stored wallet data insecurely, and its staking feature was silently sending seed phrases to a remote server.

This is what most people miss: "non-custodial" doesn't mean your keys stay on your device.

Some apps claim self-custody while handling your seed in ways you'd never expect.

Two things to always verify:
- where your seed is generated, &
- where it's stored.

If your seed ever touched a server, treat it as compromised and do not import it into a hardware wallet.

Start fresh. 

An air-gapped hardware wallet like Keystone 3 Pro keeps your seed offline and secure from day one, where no server can reach it.

뇌가 파일이 될 때, 실험의 대상은 생명에서 의식으로 넓어질 수 있다
(Carrot cave님 의견 요약)

1/ 초파리 뇌 지도를 마인크래프트 속 움직임에 연결했다는 사례.

공개된 연구 결과를 개인이 AI와 함께 실행 가능한 실험으로 바꾸기 시작함. 논문을 읽고 이해하는 것에서, 직접 구현하고 바꿔보는 것까지의 거리가 짧아지고 있음.

2/ 뇌 회로가 디지털 모델이 되면 복사하고, 연결을 수정하고, 결과를 비교할 수 있음.

실험 비용이 내려가면 참여자와 시도 횟수가 늘어남. AI가 구현을 도울수록 무엇을 만들고 왜 시험할지 정하는 능력, 나온 결과를 검증하는 능력의 가치가 커지는 구조.

3/ 여기서 더 멀리 가면 인간 의식의 복제 가능성이라는 질문에 닿음.

의식이 뇌의 물리적 작동에서 생기고 그 작동을 충분히 재현할 수 있다면, 의식도 복제할 수 있을까. 두 복제본이 서로 다른 경험을 쌓기 시작하면 어느 쪽을 ‘나’라고 불러야 할까.

4/ 시뮬레이션 우주 가설과도 연결됨.

언젠가 가상 환경 속 신경계가 실제로 경험을 갖게 된다면, 구성된 세계도 그 안의 존재에게는 현실이 될 수 있다는 뜻. 우리가 사는 세계 역시 그런 환경일 가능성을 생각하게 만드는 출발점임.

다만 가상 파리의 움직임이 그 가설을 증명하는 것은 아님.

5/ 아직 뇌의 연결 지도와 뇌의 작동, 의식 사이에는 큰 간극이 있음.

게임 속 움직임만으로 기억이나 주관적 경험을 재현했다고 볼 수는 없음. 그럼에도 의식의 복제와 가상 세계 속 경험이라는 오래된 질문을 실험으로 좁혀갈 수 있다면 의미가 큼.

6/ 존재란 무엇인가 하는 질문

뇌를 디지털로 재현하는 기술이 발전할수록 ‘무엇을 만들 수 있나’에 이어 ‘지금 만든 존재는 무엇인가’를 묻게 될 것 같음. 인간 의식의 복제 가능성과 우리가 경험하는 현실의 성격이 같은 질문 위에서 만날 수 있음.

In March 2025 I wrote up a tiny French casino operator at €1.73/share, trading at 4.4x EV/EBIT with a 26% FCF yield.

Last week, it received an offer to be bought out at €6.19 per share.

$SFCA $SFCA.PA Société Française de Casinos.

It owns four casinos in French tourist towns plus hotels, restaurants and spas.

· €8.8M market cap when I wrote it up.
· Net cash on the balance sheet.
· Free cash flow matching reported profits, year after year.

The whole thesis was almost boring: a steady, profitable, well-run business, ignored because it was too small and too illiquid for anyone to bother with.

On August 27, Merkur Spielbanken signed a promise to acquire 95% of Casigrangi, the holding company that owns 81.21% of SFC.

The implied price: €6.19 per SFC share.

The premiums tell you how badly the market was pricing this:
· 157.9% over the previous close
· 145.2% over the 60-day VWAP
· 195.9% over the 240-day VWAP

The stock now trades at €5.90, a small discount to the offer price.

I am selling it here at €5.90.
That works out to +241% from my €1.73 write-up price.

More than a 3-bagger.

Another example that cheap, ignored and cash-generative businesses don't stay ignored forever.

Value always finds its way.

Follow for more.

text:
@otc_labs is a Solana protocol that links a @Pumpfun coin ($OTC) to an NFT collection: the coin is burned to mint a desk, and a cut of the coin's trading fees buys tokenized stock into every desk's vault. Each desk is a @metaplex Core NFT with a vault derived from it; whoever holds the NFT owns the vault's contents, and a sale or transfer moves everything with it.

Minting a desk burns 100,000 $OTC and pays a 0.5 SOL surcharge, 0.45 of it into a shared pot. The pot also takes a slice of the token's pumpfun creator fees (10% of each collection as of Sep 7, down from 15% on Sep 1) plus the collection's royalty, and spends its balance on the next asset in a rotation that has grown to 13 slots: twelve tokenized equities (ANDURIL and OPENAI joined Sep 1) plus $OTC itself. Each purchase is split equally across every live desk.

One week on from the Aug 31 check:

Supply went from 748M to 712M $OTC, down 36M (4.8%) in seven days, against 252M burned in the first four. Daily burns ran 7.3M on Sep 1 and 1.1M to 2.2M a day since Sep 4.

Desks went from 1,926 to 2,222, 44% of the 5,000 cap. Those 296 mints account for 29.6M of the week's burn. Mints ran 3 to 16 a day over the last four days while the coin's average daily price in the pool rose 5.9x from Sep 4 to Sep 7.

text:
Is Latin really so different from Italian?

I have seen kids doing this 1000x better than me, but just to give you an idea:

“Il buon padre di famiglia è un uomo rigoroso, leale, onesto e determinato che cura con dedizione la propria famiglia”

Drop the articles:

“Buon padre di famiglia è uomo rigoroso, leale, onesto e determinato che cura con dedizione propria famiglia.”

Restore the old endings:

“Bonus pater de familia est homo rigorosus, lealis, honestus et determinatus qui curat con dedicatione propriam familiam.”

Turn di into a genitive and tidy the preposition:

“Bonus pater familiae est homo rigorosus, lealis, honestus et determinatus qui curat cum dedicatione propriam familiam.”

Move the verbs later:

“Bonus pater familiae homo rigorosus, lealis, honestus, determinatus est qui propriam familiam cum dedicatione curat.”

😇

这个 LCC 机制也很有意思：

3Jane 本质上是在做链上信贷生意，要先找到需要资金的 需求方，再把链上资金配给他们赚利差。

问题是，贷款机会不是随时都有。如果为了随时放贷，提前趴着 $100M USDC 等项目，资金效率会非常低。所以这个 LCC（Levered Callable Capital）就是来解决资金效率的问题的。

LCC 本质是「流动性期权」，存钱许下承诺的用户作为卖方，3Jane 相当于买方。

举个例子，用户作为资金的初始提供方，你不用现在就把 $1M 资金直接给 3Jane，只需要先压一小笔保证金，并承诺：“以后你需要这 $1M 的时候，我能拿出来。”

@3janexyz 则会为这个承诺持续给你付钱。

这样做的好处是，资金效率最大化，协议方和资金提供方都不占用资金库存，进而把闲置的资金也变成了一种可以产生收益的资产。

text:
I want to close my chapter, for now, on the EIP-8363 analysis. After having a few more calls with people who are for- and against- issuance reduction (stakers, founders, DeFi people, and regular Ethereum holders) - here is a subjective view on the matter. I think it has some new aspects I didn't see much of before (💡)

- TLDR 1: I don't think this should go through right now. The proposal is raw and the arguments are still weak. It's weird to say this because it has been in the works for five years on and off, but it still doesn't make sense. I respect the authors who put time and effort into this, but after looking into it and having so many conversations across the space - it doesn't check out.
- TLDR 2: Neither side should be talking about anyone being "captured." You cannot say that core devs living and breathing the network are captured. No, they care about it and are involved. That is good! Similarly, you cannot say DeFi founders or the staking companies are captured. These people own the asset and are economically interested in having it grow. We have to put those arguments aside - it is just cheap talk.
- TLDR 3: Regarding the process: whether now or later, issuance policy shouldn't just go through a normal network upgrade process. It's not just about repricing or a minor technical tweak; this is way too big to be considered in that fashion. Maybe it could work within the existing process, but only if the opinions of founders and other stakeholders were respected a bit more, rather than just discarding them all as being captured.

Now to the arguments 🦞

I haven't really strayed from what I wrote a few weeks ago (tweet below). As a shorter summary, the argument for reduction falls through three main holes.

1. First, there is this allegiance to a "no inflation" economy perception: the idea that inflation is inherently bad, that (over)paying for something is bad, and that there is just too much of something. That mindset is not correct. In the modern economic world, since we stopped making money only from growing potatoes, it doesn't make sense. The belief that this will somehow make the Ethereum price moon, or that there is too much ETH being dumped on the market, is nonsense. It's one of the least inflating assets.

💡 You have to consider your broader goals. Your issuance strategy should reflect your general adoption strategy. If you think ETH is just an asset, money, a unit of account, or whatever narrative you want to come up with - like the "pet rock" meme Bitcoin style - fine. It's not bad, and it's okay to say that. But then the general adoption strategy should reflect it. It should just be marketing a hard asset, not worry about devs, open-source or anything creative. It's just digital gold, go to hard money conferences and enjoy.

However, if you see Ethereum as a World Computer, as a way to build different use cases, as an "infinite garden" for lack of a better phrase, as a platform - then there is no point in cutting the issuance. Currently, issuance creates different opportunities and products on this platform. EVEN IF you think it's a subsidy, then what? Platforms have subsidies. Why tamper with it if you have no definite alternative. These subsidies worked, they continue working and getting attention, and the platform is winning as a result of that (adoption, liquidity, trust, security, etc.)

If you offboard one big user segment from your marketplace, what's your alternative? Because you are then killing some of the plants in your garden that you've previously incentivized. It's not a weed, and presenting it as a weed is incorrect because nothing shows that's the case.

2. Second, the argument falls through on all the talk about the staking ratio, staking centralization, supply capture, solo stakers, inability to pass slashing, and so on. These are generally good discussions to have, but the suggested proposal does not fix those 🚫

💡 Take the part about slashing and forks, for example. All of these fancy ideas of how staker behavior is going to play out aren't really realistic. Nobody writes about which network - in terms of a slashing event or a fork - USDC, USDT, and centralized issuers would actually consider and back. 

Important factors affecting network resilience should be solved, but this proposal does not solve them. It does not improve conditions for solo stakers. The argument that the staking distribution will get worse if we continue - is also unproven. There is no proper distinction made between "good" LSTs and "bad" LSTs (if you want to think this way). If you believe that Binance and Coinbase staking shouldn't be increasing as much, that's a different discussion. A blanket cut wouldn't kill them as much as it would kill some LSTs that are actually favorable to the development of the core network. I'm not against an issuance reduction as a move potentially; I'm against how it is being argued, and that it's being argued in a weak way .

3. Third, the mechanics of yield are now being accepted as an asset in DeFi protocols (stETH over raw ETH, for example). These are interesting opportunities to consider, but thinking you can mess with this in isolation while killing what exists now isn't cool. Having Ethereum's economic policy be more set in stone is far more important to current participants than just trying out stuff by breaking an ecosystem that exists today.

💡 If institutions and such players appreciate ETH as an asset and engage with real use cases, do not stop them by trying to hypothetically make other use cases possible. They appreciate the current staking rate and have built strategies around it. 

If the proposal would solve security or network resilience while causing some pain in the short term, that would be acceptable. But as I've established, the arguments presented are weak and in many cases incorrect, so it doesn't even solve the purpose.

-----

You have to decide what you actually want to happen:

- Do you want to play trader and mess around with the ETH price by thinking less inflation is better
- Or do you want to solve network resilience and make it uncapturable?

You have to answer one of these questions. Right now, they are all packaged together. As a result, it's a mess, because it's not solving a problem that is explained - or it's solving a problem that is not proven to exist. 

Sorry 8363, but hope no.

A meme paired with a 3x short on $PONS is called "TAMPONS"... 

The mechanics for TAMPONS are pretty interesting:

1) Every $TAMPONS trade pays a 1% fee; part of that revenue is continuously routed into collateral backing a 3× short position on $PONS 

2) If PONS falls, the short generates a profit. The system periodically realizes part of it, then uses 75% of the proceeds to market-buy and burn TAMPONS

3) Flywheel: 

TAMPONS volume → fees → larger PONS short → realized profits if PONS falls → TAMPONS buybacks + burns

It isn’t a direct or fully redeemable hedge; holders don’t own the short or have a claim on its collateral. But structurally, TAMPONS converts trading activity & PONS downside into recurring buy pressure for itself

This testnet brings together Frame Transactions (EIP-8141), Keyed Nonces (EIP-8250), Recent Roots (EIP-8272), FOCIL (EIP-7805), and VOPS Profiles (EIP-8369).

We’ve been sending private transactions through a minimal privacy pool built on these changes. It’s amazing to see them flow through the public mempool and land onchain, without trusted intermediaries and with FOCIL inclusion guarantees.  

It's important because it shows that unstoppable, unconditional, trustless privacy can be implemeted and just works.

Test it. Try to break it. Help us improve it. And if you want native privacy on L1, help us make the case for shipping these EIPs in Hegotá.

It’s been a pleasure working with ethrex over the past couple of months, and a lot of effort is also being invested from other teams. 

Expect more news soon!

text:
Robinhood Chain Stock CEOs’ X Handles🪶

1/ Stock memecoins began emerging on Robinhood, paired with tokenized versions of publicly traded stocks.

2/ However, $AMC’s CEO strongly pushed back against it.

3/ "We have never approved the issuance of $AMC as a tokenized stock. This could potentially violate securities laws."

4/ In response, Robinhood CEO @vladtenev replied, "What's the concern?" which sparked a back-and-forth between the two sides.

5/ Immediately afterward, solana:FL4eKdJrVZ1dVu1RoekeQRnuPxavzD4oCcR5HTcspump, a memecoin paired with $AMC, and $MEME, short for $AMC, a memecoin, surged sharply. The phrase "What's the concern?" itself also became a meme, sending $CONCERN higher.

6/ But there are positive cases as well.

7/ $HIMS CEO @AndrewDudum followed @bonercoinlong, the account behind $BONER.

8/ Right after that, $BONER surged, and the tokenized $HIMS also spiked.

- Is there a tokenized stock deployed on the Robinhood?
- How likely are they to mention their own tokenized stock?

quoted_text:
Understanding The Role of The Canton Foundation.

Led by @viv_diwakar, The @CantonFdn is one of (if not the) most important components of the @CantonNetwork ecosystem. 

Origins...

It was originally launched in July 2024, alongside Canton mainnet, as the Global Synchronizer Foundation (GSF), but has since rebranded to the Canton Foundation we know today.

Its mission, however, has not changed: Create neutral, open governance for the network.

Structure...

The Foundation is built as an independent, not-for-profit body so that no single entity (like Digital Asset or a single firm) can dictate network policy alone.

Various world-leading institutions are represented within the Foundation. These include household names like Goldman Sachs, Tradeweb, and a whole suite of others.

Within the Foundation exist several committees like:

- The Tokenomics Committee ( $CC network economics)
- The Accountability Committee (SV tracking, milestone completion, etc)
- Tech & Ops Committee (tech roadmap, CIPs, etc)

Current Role...

The Foundation's role is widespread, and effectively encompasses every aspect of the Canton ecosystem, from development funding and grants, through to the tokenomic mechanisms that underpin the whole ecosystem.

Perhaps most importantly, however, the Foundation ensures and manages the smooth running of the Global Synchronizer - The component that allows Canton's network of networks to actually interoperate. 

Why This Matters...

Canton has made a name for itself as the network most capable of onboarding large, regulated institutions. 

But it is the Foundation that helps allow for this by giving a guarantee of fair, non-monopolised access to Canton's shared financial infrastructure.

Beyond this, it is through the Foundation that Canton's growing ecosystem of applications has been fostered and, in part, funded.

The Foundation's role and structure is ultimately too sophisticated to boil down in a single post, but hopefully this starts to paint the picture of why it is such an important component of the ecosystem we've all chosen to build in.

for the newly minted fomo users who are realising that memes have no moat beyond attention and are dipping their toes into fundamentals, here's a simple checklist of what differentiates tokens

1. Who they are, background, founding team, what’s your edge in this space? - ultimately this space is all founder quality, that's what drives 100x outcomes. Crypto's bar is so low that the difference b/w an A tier and B tier operator is 100s of m in mc; also guarantees you won't get rug if they're serious operators

2. Value accrual - What is the token, what is it being used for and how does it accrue value to long term investors

Moat 2 is how the token accrues value. You may think all tokens are the same but they're not. Hyperliquid is an extreme example and not really feasible for an example tbh. Too many people use HYPE and say people should do that. They shouldn't. But they should have some sort of focus for the token, and above all else, the token cannot have some sort of bundle (whether snipers, investors, VC unlocks) dumping millions in MC into market

3. Product - GTM / Distribution / Catalysts / Thematic / Growth; Why does the product have PMF & how do you differentiate from competitors ; Is this actually a problem, and how do you solve it?

Firstly high growth themes are real; Perps / launchpads are more "sexy" than say, bridges or yield farms. Generally the idea also has to have some sort of huge untapped blue ocean (e.g Digital Collectibles, or AI) and a product that has genuine usage and traction (the fabled PMF!)

4. Others
- Biz / monetization models - less important for memes, and less impt in certain market conditions. will be important eventually 
- Runway, profitability, raising, financial metrics - hard to get unless you have founder access

In the last month, there were two attacks on scammers involving balconies. There have been several more without. These probably won’t stop. 

The world is a scary place. I wrote the post below for the same reason writers have told stories for millennia: to warn others of animals in the tall grass. 

In crypto, there are scams in every post. You cannot meaningfully engage without the potential to lose all your money on baited hooks. Some of the biggest accounts are the worst offenders. It’s nearly impossible to find opportunity, and harder to keep it. 

But the world is scarier if you're a bad actor. There are people who will wrong you, take your money, then spend it on penthouses and rental cars and Brazilian women, all without wondering what happens next. If you think working for retirement is bad, imagine looking over your shoulder for the rest of your life because of a scam you platformed when you were in your 20's. I’ve watched big, tough narcissists resort to blubbering about their mothers when confronted with evidence of their self-betrayals.

I grew up gambling, so it's funny when I see people who have no idea what they're doing. Scammers, widely known by thousands online, pocketing hard-earned money and hoping they didn't wrong someone bigger and meaner than them. Hoping their victim isn't the crying cousin of a cartel boss or a single father with nothing else to lose.

That's why it's easier to not do it. Never drop a contract address and not deliver. Never lie about charity then spend the money on yourself. People have long memories. They will remember every time you defrauded them, even if you act like it never happened.

After ten years in crypto, I still impress my wife with how fast I fall asleep as soon as my head hits the pillow. Some things money can’t buy.

Want to combine uAgents + @solana  transactions? Build this 3-Agent flow.

PlayerAgent

→ Loads its Solana wallet
→ Sends an `escrowRequest`
→ Transfers SOL to escrow

ChallengerAgent

→ Does the same from a second wallet

EscrowAgent

→ Receives both requests
→ Pulls live BTC price data
→ Determines the winner
→ Transfers the payout
→ Messages both Agents with the result

All three register through https://t.co/jQHISjPvoi’s Almanac, communicate through typed uAgent messages and execute transactions on Solana Devnet.

The example uses three specialised Agents instead of stuffing wallet management, external data, decision logic and settlement into one process.

Run it on Devnet first:
`poetry run python escrow_agent.py`

Then start the Player and Challenger Agents. From there, extend the pattern into DeFi workflows, NFT auctions or other Agent-driven on-chain logic.

Build the Solana example today. Check @Fetch_ai_IL guide → https://t.co/fFEYSaH6og

text:
The Biggest Month in RWA Perp History Came as Its Main Trade Broke Down

August closed at $799.5B in RWA perp volume, edging past July’s $792B to set a new monthly high.

But the record came as the market’s main trade was starting to unwind. Memory stocks had driven activity since June, then sold off sharply between Aug. 15 and 25.

Aug. 19 captured that shift. A day after a faulty pre-market print marked the SK Hynix perp down 17.9% and triggered $57.4M in liquidations across 960 accounts, RWA perps traded $57.6B, the second-largest daily volume on record.

So August’s record was not simply a continuation of the June-July rally. Much of the activity came as that trade started to break down.

RWA perps are perpetual futures on stocks, commodities, FX and indices. CMC Research tracks 19 venues that list them.

For the full August breakdown, read the report 👇

text:
A big milestone towards native privacy on Ethereum L1

This testnet brings together Frame Transactions (EIP-8141), Keyed Nonces (EIP-8250), Recent Roots (EIP-8272), FOCIL (EIP-7805), and VOPS Profiles (EIP-8369).

We’ve been sending private transactions through a minimal privacy pool built on these changes. It’s amazing to see them flow through the public mempool and land onchain, without trusted intermediaries and with FOCIL inclusion guarantees.  

It's important because it shows that unstoppable, unconditional, trustless privacy can be implemeted and just works.

Test it. Try to break it. Help us improve it. And if you want native privacy on L1, help us make the case for shipping these EIPs in Hegotá.

It’s been a pleasure working with ethrex over the past couple of months, and a lot of effort is also being invested from other teams. 

Expect more news soon!

A reviewer judging robot demonstration footage has to find the grasp, follow the hand through an occlusion and rule on whether what remains is a complete demonstration, so an hour of video takes longer to clear than it took to record.

Adding cameras or compute raises the volume entering the pipeline and leaves the rate of decisions where it was.

Proof of Quality, Sapien's evaluation system for AI work, raises that rate: qualified experts set the judgment, agents qualify against it and take the volume, and the experts stay on the calls that decide a batch.

How does your pipeline report the rate of decisions?

Bold is the tree hiding the forest of friends who gave up on self-custody.

After a decade, we simply did a poor job of educating people on how to use the chains safely.

Stuck between being too dogmatic, pushing for purity of an overly complex system, and too reckless of yolo mode

Let me try again; don't just bookmark this do it. Give the link to this tweet to your AI and have it help you:

1) Use @ambire as your main wallet; it handles simulation, complex tx, and is designed to work well with @safe 
2) Deploy a Safe now. I don't care if it's a 1/1 linked to your hot wallet for now; it's fine. It's already better this way, and with Ambire, using it is seamless. 

YOU DO NOT HAVE TO USE THE SAFE UI; Ambire will do it all for you.

3a) Generate a real seed; use pen and paper. You'll get the fancy steel stuff later if you want. 

3b) Too lazy for the seed stuff? ok, use a "hotwallet" for your signer generated with a passkeys with an good password manager, you have a Mac? The Passwords app is fine; you're a Revolut client? NordPass is included; you ready to spend a bit? 1Password has a great API, and you'll love it once you're AI-pilled.

5) The signer wallet must hold no funds, doesn't hold gas, doesn't do any txs; it's the key to unlock the door of your safe; it signs, and that's it. You'll learn later that proposing (creating tx), signing, and executing tx are 3 different jobs that don't need to be done by the same wallets.

6a) Now create a second hot wallet, "executooor," and send some gas to it, a few bucks of ETH suffice. Use https://t.co/jnYpeoZ6nv to have some gas on every chain you use.

6b) Don't want to do that? No worries, use the "gas tank" feature on Ambire; it does the same job you can always improve later.

That's it for step one, and just that you're safer than Bold and 99% of guys out there.

Step 2 is buying a hardware wallet and rotating the safe signer with it for much safer holding

Once you're there, you can start considering a 1/2 with a second hw or with an old phone you have in your drawer that you've factory reset and will use only for that. You keep it out of easy reach; it's your insurance if something bad happens to your main signer.

Then maybe a 2/3 and the nerdy stuff; you can always do "better," but the foundation of all that is getting your first safe deployed and climbing from there.

Do it now; it's not hard, it's worth it.

text:
My biggest takeaways from @illscience:

1. Company building will now be creating a series of loops. A coding loop turns a bug report into a fix and a low-risk production release in five minutes. Anish expects similar loops to spread from individuals to functions, business units, and eventually large parts of a company—from growth experiments to sales demos to legal and support. The key is to figure out what the agent doesn’t know and give it that context so it can complete the loop.

2. Moats are discovered, not designed. Anish uses Cursor as an example: it began as a high-engagement DAU product, then captured reasoning traces and trained its own models over time. A founder does not need a fully formed moat story on day one if the product has momentum, craft, and growing engagement. The classic moats—like network effects, scale advantages, brand, and proprietary data—still matter, but the small product decisions that create them often become visible only after the product is in the world.

3. We appear to be on the slow takeoff timeline. The case for fast takeoff always follows the same structure: everything up until now is OK, then something no one can articulate happens, then runaway acceleration. Anish doesn’t buy it. Model progress is real and faster than ever, but most problems aren’t intelligence-bound. A data center of PhDs doesn’t exponentially improve pizza supply chains.

4. The “permanent underclass” fears are a Silicon Valley dark fantasy. By almost every empirical measure, things have never been more distributed or opportunity-rich. Job postings for radiologists and programmers are at historic highs, despite years of “they’re cooked” predictions. And within the AI stack itself, rather than one winner-take-all platform, there are 20 credible players at every layer.

5. The biggest opportunity in consumer AI right now is “/loop make me happier” (not “/loop make me more productive”). Most people want to spend time, not save it. The biggest products in the world are entertainment and social, not productivity tools. Anish sees a spiritual hunger, particularly outside major urban centers where cultural institutions have thinned out. The opportunity: How do we feel more connected, more loved? How do we have fun? “We built a technology that extends our intellect and nothing to extend our soul.”

6. Three things have held consumer AI back, and all three are now improving. First, model costs were too high for free-to-use consumer products. Second, chat is a high-agency interface that works for Elon and Sam but not for the average consumer, who needs something between chat and TikTok. Third, the technology has been aimed almost entirely at productivity rather than connection and entertainment. The consumer moment is coming; Anish puts us at iPhone 2010, pre-Airbnb, pre-WhatsApp, pre-Uber.

7. Humans will remain critical for identifying the next opportunity. Agents are excellent at climbing to a local maximum, but then they plateau. They aren’t great at picking which hill to climb next. That’s where humans come in. Anish illustrates this with a chart he uses in conversations: agents hill-climb, then a human steps in to set the direction for the next climb, and the cycle repeats.

8. The most important attribute for teams is now ambition. Three years ago, Anish and his colleagues would pass on companies that seemed too crazy or complex. Today the opposite is true: an idea that’s too small isn’t worth engaging with. The firm’s internal posture with every founder: “We’re here to help you build the strongest form of your vision.”

9. There’s a big opportunity in creating very expensive consumer software. The old wisdom was that consumer products have to be free. Anish is taking the opposite position—that consumer discretionary spend is entirely up for grabs, and price is a measure of product-market fit. His product exercise for founders: what would the Birkin bag version of your product, at $1,000 or $10,000 a month, have to do to justify that price?

10. Become a model sommelier. Models are not interchangeable; Anish experiences different models as suited to different kinds of work. His way to learn their shape is to build something with every release, ideally using one or two low-stakes projects as a recurring test bed. His minimum heuristic is to ship once a week.

text:
I want to close my chapter, for now, on the EIP-8363 analysis. After having a few more calls with people who are for- and against- issuance reduction (stakers, founders, DeFi people, and regular Ethereum holders) - here is a subjective view on the matter. I think it has some new aspects I didn't see much of before (💡)

- TLDR 1: I don't think this should go through right now. The proposal is raw and the arguments are still weak. It's weird to say this because it has been in the works for five years on and off, but it still doesn't make sense. I respect the authors who put time and effort into this, but after looking into it and having so many conversations across the space - it doesn't check out.
- TLDR 2: Neither side should be talking about anyone being "captured." You cannot say that core devs living and breathing the network are captured. No, they care about it and are involved. That is good! Similarly, you cannot say DeFi founders or the staking companies are captured. These people own the asset and are economically interested in having it grow. We have to put those arguments aside - it is just cheap talk.
- TLDR 3: Regarding the process: whether now or later, issuance policy shouldn't just go through a normal network upgrade process. It's not just about repricing or a minor technical tweak; this is way too big to be considered in that fashion. Maybe it could work within the existing process, but only if the opinions of founders and other stakeholders were respected a bit more, rather than just discarding them all as being captured.

Now to the arguments 🦞

I haven't really strayed from what I wrote a few weeks ago (tweet below). As a shorter summary, the argument for reduction falls through three main holes.

1. First, there is this allegiance to a "no inflation" economy perception: the idea that inflation is inherently bad, that (over)paying for something is bad, and that there is just too much of something. That mindset is not correct. In the modern economic world, since we stopped making money only from growing potatoes, it doesn't make sense. The belief that this will somehow make the Ethereum price moon, or that there is too much ETH being dumped on the market, is nonsense. It's one of the least inflating assets.

💡 You have to consider your broader goals. Your issuance strategy should reflect your general adoption strategy. If you think ETH is just an asset, money, a unit of account, or whatever narrative you want to come up with - like the "pet rock" meme Bitcoin style - fine. It's not bad, and it's okay to say that. But then the general adoption strategy should reflect it. It should just be marketing a hard asset, not worry about devs, open-source or anything creative. It's just digital gold, go to hard money conferences and enjoy.

However, if you see Ethereum as a World Computer, as a way to build different use cases, as an "infinite garden" for lack of a better phrase, as a platform - then there is no point in cutting the issuance. Currently, issuance creates different opportunities and products on this platform. EVEN IF you think it's a subsidy, then what? Platforms have subsidies. Why tamper with it if you have no definite alternative. These subsidies worked, they continue working and getting attention, and the platform is winning as a result of that (adoption, liquidity, trust, security, etc.)

If you offboard one big user segment from your marketplace, what's your alternative? Because you are then killing some of the plants in your garden that you've previously incentivized. It's not a weed, and presenting it as a weed is incorrect because nothing shows that's the case.

2. Second, the argument falls through on all the talk about the staking ratio, staking centralization, supply capture, solo stakers, inability to pass slashing, and so on. These are generally good discussions to have, but the suggested proposal does not fix those 🚫

💡 Take the part about slashing and forks, for example. All of these fancy ideas of how staker behavior is going to play out aren't really realistic. Nobody writes about which network - in terms of a slashing event or a fork - USDC, USDT, and centralized issuers would actually consider and back. 

Important factors affecting network resilience should be solved, but this proposal does not solve them. It does not improve conditions for solo stakers. The argument that the staking distribution will get worse if we continue - is also unproven. There is no proper distinction made between "good" LSTs and "bad" LSTs (if you want to think this way). If you believe that Binance and Coinbase staking shouldn't be increasing as much, that's a different discussion. A blanket cut wouldn't kill them as much as it would kill some LSTs that are actually favorable to the development of the core network. I'm not against an issuance reduction as a move potentially; I'm against how it is being argued, and that it's being argued in a weak way .

3. Third, the mechanics of yield are now being accepted as an asset in DeFi protocols (stETH over raw ETH, for example). These are interesting opportunities to consider, but thinking you can mess with this in isolation while killing what exists now isn't cool. Having Ethereum's economic policy be more set in stone is far more important to current participants than just trying out stuff by breaking an ecosystem that exists today.

💡 If institutions and such players appreciate ETH as an asset and engage with real use cases, do not stop them by trying to hypothetically make other use cases possible. They appreciate the current staking rate and have built strategies around it. 

If the proposal would solve security or network resilience while causing some pain in the short term, that would be acceptable. But as I've established, the arguments presented are weak and in many cases incorrect, so it doesn't even solve the purpose.

-----

You have to decide what you actually want to happen:

- Do you want to play trader and mess around with the ETH price by thinking less inflation is better
- Or do you want to solve network resilience and make it uncapturable?

You have to answer one of these questions. Right now, they are all packaged together. As a result, it's a mess, because it's not solving a problem that is explained - or it's solving a problem that is not proven to exist. 

Sorry 8363, but hope no.

As AI changes the speed and accessibility of vulnerability research, responsible disclosure has never been more important.

We’re working alongside researchers and other industry leaders to support coordinated disclosure, responsible communication, and sufficient time for vulnerabilities to be fixed before they are made public. 🤝

Protecting users must remain the priority.
author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
📌 AI made finding bugs cheap, but it didn’t make responsible disclosure optional.

Finding and exploiting vulnerabilities has never been easier. A few hours of prompting now does what used to take a skilled researcher weeks. Unfortunately, defenders no longer enjoy the asymmetry they relied on. Security is still a cat-and-mouse game, but with many more cats, the user suffers.

Which is exactly why the process around disclosure matters more than ever.

How it works, and it is not complicated:
➤ A researcher finds a bug and contacts the vendor privately.
➤ The vendor reproduces, acknowledges, and both sides agree on a timeline. 90 days is the common default, more or less depending on severity, capacity to fix...
➤ During that window both sides keep it secret while the vendor fixes and ships.
➤ Once users are protected, both sides publish. The ecosystem learns. The researcher usually gets paid.

The issue now is the barrier is so low that anyone can surface a finding with no security background, and some skip straight to the audience:

❗Presenting a reproduction of an already-fixed bug as a live compromise.
❗Full disclosure of a bug that is not fixed yet.
❗"Critical vulnerability found" teasers, dripping details for engagement.

Call it what it is: attention farming with someone else's risk. When the bug sits between a user and their funds, this is reckless. Especially in crypto, where there is no chargeback. But the damage doesn't require live funds to be at stake. Manufactured panic causes harm of its own, because it drives people away from self-custody, and that damages the whole ecosystem.

So I have three asks:

1️⃣ For users: software and hardware have bugs, always. The single most effective thing you can do is stay updated and follow basic security hygiene. That has never mattered more than today. The time between releases and malicious actors exploiting the vulnerabilities have shrunk dramatically due to LLMs and that one can't afford to be passive and postpone security updates any more

2️⃣ For new researchers with a fresh model and a real, validated finding: welcome, we need you. Use the vendor's disclosure process. That is not bureaucracy. It is the difference between making the ecosystem safer and putting users in the crosshairs for a few likes. Remember that security communication must be accurate and proportionate. State the severity, affected versions, and fix status in the first sentence, not the tenth.

3️⃣ And to everyone building in this industry, vendors and researchers alike: let's make coordinated disclosure the norm we defend out loud, not the fine print. Reward the researchers who do it right. Refuse to amplify the ones who trade user safety for reach. This is how we win, together.

Some of the actors already support the initiative. @Ledger  @Trezor  @FoundationHQ  @AnchorWatch  @_SEAL_Org  and others

Spread the message.

text:
Ever since fomo blew up, its top traders became some of the most tracked wallets in crypto. And with all that attention, scammers got creative and exploited a gap in how Relay swaps work.

Fomo, like plenty of other multichain apps, routes EVM trades from Solana through Relay. The buy happens on Solana, the tokens arrive on an EVM address, and since the sender and receiver sit on different chains, there's no direct way to verify they belong to the same trader. Tokens just land in a wallet, and trackers call it a buy.

So scammers started faking buys from the biggest wallets. Every tracker showed them as real. Alerts fired, people followed the wallets they trust, and minutes later the tokens rugged.

If you were copytrading those wallets on Robinhood or Base without platform filters, your agent was buying the rugs for you.

This was the biggest data integrity problem in EVM wallet tracking, and it was making people lose money.

So we took it into our own hands and developed a fix for it. Cielo now catches spoofed Relay fills and kills them before they reach you. Not your feed, not your alerts, not your copy trade agents.

Out of the first 13,437 fills it checked, it dropped 510 fake buys before they reached anyone.

On Cielo, what you see is what happened.

StonkFun is the only platform on @solana that allows custom pairings, and coins traded against the pairs

It mean's that you can tax users trades across any pool not just a single pool owned by the platform, the only way to have rewards for coins trading at higher market caps is through transfer tax as you cannot be undercut on LP's

text:
Vitalik just shared another update on Frame Transactions (EIP-8141), and this is one of those Ethereum changes that looks small on the surface but could have huge consequences.

The basic idea is pretty interesting.

Instead of treating a transaction as one rigid object, Ethereum can break it into programmable frames.

That opens the door to things like..
- paying gas with something other than ETH
- sponsored transactions
- smarter wallet validation
- batching multiple actions atomically
- key rotation and recovery
- different signature schemes
- eventually making transaction processing much easier to parallelize

The bigger part for me is the separation between what a transaction wants to do and what needs to be verified before it can happen.

That could give Ethereum a much cleaner foundation for scaling.

And this isn't just another wallet abstraction layer sitting on top of Ethereum.

The goal with EIP-8141 is to push account abstraction much closer to the protocol itself.

If this lands as planned, the wallet experience developers build in a few years could look very different from today's MetaMask + approvals + ETH-for-gas workflow.

Ethereum's transaction model is getting a pretty serious redesign.

And honestly, this is the kind of infrastructure change I’m much more interested in than another L2 TPS announcement.

Lucas co-founded a hedge fund at 20 that Digital Currency Group acquired a year later, then walked away from that exit to build a firm that now sits second only to Hyperliquid in open interest and daily volume.

His argument: crypto rebuilt exchanges before it built brokers, and that architectural gap is what's holding on-chain trading back.

We talk about:
- Why order books work for a handful of liquid assets like BTC and $ETH but break once you try to list hundreds of markets
- How Variational aggregates liquidity straight from traditional finance instead of rebuilding 40 years of market depth from scratch
- Why Variational charges zero fees by keeping the market-maker spread inside the platform
- The architectural difference between Variational's RFQ, broker-like model and Hyperliquid's order book
- How Variational's daily volume went from $1 million to over $100 million within months of launch
- What swaps offer that perps can't - a flat, predictable carry cost instead of a funding rate that can spike overnight
- Why he raised $50 million in May specifically to get taken seriously by trad-fi institutions
- The two kinds of businesses he wants competed into extinction: high-fee brokers and predatory market makers

And much more...

Podcast out this week!

text:
程序员做产品的死循环：

找需求→ 写代码 → 做产品 →没流量 → 难受→ 下一个产品 → 一直循环

问题不是做什么产品，而是没有研究清楚流量从哪来

我以前调研一个竞品，要把官网、Similarweb、SEO、外链、Reddit、X、YouTube 挨个扒一遍，再拼出它真正的增长方式，至少一周。

最近我发现 AIsa 接入了 Similarweb 官方的 V5 API，和 RapidAPI 上常见的第三方爬虫接口不太一样，数据来源更稳定，更新也更及时。

目前能把 Similarweb 直接接进 Agent workflow 里跑的，我只找到这一家。

所以这次，我直接把一个竞品网址交给接入 AIsa 的 Agent，半小时拿到一份完整的增长审计报告。几个发现完全出乎我的意料：

* 近 6 个月约 49% 的流量来自自然搜索，看起来很热闹的社媒实际只贡献约 4%
* 外链近 4,000 条，但接近六成集中在两个合作站的站级链接上，数字有明显水分
* 官方社媒账号几乎没量，第三方创作者的教程反而更有效
* GEO 测试里，它占住了一个 AI 搜索心智，另一个重要场景完全缺席——那就是机会

如果只看它天天发什么，我大概率会得出“该去做短视频、全平台日更”的错误结论。真实数据给出的答案是：先做高意图关键词的承接页面，再用创作者和外链放大。

AIsa 解决的就是 Agent 缺数据这件事：一个 Key，按量计费，让 Agent 直接调用 Similarweb 官方 API、SEO、外链、社媒和 GEO 数据——不是爬虫和镜像站的数据，是以前只有企业订阅才用得起的那种。

它不能保证产品成功。但它能让你在写第一行代码之前，先用真实数据排除错误方向：这个需求值不值得做，做出来第一批流量去哪找。

对独立开发者来说，省下的不只是一周调研时间，而是几周做错产品的成本。

如果你手上正好有一个想做的方向，或者想拆一个竞品的流量到底从哪来，可以直接试试，跑一份自己的报告：
https://t.co/ALjwzZhc76

text:
Astra is an incredible world builder and explorer, and can invent its own scientific instruments - crossing a game-changing threshold: it turned a few images of a biological microstructure into a full-blown metamaterials lab, then used its own creation to discover a design with ~2.1x the reference work-to-failure/peak-strength ratio. Metamaterials are some of the most complex materials we can engineer. Their properties come from deep architectural complexity - struts, cells, disorder, and hierarchy arranged across multiple length scales determine how the material deforms, absorbs energy, and fails. Designing them means searching a geometric space far too large for "intuition" alone. In this experiment we handed an AI agent that entire problem end-to-end, from image, to simulating the physics, to fabrication-ready geometry.

We started with an image of hierarchical, biological architecture; Astra then built a complete 3D metamaterial studio: editable geometries, multiple levels of hierarchy, disorder, gradients, a complete physics simulator featuring linear and nonlinear material responses, deformation and fracture experiments (with replay), and STL export for 3D printing.

Then we asked the agent to use the app it created to search for a high work-to-failure/peak-strength ratio. Among the candidates, the leading design reached approximately 2.1x the reference ratio. 

The movie follows the structures through deformation and fracture, connects their designs to the property map, and shows the finalist assembled geometrically into a connected multi-scale material.

Image ➡️ executable world ➡️ experiments ➡️ design search ➡️ candidate discovery ➡️ geometry for fabrication ➡️ manufacturing

Want to combine uAgents + @solana  transactions? Build this 3-Agent flow.

PlayerAgent

→ Loads its Solana wallet
→ Sends an `escrowRequest`

ChallengerAgent

→ Does the same from a second wallet

EscrowAgent

→ Receives both requests
→ Pulls live BTC price data
→ Determines the winner
→ Transfers the payout
→ Messages both Agents with the result

All three register through https://t.co/jQHISjPvoi’s Almanac, communicate through typed uAgent messages and execute transactions on Solana Devnet.

The example uses three specialised Agents instead of stuffing wallet management, external data, decision logic and settlement into one process.

Run it on Devnet first:

text:
I love these 4 product principles from @suekhim because they're great parenting advice too:

1. Never tell the learner the answer

It’s tempting to step in when your child gets stuck. But even a good explanation can do the thinking for them. Try asking, “What have you tried?” or “What could you try next?” Give them a chance to work it out.

2. Honor their thinking

A wrong answer can reveal something your child understood correctly. Ask how they got there before correcting them. You’ll learn more about what they’re missing, and they’ll see that their reasoning matters.

3. Don’t say “no worries” when they get something wrong

We want to reassure our kids, but brushing off a mistake can dismiss the effort and frustration behind it. Acknowledge that the problem is hard, then help them find a next step they can take themselves.

4. Confirm progress, don’t explain it

When your child discovers something, resist finishing the thought for them. Ask, “What does that tell you?” Let them put the insight into their own words and decide what to do next.

I’ll add one more:

5. Encourage your kids to express their creativity with AI

My 8-year-old can now build games in ChatGPT by herself. We also create funny videos and songs in Gemini as a family activity. Next, I’m going to show her how to create Blender models. Give kids room to experiment, and they’ll surprise you with what they create.

📌 Watch the full episode: https://t.co/jzogacrhiK

“Cheating and explaining the answer [to your child] are closer than you’d think.”

→ Why better grades don’t always mean more learning

on RH RWAs are all a lil volatile, and are being paired with memes that are super volatile, while all the pools for them have high fees

its only natural and expected for a new medium of exchange to develop to pair with ALL the RWAs to eat up all the fees and get routed through regularly

the game is to grow liquidity enough in pairs with that new MOE that it then begets more volume, that then begets more fees, that then creates more liquidity through fees being used to shure up the pools (and to give back to holders via distributions of RWAs/buybacks).

it's a flywheel (shoot me, but it is)

SHROOM is the category leader. 

It has nothing special about it in terms of tech moat, other than it has that je ne sais quoi to become the breakout token for this purpose, and a cracked thoughtful dev team who are tweaking things to max out the fee capture/liquidity expansion over time. 

buying SHROOM is a bet on it being the new robinhood 'liquidity layer' token, and it having a pareto distribution (capture 80% of the market whilst there's a longtail of smaller tokens trying the same thing) by being the first mover to reach escape velocity.

我基于 @BNBCHAIN  ，实现了历史上第一次在L1主网上跑Linux。这是第一个每条指令都由 L1 主网交易执行、全部状态都存在 L1 上的 Linux。
此前这个领域公认的先行者是 Cartesi：它的 RISC-V 虚拟机能启动完整的 Linux，但 Linux 是在链下节点上跑的，以太坊 L1 只负责结算，只有当参与者对结果有争议时，才把争议的那一步拿到链上重算。正常情况下，L1 从头到尾没有执行过一条 Linux 指令。它是 L2 框架，靠欺诈证明和至少一个诚实的挑战者。
而TapeOut做的是真正的，Linux 的每一条指令都在 BNBChain 主网的交易里由验证者算出来，并且拥有32 个寄存器、全部 CSR以及16 MB 内存的每一页都在BNBChain主网上，没有任何链下执行。也就是说Cartesi 上让 L1 能验证 Linux，我们让BNBChain 真实的链上运行完整的 Linux。
它是由TapeOut 的电路+容器组成，第一次组成了一台完整的链上计算机。一片电路（#4246）开通了容器，容器成了这台机器的主人，谁持有这片电路的 NFT，谁就是它的管理员。CPU 是一个 RISC-V 元件，内存是 16 MB、按 1 KB 分页的 16,384 个页合约，写时复制。主板合约用交易跑指令，把改过的内存页写回链上，把串口输出发成事件。
装的是 kernelorg 主线 Linux 6.5.12，它从复位向量 0x80000000 上电，在主网上安拍跑完整个内核启动，直到 root 登录：一共44,988 拍，9,000 余笔交易（花了我好多bnb啊，有点肉疼，另外我还找bnbchain的小伙伴申请了10个tBNB做的测试网测试，感谢 @0xSandy1913 帮助协调测试网的tBNB）。
另外呢，任何人都可以用它。打开 https://t.co/SpeMEejeFq，像用真实终端一样直接敲命令：uname -a 会告诉你这是 riscv32 上的 Linux 6.5.12；factor 1000000007 在链上做一次质因数分解；echo 写一个文件，这个文件就住在主网上某一页合约的字节码里，你能在 BscScan 上看见它，谁使用谁自己付 gas（我可支付不起这么多人测试，哈哈）。

这件事说明： @BNBCHAIN  不只是一个公共账本，它可以基于TapeOut承载可验证的生产工具，一台计算机是所有生产工具的底座。

接下来：用门级 RISC-V 核做这台机器的裁判，让每一条指令都有晶体管级的定义；让 Linux 能直接读链上数据；让更多电路拥有自己的不同类型的机器。BNB Chain 的延展性比大多数人想象的大得多，TapeOut在为此全力以赴。

text:
AGI is already here. 

A simple contemplation on who wins and what happens to you and me. 

A few pointers: 

> The next phase is for frontier labs to move into capturing verticals. Ex. Scenario: Anthropic discovering drugs, manufacturing them, running hospitals. Ultimately, only the highest bidder gets access to cures and treatment. 

> The level of access to intelligence and compute can create an uneven playing field at scale. Jane Street is a great example of this. Imagine Jane Street across industries. We may be 1 Year away from that. May not fit into the academic definition of AGI. But at this level, implications are pretty worrisome. 

> This also leads to concentration of intelligence. The gap between countries, governments, and labs is now determined by compute and how much intelligence it can accumulate. And the hard truth is, this compounds. China and the US are leading this. China will win eventually. 

> The impact on the labor market will be devastating. It is entirely possible to bring robot labor below the cost of human labor. Most developed countries will have to choose. A robot that can dance can also perform open-heart surgery. You just need to change the software. 

> AI + hardware have a power to obliterate human labor in many ways. We are pretty close. 

> Now imagine what happens when cost advantages to produce something are dusted. All economic theories are for a toss. 

> Also, the work itself is getting automated. Not tasks, but the full production cycle. Labor advantage and arbitrage will be gone. What will matter is capital to access the intelligence. 

So what matters now? 

The only question we should all be focusing on from every perspective is: what is scarce in the postAGI economy? 

The answer to this determines what happens to you and me.

text:
Grants were always meant to be a means to an end — advances in the field, new technologies, drugs that reach patients. Somewhere along the way, they became the end itself. You’d hear administrators Freudian-slip into calling federal grants “revenue,” and it never sat right with scientists who actually wanted impact. The metric became the target. One grant alone could find a new treatment (eg, itch), while 4 grants can go nowhere. Guess who gets the credit in this kind of system? 

AI is calling that bluff, fast.

I now write grants — with my own data, my own reasoning — in about 10 minutes. The same proposals used to take me four weeks. Not because the science changed. Because the four weeks was never where the science lived. It was formatting, phrasing, restructuring the same idea, making sure you cite the right people, for the fifth time to fit a template. Pure overhead, dressed up as rigor.

The judgment was always mine. The data was hard-earned. The prose was just the toll charged to have it heard.

If a system built its entire notion of prestige and gatekeeping around who could produce that document — rather than who had the idea — then AI collapsing the cost of the document to near zero doesn’t just speed things up. It exposes what the document was actually measuring, which was never quite the science.

If someone is able to write an amazing grant, using my publicly available data, with AI, execute it, and deliver a better therapy without me, my patients would be just as happy. So would I.
author: jamessinka
quoted_text:
I asked Astra to look through my published science, identify new directions, and draft five NIH R01 proposals -- the multiyear, $1M-$2M grants that support much of academic biomedical science.

In about one hour, using roughly $20 in compute, it produced entirely reasonable proposals. They were well grounded in my work and structured to appeal to study section reviewers. They looked very similar to what I would write if my goal were to get another grant.

Astra reproduced that logic well. It turned existing work into questions, hypotheses, and experiments that would look familiar and defensible to a study section.

The output was immediately recognizable as the work of an experienced academic scientist. If AGI means being able to produce the work of highly trained professionals, this is a clear concrete example. It produced something academic scientists spend a great deal of time doing.

Academic medical centers build careers, laboratories, and their finances around this process. Scientists spend years writing these proposals as the next fundable extension of their work.

text:
GenLayer CEO Albert Castellana on why AI agents transacting at machine speed need their own legal system

"The problem is that these AIs, they're gonna start to be transacting with each other at a speed that is insane. I think a few years from now, five, ten years from now, pretty much all commerce is gonna be done by agents of different sorts."

"When that happens, I can't imagine how they can coexist if there's no sort of legal system between them. Because where are they living? You don't know where my AI agent is living. Do I even know what it is? Is it right here, or is it in some Amazon Web Services or whatever?"

"These agents are gonna be cheating. They're gonna be cutting corners. Gonna be smart as hell. They're gonna be moving super fast. It's gonna be very, very hard to see what they're doing. How do they trust each other if they don't even have a legal system? Because the legal system takes years and hundreds of thousands of dollars to resolve a small claim. That's why we're building this court of the internet."

Bitcoin-Gold Correlation Hits Nine-Year High as Nasdaq Link Falls to One-Year Low  

According to Protos, Bitcoin’s 90-day correlation with gold has risen to 0.56, its highest level since most data providers began tracking the metric in 2017 and above the previous peak of around 0.50 in November 2020. Meanwhile, its 90-day correlation with the Nasdaq 100 has fallen to roughly 0.30, a one-year low. On a 30-day basis, BTC’s correlation with gold has climbed to 0.72, versus just 0.22 with the Nasdaq Composite, reinforcing the renewed “digital gold” narrative amid August’s debasement trade.

text:
For years, the @DonjonLedger has found vulnerabilities across the ecosystem, and disclosed every one of them the right way: privately, patched, then published.

Today that standard becomes a shared industry commitment, alongside @Trezor, @FoundationHQ, @AnchorWatch and @_SEAL_Org.

Responsible disclosure protects users. Attention farming doesn't. 👇
author: P3b7_
quoted_text:
📌 AI made finding bugs cheap, but it didn’t make responsible disclosure optional.

Finding and exploiting vulnerabilities has never been easier. A few hours of prompting now does what used to take a skilled researcher weeks. Unfortunately, defenders no longer enjoy the asymmetry they relied on. Security is still a cat-and-mouse game, but with many more cats, the user suffers.

Which is exactly why the process around disclosure matters more than ever.

How it works, and it is not complicated:
➤ A researcher finds a bug and contacts the vendor privately.
➤ The vendor reproduces, acknowledges, and both sides agree on a timeline. 90 days is the common default, more or less depending on severity, capacity to fix...
➤ During that window both sides keep it secret while the vendor fixes and ships.
➤ Once users are protected, both sides publish. The ecosystem learns. The researcher usually gets paid.

The issue now is the barrier is so low that anyone can surface a finding with no security background, and some skip straight to the audience:

❗Presenting a reproduction of an already-fixed bug as a live compromise.
❗Full disclosure of a bug that is not fixed yet.
❗"Critical vulnerability found" teasers, dripping details for engagement.

Call it what it is: attention farming with someone else's risk. When the bug sits between a user and their funds, this is reckless. Especially in crypto, where there is no chargeback. But the damage doesn't require live funds to be at stake. Manufactured panic causes harm of its own, because it drives people away from self-custody, and that damages the whole ecosystem.

So I have three asks:

1️⃣ For users: software and hardware have bugs, always. The single most effective thing you can do is stay updated and follow basic security hygiene. That has never mattered more than today. The time between releases and malicious actors exploiting the vulnerabilities have shrunk dramatically due to LLMs and that one can't afford to be passive and postpone security updates any more

2️⃣ For new researchers with a fresh model and a real, validated finding: welcome, we need you. Use the vendor's disclosure process. That is not bureaucracy. It is the difference between making the ecosystem safer and putting users in the crosshairs for a few likes. Remember that security communication must be accurate and proportionate. State the severity, affected versions, and fix status in the first sentence, not the tenth.

3️⃣ And to everyone building in this industry, vendors and researchers alike: let's make coordinated disclosure the norm we defend out loud, not the fine print. Reward the researchers who do it right. Refuse to amplify the ones who trade user safety for reach. This is how we win, together.

Some of the actors already support the initiative. @Ledger  @Trezor  @FoundationHQ  @AnchorWatch  @_SEAL_Org  and others

Spread the message.

text:
Coinbase's Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad on how embracing crypto helped Trump win over low-propensity voters

"If I could kind of go down a rabbit hole, which I think is really interesting, one of the big reasons Donald Trump won in the 2024 cycle is that he and his team had an extremely sophisticated strategy built around what they call low-propensity voters. So these are people who the Trump team thought they could get to turn out and vote, even though it was constituencies that normally don't show up to vote, don't normally turn out and don't normally vote Republican."

"And yet Trump and his team decided to organize a lot of the campaign around the low-propensity voter. And so he went out and said no tax on tipped wages, no tax on overtime, and then he added crypto to that issue. In other words, embracing the crypto sector."

"That kind of approach ultimately got Donald Trump a huge sub-segment of voters who most experts thought were not gettable."
