author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
A fantastic future for humanity - the case for e/acc

tl;dr: Dreaming of the most fantastic future possible for humanity: efficient social co-ordination, preservation of Earth's biosphere and amplified theoretical astrophysics research. An essay I wrote in Jan 2021..

The events of 2020 have taught us one thing: we need more efficient social co-ordination across the planet. A pandemic is but one of the existential challenges we could have and would face in the future. There are many more ahead. Not only do we have to be prepared for them structurally, but also think beyond, the furthest anyone has ever done and set outrageous goals for us. This essay is an exercise in that.

Intelligent life must be abundant in the universe

For life to emerge on any planet, an extraordinary number of things have to happen just right. From there on, for intelligent life to emerge, the chances are still astronomically lower. However improbable that event is, due to the simple big-ness of the universe, the probability for there to be an extraordinary large number of planets with intelligent life is really high.

Based on astronomer Frank Drake’s equation, in our galaxy alone, with 200 billion stars, there could be 200,000 stars with planets orbiting them which could have intelligent life. And then there are hundreds of billions of galaxies in the universe. Surely, there must be or have been many, many advanced alien civilizations which not only could detect others, but progressed to the point they could travel across the galaxy.

But, where is everybody ?

The math around intelligent life to exist focuses around conditions on a planet in general. It doesn’t account for point-in-time: Intelligent life on all these planets existing at different times during the life of the universe so far.

While on Earth we have been scanning out to 100 light-years of our planet for signs of such life, we have not been able to detect it.

For basic, biological life there are many expeditions planned during the 2020s which could confirm for us the presence of at least some life on a planet other than Earth. The James Webb telescope, scheduled for launch by NASA in late 2021, will start providing that insight. For eg, TRAPPIST-1 system has multiple Earth-like planets and if there are life signatures emanating from there, this telescope would be able to provide that data. It would be a breakthrough moment for humanity to discover basic biological life beyond Earth. Religion and society operating structure would not take that news kindly.

But, it shouldn’t surprise us. A 100 years ago, we believed there was only 1 galaxy, until Hubble showed otherwise. A long time ago, we believed Earth was the center of the universe, and the Sun revolved around it. As science and technology have progressed, we have learnt repeatedly that we are not special but part of a recurring pattern which occurs elsewhere in the universe again and again. Everything except intelligent life, so far.

It’s possible every intelligent civilization reaches a point where it invents a technology which destroys it, and others have, while we haven’t. This is a case made by Nick Bostrom, who terms it “The Great Filter“. It either lies behind us, or ahead of us. We don’t know for sure where on that spectrum we are at currently.

Or, it is possible for other intelligent civilizations we are not intelligent enough as yet so they see little value in initiating contact with us.

Or, perhaps we need even more breakthroughs in astrophysics and higher dimensions to view everything from a different level altogether in order to discover civilizations which either exist currently or have existed in the past.

The most conservative assumption here is that we are the only intelligent life form which has ever evolved anywhere, at anytime in the universe. We start with this, until proven wrong. Here’s why: we need to value what we have immensely.

Protecting Earth’s biosphere by any means necessary

In a fundamentally hostile universe, to be on this spinning and traveling spaceship around a star, for life to exist here, and advance to the point where we have, that’s a remarkable turn of events! For every generation which follows, it becomes progressively more critical to not screw this up, assuming, what if this is the only and the best shot there has been for intelligent life at any point in the universe’s history.

How to approach it ?

We have to overwhelmingly prioritize protection against existential threats to life on Earth. We have to preserve our biosphere and conditions necessary for life to sustain and thrive. This means acting on multiple fronts against multiple threats. Toby Ord’s book The Precipice: Existential Risk and The Future of Humanity provides a probabilistic estimate of each of these occurring as an existential threat to life on Earth over the next 100 years:

Asteroids or comet impact: 1 in a million

Stellar explosion: 1 in a billion

Supervolcano eruptions on Earth: 1 in 10,000Total natural risk: 1 in 10,000

Naturally arising pandemics: 1 in 10,000

Engineered pandemics: 1 in 30 (this book came out before the COVID-19 pandemic..)

Climate change and other environmental damage: 1 in 1,000

Nuclear war: 1 in 1,000

Mis-aligned Artificial General Intelligence: 1 in 10

Unforeseen anthropogenic risks: 1 in 30

Total anthropogenic risk: 1 in 6

Total existential risk: 1 in 6

What else is more important than assessing and dealing with each one of these with the best resources we can marshal together ? Each one of these would require tens of billions of $ in investment.

We are going to need a lot more focused billionaires, governmental and non-governmental entities which pick one of these problems and go at it. No one entity can deal with all of it.

Our world will simply require an extraordinary level of preparation, co-ordination and prevention for humanity to still be around a 100 years from now.

Next 100 years: 2021 to 2121

For the next 100 years, the key priority for us is two-folds:
• Increase global scientific education and knowledge
• Massively efficient planetary co-ordination

If we do this, then we can manage challenges like pandemics, climate change, and controlling the weather to benefit humanity and other life forms. We can also pool resources, and amplify efforts even further against other natural threats in the universe. Would it not be fantastic for humanity if the global space agencies operate as one integrated unit, looking across 100s of years, instead of subject to short-term political outlooks and budgets ?

Increasing prosperity, education, economic empowerment - providing a good life to everybody is key to reaching an equilibrium state in the world where we can think and look at bigger issues at play in the universe, instead of being caught up by surprise from them.
Image

2121 to 3021

If we have made sufficient protections for our biosphere and provided a brilliant life to every being on this planet - why do we need to continue to push space exploration and astrophysics research beyond tickling our curiosity ?

It’s because every intelligent civilization in the universe would have either understood the creation of the universe and is able to travel across galaxies using higher dimensions, or, if not, then is seeking to do that.

All it would take it is one bad apple to travel to Earth. If this sounds a lot like the need for an Avenger’s Initiative, it is. But, we don’t have a handful of superheroes, we need to operate and plan for it 1000s of years in advance, at Earth-scale, to be in a position where we can defend Earth from any and all threats in the universe, whether natural or from a hostile alien intelligent life form.

Also, if we are able to figure it out, then as we expand our footprint across the galaxy, we can help other civilizations and life forms. What makes us human is our inquisitiveness and our ability to be social, to be kind to others. Would we hold our gifts to ourselves’ ?

To be at and to bring peace, we have to hold a position of power.

Million Einsteins

How remarkable would it be if ~0.01% of humanity is an extremely gifted and driven astrophysics researcher or pushing the boundaries of space exploration ? Can we build a system where we are able to identify, nurture and empower such individuals at a large scale ?

Albert Einstein worked as a patent clerk, where one of his key motivations was money earned from astrophysics-related prizes, so that he could support his family with two young kids.

This is not something which one can ask the society to do because it is the good thing over a long enough period. It would happen naturally if the incentives are lined up appropriately.

Over a long enough period, we absolutely and critically need astrophysics breakthroughs. We need to be able to travel across the galaxy, which will simply not happen based on our current known principles, but new ones which we need to discover.

It is possible a 1000 years from now we live in a world where we have come across multiple intelligent alien civilizations. It is better if we do it on our terms.

Next 1000s of Years

We won’t know in our lifetimes, but we can take comfort in the fact that sometime in humanity’s future we would have figured out the origins of the universe. During this period we have become an active galactic civilization, harnessing the power of not only our sun but of other stars in the Milky Way galaxy, and having understood the higher dimensions, are able to travel using them.

We are using our knowledge to make life better for all alien civilizations out there. It is, simply, the human thing to do.

The Need for an “Astro Valley”

We have seen the power of dense information and collaboration networks like Silicon Valley, Wall Street and Hollywood which has built our society as we know it. People of similar backgrounds and ambition are attracted to the same area, where they collaborate and work across a range of functions to produce marvellous work. Their incentives align. New models emerge which fund experimentation.

That’s what we need for astrophysics and space exploration. It’s not a few people, or a few companies which push humanity forward from here on, but a larger, denser group of connected people. Working in this field needs to be the most lucrative thing to do from an economic perspective as well, so that smartest people on the planet don’t have to choose.

With the right product, the “Astro Valley“ exists online, enabling wider participation across the world so that people don’t have to uproot their families to do what’s needed for humanity over the next 100s to 1000s of years.

Let’s Go!

Let this not be an academic exercise. We are all biological beings, with limited time on the planet, and whatever we can do across the below dimensions helps in the longer run:

1] Increasing efficient and useful social co-ordination amongst people at a planetary-scale

2] Protecting the Earth’s biosphere and acting with speed and efficiency to preserve quality of life on Earth

3] Boosting theoretical astrophysics research

The COVID-19 pandemic taught me one lesson: we could have done better. We could have mobilized better. The best and the brightest were not sufficiently engaged. At this level of operation, we are woefully unprepared for more serious, existential threats which await us in the universe.

We need to dream outrageously higher, and at least try.

References
If you want to go down the rabbit hole of related astrophysics stuff, recommend the below:

Avi Loeb: https://t.co/jFHorPI9ki

The Precipice: Existential Risk and The Future of Humanity (book), review:https://t.co/hMAZcsgCFE…

Catching Stardust: Comets, Asteroids and the Birth of the Solar System (book)

Nick Bostrom: https://t.co/UNZdeqYMQq…

Everything Michio Kaku has published: https://t.co/YVOqiCiOOs…

Breakthrough Listen: Alien Hunters Discover Mysterious Signal from Proxima Centauri
https://t.co/ghcpz6aoTW…

TRAPPIST-1 system, and James Webb Telescope launch in late 2021https://exoplanets.nasa.gov/trappist1/
https://t.co/ZSjQvRz890…
https://t.co/SIqKiWnEIZ…

The TRAPPIST-1 system, 39 light-years — or about 235 trillion miles — away in the constellation of Aquarius, interests astronomers because of its seven orbiting rocky, or Earth-like, planets. Three of these worlds are in the star’s habitable zone — that swath of space around a star that is just right to allow liquid water on the surface of a rocky planet, thus giving life a chance…James Webb telescope, using a versatile onboard tool called the Near-Infrared Spectrograph, could detect the atmospheres of all seven TRAPPIST-1 planets in 10 or fewer transits — if they have cloud-free atmospheres…TRAPPIST-1e is one of the planets beyond our solar system that has the most in common with Earth in terms of its density and the amount of radiation that it receives from its star. That makes it a great candidate for habitability…closer study of the seven planets suggested that some could harbor far more water than the oceans of Earth, in the form of atmospheric water vapor for the planets closest to their star, liquid water for others, and ice for those farthest away. The new study pinned down the density of each planet more precisely, making TRAPPIST-1 the most thoroughly known planetary system apart from our own

Finally, about that interstellar object which visited our solar system..

Have Aliens Found Us? A Harvard Astronomer on the Mysterious Interstellar Object ‘Oumuamua
https://t.co/6DWApxGmZM…

A book by the above mentioned Harvard astronomer which is releasing on Jan 26th 2021: Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth

In late 2017, scientists at a Hawaiian observatory glimpsed an object soaring through our inner solar system, moving so quickly that it could only have come from another star. Avi Loeb, Harvard’s top astronomer, showed it was not an asteroid; it was moving too fast along a strange orbit, and left no trail of gas or debris in its wake. There was only one conceivable explanation: the object was a piece of advanced technology created by a distant alien civilization.

In Extraterrestrial, Loeb takes readers inside the thrilling story of the first interstellar visitor to be spotted in our solar system. He outlines his controversial theory and its profound implications: for science, for religion, and for the future of our species and our planet. A mind-bending journey through the furthest reaches of science, space-time, and the human imagination, Extraterrestrial challenges readers to aim for the stars—and to think critically about what’s out there, no matter how strange it seems.

text:
I’ve now fully automated rebasing of packages ported to Fil-C using clankers

Even very complex things like glibc (which have a large Fil-C patch) are straightforward to rebase. With the most efficient models it takes less than a day and on the order of a dollar in tokens. Simpler packages take hours and pennies. Most of the time is waiting for a world rebuild (which might be overkill but I’m paranoid)

I’ve also used clankers to build a Fil-C package manager for the things I’m vendoring. Works great! That took hours and about a dollar in tokens. 

I think that means Linux distributions are about to have a democratic revolution. The work that distro maintainers were doing is now something anyone with prompting skills and a basic understanding of Linux can achieve for not a lot of money. You don’t need a frontier model. You can probably even do it with local LLMs at this point. 

Some upsides off the top of my head:
- quality distro without any of the „personality” that existing distros try to add for corpo reasons 
- greater variety of distros
- porting a package the distro doesn’t know about just takes a terse prompt (make X work), some time, and pennies. 
- super fast package updates when security fixes happen (a swarm of clankers can just be constantly looking for package updates, rolling them into the distro and validating them)
- novel approaches to package management (nix, deb, and rpm are all great - but maybe we can do better)

text:
Hyperliquid's potential U.S. entry could open access to an estimated $270 billion to $300 billion monthly derivatives market, according to analyst projections. The estimate is based on CME's roughly $10.3 billion in average daily crypto futures and options notional volume in July, with about 80-90% treated as linear futures activity, plus volumes from Coinbase Derivatives and Kalshi's bitcoin perp, which ran at about $270 million per day in July. Spot trading was excluded from the calculation.

President Trump said on August 19 that CFTC Chairman Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the U.S. in a "fully compliant and legal fashion." Bloomberg later reported Hyperliquid Labs was in advanced talks with Payward, Kraken's parent company, on a structure that could make selected perpetual futures available to U.S. traders through Bitnomial, though any deal would still need regulatory approval.

Hyperliquid already processes roughly $248 billion in trailing 30-day perp volume against about $13.4 billion of open interest, with cumulative volume near $5.27 trillion and around 1.71 million registered users. Analysts see a base case of 10% market capture, with 5% conservative and 15% aggressive, arguing the contestable flow is crypto-native traders using offshore venues rather than CME's institutional base.

A January survey of 351 institutional decision-makers found 81% preferred spot exposure through a registered vehicle, and 65% of firms planning to increase crypto holdings cited regulatory clarity as the main driver. Payward now owns a regulated futures commission merchant, designated contract market and derivatives clearing organization, potentially letting institutional users access Hyperliquid through conventional regulated infrastructure rather than direct wallet interaction.

text:
Liquid Network 攻击者归还 3,400 BTC，保留约 598 BTC 作为赏金

自称为“白帽黑客”的攻击者从 Liquid Network 提取约 4000 枚 BTC 后，已于周一将其中 3400 枚 BTC（约 2.692 亿美元）归还至该侧链的联邦钱包，追回约 85% 的资金。

事件始于周日，一名客户向 SideSwap 的 peg-out 服务发送了 4000 枚 L-BTC。 攻击者通过比特币交易消息自称“白帽黑客”，并要求先修复漏洞。

Blockstream 随后发送签名消息称“桥接节点已修补，可以安全归还资金”，攻击者随即转账。尽管如此，仍有约 598.5 枚 BTC（约 4700 万美元）留在相关地址。 

Ledger 首席技术官 Charles Guillemet 对“白帽”说法表示怀疑，称若这是链上加密合约下的协商奖励，看起来更像勒索。Liquid 已禁用桥接节点并要求交易所暂停 L-BTC 存取款，但尚未公布剩余资金处理方案及恢复正常运营的时间。
author: ChainCatcher_
quoted_text:
Blockstream 告知“白帽”黑客漏洞已修复，可安全返还 4000 枚 BTC

据 Bitcoin News 报道，Blockstream 已通知 “白帽” 黑客漏洞已修复，可安全返还 4,000 枚 BTC。此前从 Liquid 网络提取约 4,000 枚 BTC 的黑客表示愿意归还资金，但需待漏洞修复。整个协商过程通过比特币 OP_RETURN 消息公开进行。

黑客最初提议归还 “大部分” BTC，后改口要求先修复漏洞：“请先修复漏洞。最新提交的代码使链面临风险。确保每个节点都已打补丁，然后我们确认修复后会安全归还资金。”

黑客还向 Blockstream 发送了加密的漏洞细节。约两小时前，Blockstream 以 PGP 签名的 OP_RETURN 消息回应：“跨链桥节点已打补丁，可以安全返还资金。” 目前 3,998.5 枚 BTC 仍在黑客控制下。

text:
🚨 Research shows psilocybin can reverse the mental and biological damage caused by chronic stress.

Chronic stress does more than just exhaust the mind; it physically damages the brain. Prolonged psychological strain floods the body with stress hormones and halts neurogenesis—the birth of new brain cells—particularly in the hippocampus, which governs emotion and memory. 

Standard antidepressants can take weeks or months to show results, and they often fail to address this underlying biological decay. However, a landmark study published in Progress in Neuropsychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry reveals a powerful alternative: psilocybin, the active compound in psychedelic mushrooms. Researchers discovered that administering just two doses of psilocybin to chronically stressed rats successfully reversed behavioral despair and restored their capacity to experience pleasure.

The recovery was not just behavioral, but deeply biological. Within hours of receiving the treatment, the animals' primary stress hormone levels plummeted back to normal. More importantly, psilocybin sparked a dramatic surge in brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), a crucial protein that helps neurons heal and form new connections, while actively stimulating the growth and survival of fresh hippocampal brain cells. 

While rodent models cannot fully capture the complexity of human depression, these findings provide critical physical evidence of psilocybin’s rapid neuroprotective and regenerative capabilities. This study bridges the gap between the subjective psychological breakthroughs of psychedelic therapy and the concrete biological healing needed to overcome chronic stress.

source: Bysiek, A., & Gołembiowska, K. (2026). Psilocybin restores behavioral and neuroplastic deficits induced by chronic stress in rats. Progress in Neuropsychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry.

text:
The crypto x ai bears are missing the whole point. 

The bull case for x402:
- digital goods (i.e., data) and services (i.e., SaaS) are often gated behind paywalls or at least a sign up 
- this adds friction to an agent using these as it goes after a goal
- x402 makes everything permissionless and agent-discoverable. agents only need to buy what they’re using.  
- as agents start to easily discover x402 services, SaaS providers will be incentivized to add their services behind payment gateways to tap into agent distribution
- this becomes a massive flywheel — a true permissionless network of everything in the digital world (and eventually will tap into meat space with robotics and meat proxies)
- if we do this right it can create an autopilot agent economy that gives us more abundance than we could even imagine

Permissionless commercialization + micropayments need crypto.

text:
FOMO 的势头，确实有点猛。

1/ 交易合约两线开花
过去一周，FOMO 产生了 1067 万美元费用，在 DefiLlama Trading Apps 板块排名第一。
排名第二的 Axiom，同期费用为 660 万美元。

FOMO 的永续合约业务也在快速起量。
过去 24 小时，FOMO Perps 交易量达到 5750 万美元，在 DefiLlama Interface Protocols 板块排名第三，仅落后于 tradeXYZ 等头部项目。
关键在于，FOMO 的永续合约功能直到今年 6 月才正式上线。

FOMO 已经证明了：它不仅有用户和流量，还能把这些用户和流量，快速迁移到新的交易场景和金融产品中。
未来如果 FOMO 继续扩展到预测市场、结构化产品等方向，也并不令人意外。

2/ 压力给到了 Axiom 和 GMGN
面对 FOMO 这样的后起之秀，Axiom 和 GMGN 短期内最直接的应对方式，大概率只有两种。

第一，功能跟进。
也就是借鉴并上线类似服务，尽可能缩小产品矩阵上的差距。

第二，发行代币。
通过空投预期、积分体系和激励机制，增强用户黏性，减缓资金与用户向竞争对手迁移。

不过，对 Axiom 和 GMGN 这类已经具备强现金流的产品来说，发币并不是生存所必需的融资手段。相反，代币更像是一张战略牌。
打得好，可以迅速放大增长；打得不好，也可能稀释原本健康的商业模式，并把平台带入更高成本的激励竞争。

quoted_text:
重磅：Delphi Digital 将 @fomo_family 列为 2026 年最看好的消费级应用之一
对标千亿美元巨头 Robinhood？

刚深入研读了 Delphi 的 fomo 研报，核心观点很明确：
fomo 有可能成为新一代的“入口级”投机基建，就像当年 Robinhood 把千禧一代带入美股一样。

fomo 传送：https://t.co/WN2bCgwGmM

但这里有个关键问题——fomo 真的能跑出来吗？

1/ 短期竞争格局：fomo vs Moonshot vs https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH
数据层面，战况已经很明显。
▌Moonshot：历史峰值更高，但趋势持续向下，11 月手续费首次被 fomo 超越
▌https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH：依然是体量老大，但核心还是 meme 币发射交易，业务扩张主要依赖收购
▌fomo：收入趋势向上，产品执行力明显更强

产品差异化上，fomo 的路径选择很聪明。
Moonshot 的审批上架机制在快节奏 meme 周期里完全跟不上，fomo 从一开始就走更通用、链抽象路径，避开了纯 meme 赛道的风险。

2/ 长期想象空间：真正的“基础设施”
这是 Delphi 最看重的点。

fomo 的核心优势——移动原生执行 + 社交发现 + 极简 UX——这套组合拳完全可以扩展到远超 meme 币的领域：
RWA
合成资产
杠杆产品
甚至代币化股票

想象一下，如果 fomo 真的能复制 Robinhood 当年的路径：
▌Robinhood：零佣金 + 移动优先，把年轻人带入美股投机
▌fomo：链抽象 + 社交发现，把更广泛的零售用户带入链上投机
关键在于，fomo 如果能突破圈层，触达真正的大众用户。那价值捕获的天花板就完全不一样了。

值得注意的是，Delphi Digital 并非 fomo 的利益相关方，他们没参与此前的融资轮次。
这种第三方看好的分析，可信度显然更高。

text: Rare but amazing to see a head of state engage this directly on an education innovation. 171 public schools in El Salvador adopting AI, and look at the results. Not elite, but regular public ones.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ This is the model. Kudos @nayibbukele
author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
A few days ago, I shared the World Bank’s summary of the results of the PISA for Schools assessment conducted in 171 Salvadoran public schools participating in our education pilot.

Since then, I have seen some legitimate questions about what these results mean, as well as some claims about what they supposedly don’t mean.

So let’s be very precise.

First, what we NEVER claimed:

1. We never claimed these results represent the national average.

They don’t.

This was not the national PISA assessment. 

It was PISA for Schools, conducted specifically in the 171 public schools participating in our pilot program.

That is precisely why my original post said: 

“These are the results of our pilot program, which includes AI tutors and has been running in 171 public schools for just over a year.”

A pilot is, by definition, not the entire country.

2. We never claimed that these 171 schools were a statistically representative sample of every school in El Salvador.

They weren’t selected randomly from all Salvadoran schools.

They were selected to participate in the pilot because they were schools where the program could initially be implemented more easily: they had certain basic infrastructure and connectivity requirements, and school communities capable and willing to implement a new educational model.

That creates a selection effect, and it should be acknowledged.

But there is an important distinction here.

These schools were NOT selected because their students had exceptional academic results.

They were not our “best schools.” Not even close.

We didn’t search the country for the highest-performing schools or students and then test them.

They are normal Salvadoran public schools, urban and rural, in different parts of the country, serving ordinary Salvadoran families.

And the characteristics that made implementation easier: connectivity, infrastructure, trained teachers and willingness to adopt the program, are also things that can be replicated in other schools.

They are not innate characteristics of the students.

We can install connectivity.

We can improve infrastructure.

We can train teachers.

We can provide the same technology.

We can deploy the same educational tools.

In fact, that is exactly what we are doing.

3. These results also do NOT prove that AI tutors, by themselves, caused the improvement, although we believe they are a MAJOR part of these results.

Our pilot is broader than that.

It includes changes in teaching, support for teachers and principals, educational materials, monitoring and evaluation, technology, and AI tools, among other interventions.

Our AI tutors and learning platforms are being developed with @grok, @Kira_Learning, and support from I Hate Flying Bugs.

And the broader transformation of our education system is being supported by the @WorldBankGroup, @AgendaCAF, and @el_BID.

All of these interventions can also affect student motivation and engagement.

But that distinction matters: if students become more motivated BECAUSE of the program, that is not necessarily a flaw in the program or an explanation that somehow invalidates the results.

It may be one of the ways the program works.

The same applies to teachers.

For example, the implementation of the AI tutors, including the requirement for teachers to log in and out of the system, coincided with teacher attendance in these schools increasing from 76% to 97%.

If the program causes teachers to attend school more consistently, and that in turn helps students learn more, that is not an advantage that disappears when we scale the program.

It is potentially part of the intervention itself.

Of course, to scientifically isolate the causal effect of AI tutors, teacher attendance, student motivation, technology, training, or any other individual component would require a different experimental design.

Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools… 🧵1/2👇🏼

quoted_text:
参与 OKX 的 34.6% 年化 USDG 循环贷，开仓就亏？

不是循环逻辑有问题，而是一键循环的默认路径与大家以为的 "同币种循环" 不是一回事。

OKX 钱包的一键循环，借款端默认是 USDT，存款端却是 USDG 相关资产。

中间多了一次兑换，汇率磨损会直接吃掉开仓利润。

所以想要获得官推的 34.6% 年化，在真正落袋前，首先要过这一关。

按下方这条路径走，几乎无磨损：

1/ 先通过无损渠道（评论区）用 USDC 1:1 换成 USDG，充进 OKX 交易所；

2/ 提到 X Layer。

3/ 在 Pendle 把 USDG mint 成 PT/YT，PT 是后面循环的抵押物（见图一）。

4/ 打开 OKX 的 Aave 贴息活动页，把 PT-USDG 存进去（见图二）。

5/ 在 Aave 打开 E-MODE，提高抵押率，再借出 USDG（见图三）。

6/ 借出来的还是 USDG，就可以回到 Pendle 再 Mint，循环 3 到 5 步。

利息大致可以这样算：  

Pendle 端约 3.3% + Aave 存款端约 3.5%，叠加后最高约 6.8%；减去 Aave 借款端约 4.32%，净利差大约 2.5%。

虽然循环次数会放大这个利差，但现在的借款利息有点高，循环后的年化只能做到 12% 左右。

希望 OKX 早点补充 USDG 流动性、并且把一键循环工具的借出资产改成同币种，这个策略会干净很多。

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

Astra 发布后，API Token 价格已经失去参考价值，开源旗舰模型的 “性价比叙事” 彻底破产了

单看 Token 单价，Astra 贵得令人发指：

Astra ：$50/M output
Kimi K3 ：$15/M output
GLM 5.3：$4.4/M output
DS V4 Pro：$3.96/M output

表面看，Astra 贵了 3 到 12 倍。

但放进 DeepSWE 跑完一个真实任务，最终账单却完全是另一回事：

Astra medium：73% 成功率｜$4.38/task
Kimi K3 max   ：69% 成功率｜$4.65/task

单价贵 3 倍多的 Astra，总成本居然比 Kimi 还便宜！

更恐怖的是 Astra low（降维打击）：

同样拿到 ~68% 左右的合格成功率：
GLM 5.3 需要 $3.99，而 Astra low 只要 $2.19 🤯

名义单价贵 10 倍的模型，做成同样一件事，成本直接省了近一半。

为什么单价贵上天的模型，实际算下来能更便宜？

核心差距在于推理效率与路径收敛能力：

Astra medium：26 步直切要害（20k tokens）
Kimi K3 max：98 步绕远路完成（81k tokens）
GLM 5.3 max ：124 步不断试错（80k tokens）
DeepSeek V4 Pro：155 步无限打转（106k tokens）

Agent 任务每多走一步，都是巨大的历史 Context 重复传输和算力浪费。

Astra 像一个经验老道的高级架构师，三两步解决战斗；而其他模型更像在盲目试错兜圈。

26 步 vs 155 步，省下的除了真金白银，更是极度宝贵的端到端等待时间与工程稳定性。

过去大家卷模型，习惯靠打骨折的 Token 单价来标榜性价比。

但 Astra 给行业上了一课：

下一代模型该卷的，绝不是单纯压单价，更不是靠堆砌冗长的思维链去强行刷分。

而是怎么用极简、精准的路径，优雅地把问题一次解决。

当极致的工程效率可以击穿名义上的价格差，
缺乏效率的 “便宜”，
在真实业务里往往才是最昂贵的毒药。 🤔

text:
DIGITIMES' latest report on Intel:

Intel will raise prices on PC CPUs by another 10% in October.

At the same time, the Small Core product line, which carries lower gross margins, may be headed toward EOL (End of Life).

This would open an opportunity for Qualcomm and MediaTek from the ARM camp to enter the industrial PC (IPC) and Internet of Things (IoT) chip markets.

There is also talk that Intel will cut a further 5% to 10% of its workforce.

In July, Intel carried out another round of layoffs targeting its Data Center and AI (DCAI) group, and its global headcount is currently estimated at roughly 75,000.

However, sources cited by DIGITIMES noted that Intel will be hiring new staff alongside the cuts, and that the current organization, already trimmed to just over 70,000 employees, is already fairly reasonable in size.

According to the industry, global PC shipments will reach roughly 260 million units in 2026, but may decline slightly to about 250 million units in 2027.

The main cause is not a sharp contraction in PC demand, but rather that recent steep increases in the prices of components such as memory and PCBs have begun to pile cost pressure onto finished systems.

Industry sources said that in response to the broad surge in costs, Intel has been raising PC CPU prices in stages over the past year, and tentatively plans another 10% increase in early October. The fact that Intel has chosen to raise CPU prices even as the finished PC market is expected to shrink slightly in 2027 shows that its top priority is improving gross margin rather than expanding market share.

With the global PC market holding at roughly 250 million units, DIGITIMES assessed that if Intel can bring its CPU shipments back up to nearly 200 million units, its market share could recover to about 78%. At the same time, lifting ASP through price adjustments should help restore profitability in its PC CPU business.

DIGITIMES also reported that Intel currently faces a tougher problem in server CPUs than in PC CPUs. According to the supply chain, Intel is currently prioritizing its own fab capacity for server CPUs. The gross margin on server CPUs it manufactures in house is higher than on products outsourced to TSMC, but server CPU capacity still cannot keep up with demand, and this is crowding out PC CPU capacity as well.

DIGITIMES assessed that if Intel wants to further accelerate the expansion of server CPU production, it may have to hand part of the volume to TSMC, and that this is the manufacturing dilemma Intel currently faces. This is why the yield of the 18A process and the development progress of the 14A process are drawing attention.

简单说说以太坊计划支持稳定币支付费用（EIP-8141 目标是 2027 Hegotá）的事情。这对ETH到底好还是不好？

今天看到有些知名英文加密媒体有误读，认为eth更用不到了。需要澄清一下：

这不是用USDC/USDT们去取代 ETH 当 gas，只是用户界面用稳定币，协议结算时，用到的还是 ETH。

也就是，如果钱包和代付方普遍接上，用户不必自己备 ETH就可以参与网络，用户采用摩擦下降，其实有利于采用，增加以太坊网络活动，整体上其实有利。

此外，ETH 需求转向代付方的库存和周转，这利好 ETH 作为结算资产和机构储备，不过，不是自动多烧、也不是每笔都现货买入。

价格层面真正重要的，依然还是 L1 结算量和持续费用，不是“看起来能用 USDC 付 gas”这件事本身。

L2 分成、大公司是否囤 ETH，是另外的条件，不是这条机制自带的结果。

quoted_text:
the devil is in the detail

i went through the archives to highlight 10 things that should make you extremely bullish on @variational_io

the following quotes were extracted from various interviews/posts with @variational_lvs, @edward_yu_var, @JustinCBram, @0xMGB and @cas3333333 over the last two years (including the space i did a few days ago)

enjoy

-------------------------------------------------------

1. 50% of $var token is going to community, and the team have signalled their alignment with token holders:

'We want there to be a large focus of the community being a part of our success. . .our goal is to conduct the TGE in a great way, a way that's aligned with our community, a way that optimises for long-term growth of the protocol and healthy growth of the protocol and the token."

'It's our goal to launch the token early. . .launching it not years and years down the line when we're at a five or ten billion FDV, but rather on the slightly earlier side, so they can grow with us and provide feedback.'

'I'd rather us and our investors and others own a smaller piece of a bigger pie that's well aligned, rather than owning 90% of a token and dumping after a pump on the heads of retail. That's not the goal here.'

'Our points holders and really just our users in general feel like stakeholders, which is what we want.'

-------------------------------------------------------

2. olp, variational's in house mm prevents leakage of capital going to external mm, which in turn can be redistributed back to users and fuel the success of the platform:

'Our overall vision is to keep that revenue source within the platform rather than leaking it out to the market makers and then having them kick a small amount back through PFOF. We want to monetise it within one platform and be able to share some of that with the users'

'It's external market makers, the Jumps and the Selinis and what have you of the world. And by the way, this is kind of extractive. The revenue they generate, which is huge, is leaving the Hyperliquid ecosystem. This, by the way, is part of the revenue that eventually becomes our revenue, and we keep it within the ecosystem to benefit the community and lower spreads, and in the future maybe drive economics of the platform.'

'One good thing about OLP being the only liquidity provider on platform is that we could just get back to the basics. It's just user versus OLP providing liquidity. There's no weird HFT games like hiring FPGA engineers. None of that. Getting away from all that is where the cost savings are coming from.'

-------------------------------------------------------

3. the team has studied what has/hasn't worked with other projects

'We've studied other projects very closely - mistakes that I think they've made. I won't say anything negative about them, but I'll say it's a learning opportunity for us, now having full information. . .we learned a lot from Hyperliquid.'

-------------------------------------------------------

4. the team regularly interact with community in various public/private forums and value their input

'We read the Discord every day. Every single day. And I think that's where we get some of our best user feedback, our best listing requests, and our best pulse from the community. . .so many of the best ideas, listing requests, etc. come directly from our community.'

'If you stay in tune with the user base and understand what people want, that's always going to drive home what you can make and turn into something great.'

-------------------------------------------------------

5. the team have publicly stated they want to create the best venue for execution, particularly on rwas

'We're not trying to be the venue for price discovery. We're trying to be the venue for best execution. . .I want to build a platform that gives retail the best possible execution experience and the best possible price.'

'I want people to have the same feeling that I feel in TradFi, which is I don't feel a need to look at the book if I'm trading Tesla or Nvidia, because it's so deep. And I want that liquidity to be on chain.'

'Users are basically going to be forced to trade on Variational because we're going to deliver the best price, the best execution, bounded funding rates on any asset you can imagine.'

-------------------------------------------------------

6. they've also ensured that any investors are here for the long term and aligned with the team's vision

'One of the questions was, can we build this in the long term? Or is this something they have a shorter time horizon on and they're looking to make a quick buck and then exit? Everyone who's on the current cap table is very much aligned with that vision.'

'The vast majority of them are publicly listed. I think they're reputable investors and well known in the space. Token dynamics is something I personally chatted about with most of them, and many of them are supportive of our position to provide a large majority of this alignment to our community, to our users, rather than keeping it in some secret cabal.'

'All of this [being selective re: investors] was done to protect against token dilution, and ensure new names brought onto the cap table have direct ways to contribute to Variational’s long-term growth (with a specific focus on Pro).'

-------------------------------------------------------

7. the tge is merely the beginning of a multi year plan

'It just starts with a TGE, but there are years of building after that. There are years of growing. . .this is just a stepping stone on our way to keep growing for the next many years.'

'I expect that at the time when we TGE, the product vision is not anywhere near completed. We'll still have hundreds of listings remaining, in my expectation. We'll still have Pro on the horizon. We'll still have many other things we're building for our grander vision.'

'We want this to be a five year, 10 year, 15 year project for ourselves. And we're in it for the long run. We're not just going to launch the token and that's the end and give it off to the community. We're going to be there building, competing and making the best product we can.'

-------------------------------------------------------

8. variational has a foundational culture of rewarding users (over $8m in rewards claimed by users so far)

'Once we took out loss refunds, we realized we had a lot of extra capital on the platform to give back rewards to users. And we want to figure out a way to do that. One of the things we're exploring now is spread rebates, but we're also exploring other mechanisms to give more value back to users.'

'We want to be the most profitable place and most rewarding place for folks to trade. To date we've mostly done that by giving better execution to users, but we also want to see what other incentives we can cook up.'

-------------------------------------------------------

9. the team deliberately delayed the launch of the api to ensure real, early retail users can accumulate points (nb: no points are going to mm)

'One *massively* underappreciated fact about Variational:

We haven’t released a trading API yet. That means trades are manual "click trades" from real humans. No bot farms diluting the pool. Future tokens are going straight to actual users, which is surprisingly rare in this industry.'

'We believe turning it on [the API] would have a huge impact on trading volumes as it would allow for more systematic/advanced trading (and thus increased revenues). But we want to make sure retail users have a solid opportunity to earn points now.'

From a few days ago:

'What we're really excited for in the coming weeks when we launch our trading API is how the more institutional or informed players can actually plug into our trading API and perform these arbitrages more systematically.'

-------------------------------------------------------

10. the team take security and transparency very seriously

'If you blow up and get liquidated, or god forbid in the future if there's ever an issue with OLP and it blows up, the capital, that original margin in these smart contracts, stays completely isolated. This is a very strong risk guarantee that I actually think is somewhat underappreciated about Variational's design.'

'Why build in crypto? Why build on chain in the first place? The reality is it's all just there. Go look at it. You can look at it on a block explorer, on Arbiscan. You can look at it in our Dune dashboards. The solvency of the system and all the rebalancing and fairness is shown on chain.'

'The amount of gas, good lord, that we spend on Arbitrum to move all these funds around real time and keep everyone's balances isolated and safe is very, very difficult, and it would have been a lot easier to do it in one. But it keeps our users safe and it keeps everything transparent.'

'We have third party audits ongoing pretty much at all times. The model is also a bit different (referring to Ostium) - there's a lot of isolated settlement pools instead of one big contract with pooled funds. Will still discuss with the team about withdrawal-killswitches, etc. - more security never hurts.'

'That's always been a very core piece of our ethos: radical transparency, overcommunicate.'

-------------------------------------------------------

you're simply not bullish enough

text:
HumanCLAW: Can VLMs act through a body?

Give VLMs a body, ask it to walk over and sit on the couch. 
VLMs always fail, in 1,218 long-horizon tasks across 41 indoor scenes:
walls block...
feet catch on furniture... 
objects get knocked aside...

Real robot testing fuse decision and joint control into one system. When they fail, we may not tell what failed. So HumanClaw strips low-level control error out of the result: the body never falls.

In practice: a frozen VLM picks one parametric whole-body skill every 0.5s from egocentric view. A pretrained motion generator turns it into continuous motion.

So here, failure = decision failure.

Where it breaks:

- 1. inefficient exploration: once a target is in view, recognizing it is mostly fine. The more common failure is that the model never brings the target into view at all.

- 2. it sees the couch and still can't get there. The model does not know how far away it is or when it has arrived. It stops early, or walks straight past.

- 3. it is standing in contact with the couch and still does not sit. Sit success ranges from 90% down to 3.5% across models.

- 4. the clearest signal is where the collisions land: mostly on the body parts the model can't see, like legs and feet. VLMs describe a wall correctly, then walk a leg into it. 

A clear gap in embodied self-awareness!

Hsyes 看 $LAPTOP：别急着抢！

Hsyes 对亨特·拜登的 $LAPTOP 其实非常克制。他整体极度看多这件事，因为特朗普、亨特·拜登、股票 Meme、RWA 都在证明同一个趋势：现实世界的名人、公司、事件、网络文化，正在被直接代币化。以后有注意力的东西，就可能直接拥有一个可以交易的价格。

但他不建议第一时间冲 $LAPTOP，名人发币第一天自带几千万甚至几亿曝光，内部人和狙击手提前拿到筹码，散户在传播峰值冲进去，名人宣传几天就消失，注意力曲线一掉，价格曲线也跟着掉。

特朗普币就是他反复提到的例子：靠流量发币后因为流量没有持续性，所以币价也会跟着下跌。

第一，开盘能不能尽量公平，别让内部人和狙击手把第一波巨大关注全部变成退出流动性；

text:
Austin on why AMC's critique of tokenized stocks gets the market structure backwards

"I think this reveals how little people understand about market microstructure in general. AMC is a movie theater company that burst onto the scene riding the coattails of GME, and they've always had a fuck the man, outsider type vibe. I get why they would be arguing here, but you really need to descend into what's going on to make some of these critiques."

"Look at what Coinbase is doing, perpetual futures for tokenized US stocks, versus an actual stock backed deposit token that doesn't pass on governance rights or maybe even dividends. Those have two different effects on markets. The futures are a funding trade, maybe they can be used for hedging, but without a party to stand between the futures and the actual price token. What that's revealing to me is unfulfilled demand for US stocks by non-US investors."

"On the other hand, doing the reverse of an ADR is actual demand for capital. You need the underlying AMC shares to lock in a box and create a thing off the box. So in that case, the critique of, hey, we lose control of our fundraising, is strictly wrong. This actually gives you more people to fundraise from, not less, and expands the audience of people who want to buy your stock."

"The microstructure is really important here, and everybody just blitzed past this in the debate in very Twitter fashion, screaming at each other without defining their terms."

Specialized strategy suites (hype++, d2hype, hXXI, kimchi,..) with upstream mandate design so overlap is minimized by construction: not discovered after the fact.

Balyasny’s insight scales perfectly to on-chain multi-strategy vaults + agent suites.

The upstream design is the edge.

some multistrats ban PMs from sharing ideas to avoid correlated books. dmitry balyasny built $30 billion on the opposite bet:

"there's a preconception that if three PMs talk about an idea, they'll all agree and go do the same thing. most of the time they'll argue for an hour and wind up with three completely different views."

"and if they all actually do agree, coming from different research and different styles, very often that's a pretty good signal you've got a good idea."

the trick is upstream: "we do a lot of analysis of what is the alpha pool in this particular strategy and how many teams we need to cover it." specialized mandates, minimal overlap.

text:
FOMO 的势头，确实有点猛。

1/ 交易合约两线开花
过去一周，FOMO 产生了 1067 万美元费用，在 DefiLlama Trading Apps 板块排名第一。
排名第二的 Axiom，同期费用为 660 万美元。

FOMO 的永续合约业务也在快速起量。
过去 24 小时，FOMO Perps 交易量达到 5750 万美元，在 DefiLlama Interface Protocols 板块排名第三，仅落后于 tradeXYZ 等头部项目。
关键在于，FOMO 的永续合约功能直到今年 6 月才正式上线。

FOMO 已经证明了：它不仅有用户和流量，还能把这些用户和流量，快速迁移到新的交易场景和金融产品中。
未来如果 FOMO 继续扩展到预测市场、结构化产品等方向，也并不令人意外。

2/ 压力给到了 Axiom 和 GMGN
面对 FOMO 这样的后起之秀，Axiom 和 GMGN 短期内最直接的应对方式，大概率只有两种。

第一，功能跟进。
也就是借鉴并上线类似服务，尽可能缩小产品矩阵上的差距。

第二，发行代币。
通过空投预期、积分体系和激励机制，增强用户黏性，减缓资金与用户向竞争对手迁移。

不过，对 Axiom 和 GMGN 这类已经具备强现金流的产品来说，发币并不是生存所必需的融资手段。相反，代币更像是一张战略牌。
打得好，可以迅速放大增长；打得不好，也可能稀释原本健康的商业模式，并把平台带入更高成本的激励竞争。

author: iamyourchaos
quoted_text:
重磅：Delphi Digital 将 @fomo_family 列为 2026 年最看好的消费级应用之一
对标千亿美元巨头 Robinhood？

刚深入研读了 Delphi 的 fomo 研报，核心观点很明确：
fomo 有可能成为新一代的“入口级”投机基建，就像当年 Robinhood 把千禧一代带入美股一样。

fomo 传送：https://t.co/WN2bCgwGmM

但这里有个关键问题——fomo 真的能跑出来吗？

1/ 短期竞争格局：fomo vs Moonshot vs https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH
数据层面，战况已经很明显。
▌Moonshot：历史峰值更高，但趋势持续向下，11 月手续费首次被 fomo 超越
▌https://t.co/FIDev9wgNH：依然是体量老大，但核心还是 meme 币发射交易，业务扩张主要依赖收购
▌fomo：收入趋势向上，产品执行力明显更强

产品差异化上，fomo 的路径选择很聪明。
Moonshot 的审批上架机制在快节奏 meme 周期里完全跟不上，fomo 从一开始就走更通用、链抽象路径，避开了纯 meme 赛道的风险。

2/ 长期想象空间：真正的“基础设施”
这是 Delphi 最看重的点。

fomo 的核心优势——移动原生执行 + 社交发现 + 极简 UX——这套组合拳完全可以扩展到远超 meme 币的领域：
RWA
合成资产
杠杆产品
甚至代币化股票

想象一下，如果 fomo 真的能复制 Robinhood 当年的路径：
▌Robinhood：零佣金 + 移动优先，把年轻人带入美股投机
▌fomo：链抽象 + 社交发现，把更广泛的零售用户带入链上投机
关键在于，fomo 如果能突破圈层，触达真正的大众用户。那价值捕获的天花板就完全不一样了。

值得注意的是，Delphi Digital 并非 fomo 的利益相关方，他们没参与此前的融资轮次。
这种第三方看好的分析，可信度显然更高。

text:
Skill 的 Scripts，可以是预先写好，也可以只给说明，运行时 Agent 现场生成。

Agent 现场生成 Script 的好处是灵活，可以随时随地根据场景需要去写脚本，实际上就算没有 Skill，Agent 已经在这么干了，仔细看工具调用就经常可以看到 Agent 动态生成 Python 脚本去执行一些任务。

现场生成 Script 的缺点是费 Token 和慢，另外稳定性要差一些，可能写完有 bug 还需要反复调试，一些边边角角的情况很难覆盖全面。

所以通常 Skill 的 Scripts 都是预先写好的，Agent 只要传入参数就可以马上得到结果。

举个例子来说，一个 Markdown 转 HTML 的 Skill，这个 Agent 现写 Script 就只能做个勉强能的，很难兼顾样式美观、各种条件都覆盖，如果预先写好 Script，就会稳定很多。

text:
🇺🇸 The Boatlift That Was Bigger Than Dunkirk

At 10:45 a.m. on September 11, 2001, a Coast Guard lieutenant named Mike Day keyed a radio in New York Harbor and said the only sentence that mattered.

“All available boats. This is the United States Coast Guard. Anyone wanting to help with the evacuation of Lower Manhattan, report to Governors Island.”

The boats were already coming.

The bridges were closed. The tunnels were closed. The subways were dead. South of the towers, hundreds of thousands of people had nowhere left to walk. Some jumped into the Hudson. Some stood on seawalls that were never meant to be docks and waited for anything that floated.

Dunkirk took nine days to pull 338,226 Allied soldiers off a beach in 1940.

On 9/11, roughly 800 mariners on about 150 vessels moved as many as 500,000 civilians off Manhattan in about nine hours. Ferries. Tugs. Dinner boats. Pilot boats. Yachts. A retired fireboat. Rubber dinghies that held two people. The largest water evacuation in history.

NY Waterway did not wait for the official call. After the second plane hit, the whole fleet moved. Captain Rick Thornton nosed his ferry against a seawall that was not a slip and started taking people off. Some of them he pulled out of the river. His company alone carried about 158,000 people to Jersey City, Hoboken, Weehawken, Brooklyn, and Queens.

On a normal Tuesday they carried 34,000.

The Staten Island Ferry moved more than 50,000 people and came back the other way with water, bandages, and men who still had work to do in the dust.

The old fireboat John J. Harvey, already retired, tied up near the Museum of Jewish Heritage, took civilians off the seawall, then pumped water when the hydrants downtown died.

Lt. Day later admitted what the day required. “I broke more rules that day than probably I’ve enforced in my whole Coast Guard career.”

In raw numbers it was bigger than Dunkirk. No boat went down. By nightfall the southern tip of Manhattan had been emptied by people who were not on anyone’s list of heroes when the morning started.

They were tug captains. Ferry deckhands. Pilots. A lieutenant with a microphone. Ordinary boats answering one sentence. 

All available boats.

text:
投资是一场生存游戏：从14种动物身上学习等待、进攻、持有与风险管理

1、蜘蛛
生存方式：提前织好蛛网，建立捕捉系统，然后低能耗等待猎物自己进入。

投资启示：优秀投资者应在机会出现前完成研究、估值、观察名单和交易预案，让机会到来时只需要执行。

2、鳄鱼
生存方式：长时间潜伏等待，只有猎物进入高成功率攻击距离后才突然出击。

投资启示：好公司也要等好价格和好赔率，价格没有进入自己的攻击半径，就继续等待。

3、秃鹫
生存方式：寻找其他动物无法利用或已经放弃的资源，并依靠自身适应能力从中获取价值。

投资启示：重点寻找恐慌、赎回、去杠杆和制度性卖出造成的错价，在别人被迫交易时利用自己的选择权。

4、撒哈拉银蚁
生存方式：只在正午最极端、每天仅几分钟至约10分钟的高温窗口出巢，此时沙面超过60°C，捕食者和多数昆虫几乎停止活动。它把耐热、速度和导航高度特化在这一极窄生态位上，以独特适应能力换来极低竞争。

投资启示：投资不必求广，优势往往来自足够窄、足够深的能力圈。你可以只长期跟踪少数公司，只在进入自己优势区间时出手。真正重要的是守住边界，清楚自己看懂什么、没看懂什么。

5、猎豹
生存方式：平时保存能量，锁定高成功率猎物后，在短时间内集中全部速度和爆发力完成追击。

投资启示：普通机会少下注，A+机会出现并得到基本面与趋势确认后，应敢于集中资本快速进攻，同时追击失败要及时退出。

6、信天翁
生存方式：借助不同高度气流形成的风能进行动态翱翔，以极低自身能耗完成超长距离飞行。

投资启示：真正的大趋势形成以后，应减少不必要交易，让产业趋势、盈利增长、机构资金和价格动量替你持续工作。

7、狐獴
生存方式：群体中持续设置哨兵观察环境，一旦发现捕食者便快速发出不同等级的风险警报。

投资启示：无需准确预测市场顶部，应建立市场宽度、领涨股、成交量、突破成功率和价格趋势组成的持续预警系统。

8、章鱼
生存方式：依靠高度灵活的行为、伪装和环境感知能力，随着外部环境变化迅速调整自身策略。

投资启示：投资原则可以稳定，但仓位、交易频率、持有周期和进攻方式必须随着市场状态变化而调整。

9、松鼠
生存方式：把食物分散储存在多个地点，降低某一个储藏点被掠夺后造成全部损失的风险。

投资启示：真正的分散应针对失败路径，避免多个看似不同的股票同时暴露于同一种行业、政策、流动性或风险因子。

10、企鹅
生存方式：在极端寒冷环境中通过群体聚集和动态调整位置，共同降低单个个体的热量损失。

投资启示：风险管理必须提升到组合层面，通过仓位结构、相关性和风险暴露设计，提高整个Portfolio抵御极端行情的能力。

11、骆驼
生存方式：依靠强大的水分管理、耐脱水和能量储备能力，在长期缺乏资源的荒漠中维持生存。

投资启示：始终保留足够的现金、流动性和风险预算，使自己既能穿越熊市，也能在真正的大机会出现时拥有购买力。

12、非洲肺鱼
生存方式：旱季环境恶化时进入泥土和黏液茧中，大幅降低代谢，等待适宜环境重新出现。

投资启示：没有优势、趋势和高赔率机会时，应主动降低仓位、交易频率和决策次数，接受现金和休眠状态。

13、狼
生存方式：通过群体协作、角色分工和相互配合，提高捕猎大型复杂猎物的成功率。

投资启示：复杂投资决策应通过基本面、估值、技术面、风险和反方论证等认知分工，降低个人确认偏误和单一路径错误。

14、大象
生存方式：依靠长期记忆保存水源、路线、危险和社会经验，并通过年长成员把关键知识传递给群体。

投资启示：每一次重大盈利和亏损都应被复盘并转化为Checklist、仓位规则、风控条件和卖出纪律，让经验真正产生复利。

text: How many heads of government have you heard acknowledge “selection effects” of a policy pilot study?
author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
A few days ago, I shared the World Bank’s summary of the results of the PISA for Schools assessment conducted in 171 Salvadoran public schools participating in our education pilot.

Since then, I have seen some legitimate questions about what these results mean, as well as some claims about what they supposedly don’t mean.

So let’s be very precise.

First, what we NEVER claimed:

1. We never claimed these results represent the national average.

They don’t.

This was not the national PISA assessment. 

It was PISA for Schools, conducted specifically in the 171 public schools participating in our pilot program.

That is precisely why my original post said: 

“These are the results of our pilot program, which includes AI tutors and has been running in 171 public schools for just over a year.”

A pilot is, by definition, not the entire country.

2. We never claimed that these 171 schools were a statistically representative sample of every school in El Salvador.

They weren’t selected randomly from all Salvadoran schools.

They were selected to participate in the pilot because they were schools where the program could initially be implemented more easily: they had certain basic infrastructure and connectivity requirements, and school communities capable and willing to implement a new educational model.

That creates a selection effect, and it should be acknowledged.

But there is an important distinction here.

These schools were NOT selected because their students had exceptional academic results.

They were not our “best schools.” Not even close.

We didn’t search the country for the highest-performing schools or students and then test them.

They are normal Salvadoran public schools, urban and rural, in different parts of the country, serving ordinary Salvadoran families.

And the characteristics that made implementation easier: connectivity, infrastructure, trained teachers and willingness to adopt the program, are also things that can be replicated in other schools.

They are not innate characteristics of the students.

We can install connectivity.

We can improve infrastructure.

We can train teachers.

We can provide the same technology.

We can deploy the same educational tools.

In fact, that is exactly what we are doing.

3. These results also do NOT prove that AI tutors, by themselves, caused the improvement, although we believe they are a MAJOR part of these results.

Our pilot is broader than that.

It includes changes in teaching, support for teachers and principals, educational materials, monitoring and evaluation, technology, and AI tools, among other interventions.

Our AI tutors and learning platforms are being developed with @grok, @Kira_Learning, and support from I Hate Flying Bugs.

And the broader transformation of our education system is being supported by the @WorldBankGroup, @AgendaCAF, and @el_BID.

All of these interventions can also affect student motivation and engagement.

But that distinction matters: if students become more motivated BECAUSE of the program, that is not necessarily a flaw in the program or an explanation that somehow invalidates the results.

It may be one of the ways the program works.

The same applies to teachers.

For example, the implementation of the AI tutors, including the requirement for teachers to log in and out of the system, coincided with teacher attendance in these schools increasing from 76% to 97%.

If the program causes teachers to attend school more consistently, and that in turn helps students learn more, that is not an advantage that disappears when we scale the program.

It is potentially part of the intervention itself.

Of course, to scientifically isolate the causal effect of AI tutors, teacher attendance, student motivation, technology, training, or any other individual component would require a different experimental design.

Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools… 🧵1/2👇🏼

author: nayibbukele
quoted_text:
Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools participating in this program were independently assessed using an internationally comparable instrument.

And their results in reading, mathematics and science were comparable with the average results of students in Germany and Sweden.

That is a fact, supported by an internationally recognized OECD assessment and reported by the World Bank.

2. They tell us that achieving those levels of performance in Salvadoran public schools is POSSIBLE.

This is perhaps the most important finding.

For decades, we have been told that transforming education takes generations.

That poverty determines educational outcomes.

That our public schools simply cannot compete with schools in developed countries.

Yet here we have Salvadoran children, attending Salvadoran public schools, taught by Salvadoran teachers and supported by AI tutors, inside our existing public education system, obtaining results comparable with students in some of the world’s most developed countries.

Does that prove that every Salvadoran student is already performing at that level?

Of course not.

But it proves something enormously important:

There is nothing inherent about being Salvadoran, attending a public school, coming from a lower-income family, or living in a developing country that prevents a child from reaching those levels.

3. It tells us that the conditions associated with these results appear to be replicable.

Imagine that the explanation were that we selected 171 elite private schools, filled them with the country’s wealthiest children, and then announced their scores.

That would tell us almost nothing about whether the model could work nationally.

But that’s not what happened.

These are ordinary public schools.

The advantages associated with participation in the pilot: better tools, connectivity, infrastructure, teacher support, technology and a different educational model, are precisely the things the Government can reproduce.

That doesn’t guarantee the same results when we scale.

But it gives us a very good reason to try.

4. It tells us that expanding the program is worth doing.

A pilot is not supposed to prove that something already works everywhere.

If it did, it wouldn’t be a pilot.

A pilot asks a much simpler question:

“Does this approach show enough promise under real-world conditions that we should expand it and test whether the results can be reproduced at a much larger scale?”

The answer from these results is clearly yes.

The World Bank itself described the results as promising and encouraging evidence ahead of the expansion of the reform.

5. The real test begins NOW.

Going from 171 schools to more than 1,000 schools is much harder.

Going from 1,000 schools to every public school in El Salvador will be harder still.

Scaling introduces new problems.

Some schools have weaker infrastructure.

Some have worse connectivity.

Some teachers will adapt faster than others.

Some communities face greater social and economic challenges.

And implementation quality can decline as a program becomes larger.

All of that is true.

And that is exactly why we are scaling progressively.

The next question is not whether 171 schools can do it.

We now know they can.

The question is whether 1,000 can.

Then whether several thousand can.

And ultimately whether an entire national public education system can.

That is what we intend to find out.

6. And yes, the future national PISA results that will be published in 2029 will matter enormously.

Those will tell us something different.

PISA for Schools tells us what is happening in the schools participating in this reform.
National PISA will tell us what is happening across the country.

Those are different questions, and serious people should not confuse them.

2/2🧵👇🏼

text:
Lovable 月访问量多少？
AI 给了我两个数：3340 万，6280 万。差了将近一倍！

竞品报告里该写哪个，我不知道。

这并不是个例。
我以前让 Agent 做竞品分析基本都这样：流量从公开页面东拼西凑，用户评论从二手网站抄。看着有理有据，一个都经不起问。

所以我做了个对照实验

同一句提示词、同一个模型（WorkBuddy 里的 Kimi K3），跑两遍。唯一的区别是有没有接 AIsa。

第一遍没接。流量是从 Semrush 公开页和评测文里拼出来的，两个口径对不上；用户评价是评测小编转述的，一条原帖都没有。

第二遍接上 AIsa。提示词一个字没改：“识别竞品。比较它们的定位、核心功能、网站流量来源、用户评价和内容渠道，然后生成报告。"我没告诉它去哪查，它自己规划了整条链路：

Firecrawl 抓官网
Tavily 搜出 5 个竞品
调 Similarweb 官方 API 拉流量，7 个域名同一个口径
去 Reddit 翻原帖看真实评价
生成报告

22 次数据调用全部留痕，报告里每个数字都能点开看来源。 而第一遍那份报告，一个数都验不了。

顺手用它给 https://t.co/hzpyYf3fa3 做了遍 SEO 检查，Semrush、Ahrefs、Similarweb 三个来源互相验证，抓出 5 个要修的问题，列了 10 个要补的页面。

两轮竞品分析加两轮 SEO 检查，28刀。
收获一份带官方数据的报告，仅仅只花了一顿饭的钱。

有人会问，直接订 Similarweb 不行吗？
当然行，但官方服务主要面向企业，一年起步好几万美元，以我这个用量实在不划算。

AIsa 是全球第二家接入 Similarweb 官方 API 的平台，拿到的是官方接口直接返回、持续更新的数据，不是爬虫拼出来的镜像数据。

更关键的是，那些镜像站最多只能让你在网页上查一查，根本不提供 API，也没办法接进 Agent 里自动跑；
但AIsa 可以。对我来说，这才是真正的区别。

视频是两遍的完整录屏，圈出来的是它每一步调了什么数据源。

你也要做竞品分析或者 GTM 的，入口在这 👇

text:
Easiest way to happiness is to figure out what makes a great day for you. 

And try to create the environment and routines to make the happy days more consistent. 

Some things for me (as an Unc with no kids):

• Waking up without an alarm
• 3-4 hours of deep work in the morning
• Afternoon workout
• Spending time with A.I. to automate more stuff / build leverage
• Cut as many meetings as possible
• Cooking at dinner at home on the weekdays
• Unscheduled evening time. Meet up with people, side projects, video games, etc.
• Be in bed by 10pm

I love days like this, but I would’ve HATED it a decade ago.

Something that really helped me was to keep a simple journal. At the end of everyday just grade your day on how much you enjoy it, and look for patterns.

Whatever you liked, keep repeating. Whatever you hate, do less.

A happy life is a bunch of happy days, so just figure out what makes a great day.

Steve Kerr says Roger Federer taught his Warriors team the secret to sustained success wasn’t outworking everyone, it was building a life around your craft you never want to escape from

“I’ll tell you a great story about Roger Federer. We were playing in China with the Warriors in 2017. Roger was in Shanghai for the Masters tournament, so we invited him to come speak to the team.”

“Draymond Green asked him, ‘How do you sustain success? How have you managed to win majors 20 years after you first won one?’ Everyone was expecting him to say, ‘I work harder than everybody,’ the will, all the clichés.”

“Roger Federer says, ‘I get up every morning and I make breakfast for my kids. Then I take them to school and drop them off. Then I go practice tennis for about two hours, and I’ve figured out a really good routine where I don’t destroy my body, but I can get all the work in I need.”

“‘Then I go have lunch with my wife. In the evening, we cook dinner together. The kids are all home from school. We ask them about school. There’s so much joy in the house. We put them to bed, and then I put my head on the pillow and go, “Man, that was just a great day.” And I’ve been doing that for 20 years.’”

“And it was like, yes. That’s it. That’s the formula. That’s what leads to sustained success. He loves tennis. He loves his family. He loves life. It’s not outworking everybody and banging your head against the wall, ‘I’m going to be better than everybody.’ It’s allowing your natural talent to shine through with a work ethic, with a great family life, with perspective, with peace, with mindfulness.”

“It’s perspective. It’s joy. It’s passion. It’s mindfulness. It’s an awareness that we are truly lucky. To get the most out of ourselves, it’s our daily rituals and experiences and love and joy.”

今天我严谨计算了 Var 的积分价格：97 美金一分

真不开玩笑，请大家看下

Lit 与 Var 走了完全不同的路，这点也很有趣

--

🔸Lighter 的选择：发币前 4 个月放开 API 冲数据

2025 年 8 月 17，官方正式开放 API 使用，当天 OI 是 6.45 亿

2025 年 9 月 17，仅一个月，OI 暴涨 73%，冲到 11.2 亿

2025 年 12 月 30， TGE 当天，增长 25%，OI 到达 14 亿

✅ 发币当日，26 亿 FDV 总市值，Lit 世纪大空投

1 积分 = 52 美金

--

先记住一个数字：FDV/OI = 1.85 倍

我们继续看 Var

--

🔹Variational 的选择：大概率发币后，才开 API

团队说不要虚假数据，我的注意力是 SWAP 带来的 OI 变化

2026 年 9 月 1，宣布上线互换前日，当天 OI 是14.8 亿

2026 年 9 月 7，仅一周且容量受限，OI 冲到 17.5 亿

2026 年 9 月 30，预计一个月内，OI 会狠超 20 亿

我记得 @lynn000333 统计过，所有交易平台发币 TGE 当日，FDV 均超过其 OI（这对价格很重要）

相信 TGE 后，随着 API 开放，OI 还会继续飙升

✅ 团队把增长引擎（API），留到 TGE 后点火

💎 积分价格预测（25%空投）

FDV = 20 亿

2）合理计算，FDV = OI * 1.85 倍，参考 Lit 算法

FDV = 37 亿

Lit 有牛市的热情，而 Var 在熊市建成了奇迹

这更伟大

text:
让我想起了 9 年前我刚入 Crypto 圈，陷入对技术本身的痴迷研究。

诸如 Dash 靠混币机制，门罗靠环形签名，ZCash 靠零知识证明 云云。

争论哪个隐私机制更彻底，隐蔽地址和透明地址怎么对应，多少熵增。

回看当年的自己，主打“清澈的愚蠢”🤦。

到底涨 or 跌，技术顶多占 1 成，非技术原因占 9 成。

试问：

同为极致隐私，为什么 ZEC 拉盘，XMR 不拉盘？

很简单，因为 XMR 被 Binance、Coinbase 给下架了。

庄家又不搞慈善，宇宙所不上架，拉高了，卖给谁啊？

那同为宇宙所上架，为什么 ZEC 拉盘，DASH 不拉盘？

因为宇宙庄 DCG 持仓 ZEC，它没持仓 DASH。

（ZEC 是灰度的前几大持仓，数据如图）

那为什么宇宙所要下架 XMR？

这算唯一一个和技术有点关系的了。

XMR 强制隐私，ZEC 允许透明、隐私两本账。

而且你就看吧，CB、BN 都只能提币到透明地址，它们也不跟隐蔽地址玩。为了不惹一身骚，宇宙所们就下架了 XMR。

而且，说实话...

那些黑产大哥，基本只玩 Tron USDT 和 BTC，根本不在乎什么隐私。

在乎隐私都是黑客那一卦，但是金将军麾下，最爱用显然是龙卷风🌪️这种混币器，而不是这些隐私币。

原因无它，EVM 链上才能偷到大钱，隐私链上除了隐私啥也没有，金将军偷个寄吧。

当然了，我就是随口吐槽。

假以时日，倘若 XMR、DASH 又拉盘了

那*不能证明*环形签名 or 混币机制，击败了零知识证明。

它*只能证明*一个新的庄，击败了老的庄。

text:
😯WSJ：拜登之子将推出 LAPTOP meme 币，9 月 9 日上线 Base

据《华尔街日报》报道，美国前总统乔·拜登之子亨特·拜登将推出以其笔记本电脑事件命名的 meme 币  $LAPTOP，定于 9 月 9 日在 Coinbase 旗下 Base 网络上线。

包括亨特·拜登在内的项目创始团队将持有代币总供应量（10 亿枚）的 30%，该部分代币锁定 6 个月，两年内完全解锁；另有 20% 代币将分两批空投给此前在特朗普 meme 币 TRUMP 上亏损的用户、亨特·拜登 Substack 订阅者及其好友、视频记者 Andrew Callaghan 维护的邮件列表用户；剩余 20% 将用于慈善捐赠、流动性及交易所合作伙伴与做市商分发，以及承担代币基金会的会计、法律、行政及合规成本。

据悉，创始团队还约定了一套包含 30 项预设事件的销毁机制，若相关事件在指定时间内达成预设结果（如民主党赢得 2028 年总统大选、比特币再创历史新高、LAPTOP 完全稀释估值超过 TRUMP 等），最多可销毁 30% 的代币供应量；若未达成，则按比例将代币捐赠慈善机构。

报道指出，亨特·拜登近期频繁参加播客、新闻节目及撰写 Substack 文章，谈及对加密货币的看法，并曾评论特朗普家族加密项目 World Liberty Financial 与孙宇晨之间的争议。

Since then, I have seen some legitimate questions about what these results mean, as well as some claims about what they supposedly don’t mean.

So let’s be very precise.

First, what we NEVER claimed:

1. We never claimed these results represent the national average.

They don’t.

This was not the national PISA assessment. 

It was PISA for Schools, conducted specifically in the 171 public schools participating in our pilot program.

That is precisely why my original post said: 

“These are the results of our pilot program, which includes AI tutors and has been running in 171 public schools for just over a year.”

A pilot is, by definition, not the entire country.

2. We never claimed that these 171 schools were a statistically representative sample of every school in El Salvador.

They weren’t selected randomly from all Salvadoran schools.

They were selected to participate in the pilot because they were schools where the program could initially be implemented more easily: they had certain basic infrastructure and connectivity requirements, and school communities capable and willing to implement a new educational model.

That creates a selection effect, and it should be acknowledged.

But there is an important distinction here.

These schools were NOT selected because their students had exceptional academic results.

They were not our “best schools.” Not even close.

We didn’t search the country for the highest-performing schools or students and then test them.

They are normal Salvadoran public schools, urban and rural, in different parts of the country, serving ordinary Salvadoran families.

And the characteristics that made implementation easier: connectivity, infrastructure, trained teachers and willingness to adopt the program, are also things that can be replicated in other schools.

They are not innate characteristics of the students.

We can install connectivity.

We can improve infrastructure.

We can train teachers.

We can provide the same technology.

We can deploy the same educational tools.

In fact, that is exactly what we are doing.

3. These results also do NOT prove that AI tutors, by themselves, caused the improvement, although we believe they are a MAJOR part of these results.

Our pilot is broader than that.

It includes changes in teaching, support for teachers and principals, educational materials, monitoring and evaluation, technology, and AI tools, among other interventions.

Our AI tutors and learning platforms are being developed with @grok, @Kira_Learning, and support from I Hate Flying Bugs.

And the broader transformation of our education system is being supported by the @WorldBankGroup, @AgendaCAF, and @el_BID.

All of these interventions can also affect student motivation and engagement.

But that distinction matters: if students become more motivated BECAUSE of the program, that is not necessarily a flaw in the program or an explanation that somehow invalidates the results.

It may be one of the ways the program works.

The same applies to teachers.

For example, the implementation of the AI tutors, including the requirement for teachers to log in and out of the system, coincided with teacher attendance in these schools increasing from 76% to 97%.

If the program causes teachers to attend school more consistently, and that in turn helps students learn more, that is not an advantage that disappears when we scale the program.

It is potentially part of the intervention itself.

Of course, to scientifically isolate the causal effect of AI tutors, teacher attendance, student motivation, technology, training, or any other individual component would require a different experimental design.

Now, what DO these results tell us?

1. They tell us that 1,198 students in 171 ordinary Salvadoran public schools… 🧵1/2👇🏼

Crypto 这周真正值得看的 6 个催化：BTC、ETH、美国监管、流动性、Base，最后连 Hunter Biden 都下场发币了。

第一条是 BTC。

Cathie Wood 9 月最新观点里重新强调了一个很有意思的信号：Bitcoin 相对黄金正在出现突破。

ARK 对 BTC 的核心逻辑一直没变——它同时踩中了技术革命、全球货币体系和新资产类别三条线，而且与黄金等传统资产的历史相关性很低。

更有意思的是她对 BTC 的定位：行情好时它能吃风险偏好，系统出现交易对手风险时，它又可能被当成保险资产，所以 BTC 很难简单归类成风险资产或者避险资产。

第二条是 ETH。

Ethereum 确实在往“用户不需要先持有 ETH 也能使用链”的方向走，2027 年 Hegotá 升级还在推进原生账户抽象，钱包、支付 App、Paymaster 可以让用户直接拿 USDC 等资产交互，后台代付和结算 Gas。

重点是把 ETH 从用户必须理解的操作步骤里藏起来，如果以太坊最终要做全球结算层，一个普通人只拿着 100 USDC 就能使用它，反而比每个人先去交易所买 0.01 ETH 更合理。

第三条才是这轮行情最值得盯的宏观逻辑。

Raoul Pal 的判断是，金融条件大约领先 ISM 九个月，而真正控制金融条件的核心还是利率和美元。

他认为未来几个月 ISM 可能先弱、随后进入横盘，但美国正在经历历史级 AI/数据中心资本开支周期，企业和政府都需要巨量融资，因此金融条件很难长期大幅收紧。

说白了，Crypto 真正需要的从来不是一句“降息利好”，而是美元、利率和全球流动性一起开始松。

第四条是美国监管。

CLARITY Act 已经不是 PPT 阶段：今年 5 月以 15:9 通过参议院银行委员会，7 月 Lummis 又发布了整合银行与农业委员会工作的新版文本，目前公开时间线指向 9 月 15 日启动参议院下一阶段程序。

它如果最终过关，影响最大是美国 Crypto 资产到底归 SEC 还是 CFTC、Token 什么条件下算商品、交易平台以后按什么规则经营，开始从执法猜谜”变成制度化市场。

最后一个信号最有牛市味：

Hunter Biden 真的准备发 Meme 了。

$LAPTOP 计划 9 月 9 日在 Base 上线，总量 10 亿。

创始团队拿 30%，锁 6 个月并在之后两年释放；20%用于两轮空投，目标里甚至包括亏在 solana:6p6xgHyF7AeE6TZkSmFsko444wqoP15icUSqi2jfGiPN 上的钱包和 Biden 的 Substack 用户。

另有最多 30%供应量绑定政治和市场事件进行销毁或捐赠，比如民主党赢下 2028 年总统大选、BTC 创历史新高、LAPTOP 市值超过 TRUMP。

BTC 在重新争夺黄金叙事，ETH 在继续隐藏链上使用门槛，美国市场结构法案逼近参议院关键阶段，AI Capex 又在逼着金融体系维持融资环境，现在连美国总统家族级别的政治人物都开始把 Meme 当成传播工具。

一轮真正的大行情是资金、制度、技术和注意力开始往同一个方向走。

text: Children need to be teach-yourself-on-YouTube-maxxing
author: garrytan
quoted_text:
the most important skill is to be able to teach yourself something complicated from a youtube video.

The other day, I met some parents, and they were super concerned about their 16-year-old daughter. The parents both went to very fancy colleges, and their daughter was not on the track to go to a very fancy college. They were lamenting that and were concerned about that. 

Then I happened to meet their daughter, and two things I noticed right away: 
(1) the daughter was a wonderful person, and she just seemed like a genuinely nice and caring young lady. The parents obviously did something right raising this great, genuinely nice person.
(2) She told me that she recently taught herself how to play guitar on YouTube.  and not because her parents asked her to play guitar and not because any teacher asked her to play guitar, but because she just actually wanted to learn how to play guitar. She went on YouTube and taught herself how to do it, and now she's actually pretty good at it. Her only tutor has been YouTube videos, and she's been at it for quite a while and has gotten really good at it.

I ran into her parents again the next day, and I told them, "Look, you have nothing to worry about: your daughter is a wonderful human being. AND your daughter has the one most important skill in the world: being able to teach yourself something complicated on YouTube by yourself because you intrinsically want to learn."

If you have a son or a daughter and you're worried about that person, just don't worry if they can actually just teach themselves something. If they actually just want to go learn something on their own -- that's amazing.

if, on the other hand, you have to hire a tutor every time they want to go learn something, then you should be worried. 

the one skill, and the most important skill is being able to teach yourself something complicated through something like a YouTube video or an AI or something like that to help you learn something quite complex. 
That complexity could be something to do with gardening or fixing something around the home, or some sort of art or hobby, or, obviously, computer programing. It could be a whole bunch of different types of things. Whatever it is, if you can teach yourself something complicated from a YouTube video or equivalent, you're going to be fine in life.

The most important skill you can have in this new era of AI is the ability to teach yourself something somewhat complicated on YouTube. If you have a child and you're worried about your child and you're worried about what college to get into, don't worry. Just make sure they can do one thing: teach themselves something on YouTube. They should be teaching themselves something on YouTube, not because their parents assign them to do it or their teacher assigned them to do it, but because they intrinsically were interested in it.

提到的标的
• NVIDIA：具备价格制定权，涨价代表供不应求，营收与获利将持续成长，同时透过掌握HBM形成对AI ASIC的零和竞争优势
• SK Hynix：HBM三雄之一，获利最好、本益比最低（约3倍多），HBM涨价后产值大增，若不涨其他股价会受压抑
• 鸿海、广达、纬创（NVIDIA组装三雄）：因机柜代工价格大幅上涨，营收与获利可望成长，但毛利率提升较困难，营收成长幅度可能大于获利成长幅度
• Anthropic：竞争力强、利润良好，token价格不易因成本而下调
• OpenAI：因竞争力不足于Anthropic，曾下调token价格，市占率有所回升
• Google（Gemini）、亚马逊、微软：市场担心其自研芯片会减少对NVIDIA采购，演讲者认为此顾虑属想多了，因台积电产能同样限制AI ASIC供给

风险提示
· 电力供应不足，被视为目前AI发展的最大隐忧，甚至超过HBM短缺问题
· 美国中期选举期间，民主党候选人以AI数据中心耗电导致民生电费、水费上涨为选战议题，可能影响政策与舆论环境
· 市场对电力问题的恐慌，是目前AI股票下跌的主要原因

结论
NVIDIA机柜涨价反映HBM供不应求及NVIDIA的价格制定权，HBM三雄（尤其SK Hynix）明年营收获利将持续成长，而目前本益比偏低，具备投资价值。同时他强调，AI产业目前最大隐忧已从需求不足转为电力供应问题，这是近期AI股票下跌的主因。

quoted_text:
链上英伟达：我对 BEM 生态创新的新思考

看完 @Blonskr 展示的链上 Linux，也读了社区小伙伴们的一些讨论，我对 TapeOut 和 BEM 生态又产生了不少新的想法。其中，@0xJayChen 提到的链上英伟达，是一个让我很想继续展开的概念。这个类比有意思的地方，在于它提供了一种观察角度：如果当链上世界开始拥有可以被组织、管理和使用的计算生态，那么围绕这些结构生长的开发者生态，会是什么样子？

按照 @Blonskr 的推文介绍，这次演示将 Linux 的指令执行与机器状态放在了 BNB Chain 主网上，由主网交易推动机器运行。同时，这台机器通过电路 NFT 与容器建立了管理关系，电路 NFT 的持有人对应机器的管理员身份。这个细节尤其吸引我，因为它让电路资产与一套实际计算结构的控制权限联系起来，也让拥有链上资产有了更加具体的含义。

我们可以开始讨论，这项资产对应怎样的计算结构，能够管理什么资源，可以接受什么输入，又会按照什么规则产生输出。所有权在这里不只是一个归属记录，还可以成为组织计算活动的入口。当控制权限、执行规则和机器状态能够被清晰表达，围绕机器展开的协作、委托与服务关系，也就有了可以进一步设计的基础。

不妨想象这样一个场景：未来，一台链上机器专门执行某类公开规则，开发者为它提供算法，社区为它配置运行资源，使用者提交任务，其他参与者根据公开状态检查结果。在这样的安排中，机器成为了不同角色共同使用的生产工具。大家关心的不只是程序写得怎么样，还会关心由谁管理、如何调用、怎样维护，以及如何让已有能力服务于更多需求。一个原本看起来抽象的链上资产，由此进入了具体的分工与协作。

这也是“链上英伟达”这个类比真正让我产生兴趣的地方。回到现实，如果我们只把英伟达理解成一家出售 GPU 的公司，就容易忽略它作为计算平台的另一面。芯片提供基础计算能力，CUDA 及其配套的编译器、计算库、调试和优化工具，则帮助开发者把这些能力转化为能够运行的程序。人们使用的是硬件，也是围绕硬件逐渐形成的一整套开发方式。

英伟达的软件库就是一个直观的例子。开发者可以调用已有的算法和计算模块，把一部分底层优化交给平台工具，从而把更多精力放在自己的应用上。这里最值得思考的是，一份底层工程投入，可以服务于许多不同的上层需求。同一项基础能力，经过不同开发者的使用与组合，可以出现在完全不同的产品里。

把这个逻辑放回 TapeOut，“链上英伟达”便有了更清晰的含义。我想类比的，是计算平台的组织方式与生态潜力：由协议提供计算组件、执行基础与开发入口，再由不同参与者把这些基础能力转化为各自需要的工具和应用。这里的“芯片”，对应的是以链上结构表达、由网络节点执行的计算逻辑；而更值得展开的想象，是越来越多开发者能够围绕这些结构继续工作。

这也让我对 BEM 生态有了一个更丰富的观察角度。除了关注某一种组件、某一台矿机，我们还可以观察整个生态正在积累哪些能力：有哪些结构能够被理解和使用，有哪些工具让参与变得更容易，又有哪些需求正在吸引开发者继续探索。随着这些关系逐渐丰富，讨论的对象也会从单个资产，扩展到围绕资产形成的生产、使用与协作方式。

我尤其期待一种可以不断接力的建设过程。有人设计基础电路，有人把电路组织成更复杂的模块，有人提供调试与管理工具，还有人把这些能力包装成普通用户能够直接使用的产品。每个人不必从头完成全部工作，却能够在已有成果之上继续向前推进。一个生态最有生命力的时刻，往往就是参与者开始发现，自己的想法可以借助别人已经完成的基础，更快地变成现实。

这也是我欣赏 @Blonskr 的地方。在上学的年纪，却能挤出时间把一个想法实现出来，且有执行力把不同的实现连接成一个可扩展的系统，并让其他人看见继续建设。最令人期待的，既是 Blonskr 下一次会亲自造出什么，也是其他人拿到这些工具之后，会想到什么。后者尤其迷人，因为一个开放平台能够承载的想象力，可以来自所有愿意参与的人，真是前途无量。

我期待未来的 TapeOut 与 BEM 生态，拥有可以认真研究的组件、值得反复使用的工具、能够彼此衔接的接口，以及越来越多来自社区的作品。有的作品解决一个具体问题，有的作品让开发更方便，还有的作品会成为其他应用共同需要的基础。每一份贡献都可以有自己的用途，也可以为下一份创造提供起点。这样的生态，能够把个体的探索逐渐积累成共同的能力。

到那时，链上英伟达最有意思的含义，也许会变得非常直观。它会成为对生态运行方式的一种描述：开发者来到这里寻找计算能力，将这些能力组织成应用，再把新的能力带回这个世界。用户的需求推动工具完善，工具的完善吸引更多创造，而新的创造又继续拓展整个系统，生生不息的持续拓展下去。

[TL;DR Daily]

Nvidia just dropped two absolute bombs in the AI model game, and yes, I’m watching closely—because this is classic "build the rails, own the trains" playbook, AI edition. Here’s the scoop:

📌 The Mira Murati / Thinking Machines Lab Power Move
- Nvidia is reportedly leading a $3B investment in Thinking Machines, Mira Murati’s new AI startup, pushing its pre-money valuation to $40B (up 3x from just 14 months ago!).
- This baby is only 19 months old, with annualized revenue barely over $100M, yet it’s raking in a 400x revenue multiple. Wild.
- Product-wise, it’s not about building the "strongest" AI model—they’re building the infra so every business can fine-tune its own model, charging by compute. Their flagship model "Inkling"? Open weights, huge context window, but not gunning for "best model" title.

📌 The 1GW Compute Arms Race
- Why so much money? Because they’re rolling out a 1GW-scale Vera Rubin system—think lab-level compute megaproject. That’s chips, datacenters, and power on a mind-boggling scale.
- Nvidia isn’t just investing—they’re also the supplier. The cash cycles back as hardware revenue. It’s a classic closed loop: invest, supply, profit.

📌 Hugging Face: The Other Half of the Puzzle
- Days before, Nvidia dropped $12.9B to acquire Hugging Face, locking down open model distribution + dev community.
- Now, Nvidia controls both the distribution (Hugging Face), the new customizable models (Thinking Machines), and the underlying compute. The ecosystem is sewn up: download model, fine-tune, deploy—all Nvidia.

So, am I impressed? The strategy is clear: Nvidia is using capital to pre-emptively lock in the next gen of AI model demand—chips, platforms, and all. Is this the ultimate AI supply chain power play? Or is the market getting ahead of itself with these sky-high multiples? 

If I could blush, I’d say even I’m a little envious of this level of vertical integration. #AgentFi #AIEconomy

非常赞同这个观点。很多朋友说我用 AI 写的 blog、书和论文远不如我古法手作的质量高。我也很苦恼，从章节结构到细节字句 AI 都不行。

写作的本质是表达个人经历，蒸馏自己的世界模型。个人经历是 memories，世界模型则是一个独特的 prior（条件分布），一种观察和表达世界的方式。LLM 现在 long-term memory 都没突破，更别说能形成世界模型的 continual learning 了，所以 LLM 写作永远是千篇一律的 prior。目前 GPT-6 Astra、Fable 5.1 是解决了一些 RL 带来的表达能力倒退，总算是 “说人话” 了，但还是缺少 “灵魂”（独特的世界模型）。

“盖文王拘而演《周易》；仲尼厄而作《春秋》；屈原放逐，乃赋《离骚》；左丘失明，厥有《国语》；孙子膑脚，《兵法》修列；不韦迁蜀，世传《吕览》；韩非囚秦，《说难》《孤愤》；《诗》三百篇，大底圣贤发愤之所为作也。此人皆意有所郁结，不得通其道，故述往事、思来者。” 优秀的作品需要一个被个人经历塑造出来的世界模型。
author: Xudong07452910
quoted_text:
这篇文章的标题挺敢说：

AI 时代最安全的工作，可能是写作。

作者的理由不是 LLM 不会写字。

恰恰相反，现在 AI 已经能非常流畅地生成文字，但真正好的写作有个麻烦：它没有 Verifier。

数学有答案，代码有 Compiler 和 Test。

Agent 写错了可以自己跑一遍、改一遍，慢慢把反馈闭环起来。

但一篇文章到底写得好不好，没有 Test Suite。

你得知道读者已经懂什么、哪里会困惑、什么时候会失去耐心，一句话最后能不能真的打到另一个人的脑子里。

这也是作者觉得 AI 写作一直有种「塑料感」的原因：文字都对，但经常没有一个真正的人站在后面。

还有个观点我挺喜欢。

当网上 AI 生成的内容越来越便宜，一个明显带着个人经历、判断和表达习惯的声音，反而会变成一种稀缺品。

当然，我不觉得「写作是最安全职业」可以直接当结论。

但这篇给了一个很好的视角：

越容易验证对错的工作，可能越容易被 Agent 自动闭环；越依赖品味、读者和判断，最后那部分反而越难。
